docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Power and systems panels appearing at the top right mean the cockpit has no instruments.power / instruments.systems rectangles; add them to place the instruments.
  • In a 3D cockpit, instruments that drift off their bezels on a narrow window point to a Design that does not match the proportions the bezels were measured at; the field of view widens to fit the design's width (app::flight::cockpit_fov), see Cockpits.
  • Press F12 in the cockpit view to move instruments with the mouse (layout editor, see Cockpits); S saves the result as an addon you can inspect.
  • An anchored instrument that looks mirrored or upside down has its normal pointing into the surface; the editor's ray pick always turns the normal towards the eye.
  • If instruments sit in the wrong place on a cockpit, adjust the instruments rectangles in the cockpit's rules section — no code change needed; positions are in the cockpit's design space (640×480 unless Design says otherwise), not in the image's pixels.
  • The original cockpits' cyan colour key becomes transparent black on load; a cyan halo means the key was not applied (load_image(.., colour_key = true)).

docs.title: Input and gamepads
docs.text: src/input/ turns device state into simulation Controls and one-shot Commands, using bindings from an editable YAML file (bindings.yaml). The device reading itself is in src/app/devices.rs (keyboard, mouse) and src/platform/ (gamepads). The in-game controls menu is modelled in src/input/editor.rs and drawn by src/app/controls.rs. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added the power, equipment and wingman actions, gamepad chords and the controls menu. The default layout is on Controls.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    KB["macroquad keys<br/>KeyCode → name"] --> RAW["RawInput<br/>held, pressed, shift,<br/>mouse_offset, buttons, pad, pad_previous"]
    MS["mouse"] --> RAW
    GP["platform::Gamepads::poll<br/>→ PadState"] --> RAW
    RAW --> T["Bindings::translate(&raw, mouse_flight)"]
    T --> C["Controls (sim)"]
    T --> CMD["Vec<Command> (app)"]
    T --> CH["ChaseInput (camera)"]
    TAB["ACTIONS table<br/>name, action, keys, pad, group, label"] --> B["Bindings::from_yaml<br/>(defaults + bindings.yaml)"]
    B --> T
    ED["editor::Editor<br/>(controls menu)"] -- "edits a copy;<br/>saved on leaving" --> B

  • One table. ACTIONS lists every action once: its bindings.yaml name, the Action, its default keys, its default pad chords, its menu Group and its label. Parsing, defaults, to_yaml_text, the controls menu and the Controls tables all come from it, so they cannot drift apart. Entries are built with a const fn a(…) so the whole table is a compile-time constant.

  • Key names are macroquad's KeyCode variant names, lower-cased (KeyCode::Kp7 → kp7), produced by app::devices::key_name. Every key macroquad knows is therefore bindable.

  • Held vs pressed: axes, fire beams and afterburner are held; throttle steps, missile, link mode, targeting, views, power and equipment switches fire once per press. A Shift+X chord fires only with Shift held; a plain X only without it, so both can be bound to different actions. While Shift is held, a key used in any Shift chord is ignored by held actions bound to the plain key (shifted_keys): Shift+E (wingmen evasive) does not also roll the ship on E.
  • Gamepad chords. A PadChord is a button with an optional modifier button (LeftShoulder+A). Any button used as a modifier somewhere (modifiers()) does nothing on its own, and a plain binding does not fire while another modifier is held — holding the modifier switches the pad to its second layer. The defaults use the left shoulder as the only modifier.
  • Gamepad presses are detected by comparing with last frame's PadState.
  • Sticks add to the keys and are clamped; a dead zone is applied and rescaled (input::dead). StickLayout::Space (default): left stick yaw and pitch, right stick roll and vertical slide; StickLayout::Aircraft swaps yaw and roll (the original's Alt+J). Stick forward = nose down unless invert_pitch.
  • Mouse flight (toggle C): cursor offset from the centre / mouse range gives yaw and pitch, cursor down = nose down (as the original readme states) unless mouse_invert; left button = beams, right button = missile.
  • Bindings file: bindings.yaml in the user data folder (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/ or ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/). Created with the defaults on first run (app::load_bindings); keys not mentioned keep their defaults; the controls menu rewrites it in full when it saves. A bindings.ini of an earlier build is read once with the legacy reader (Bindings::from_ini) and saved as bindings.yaml.
keyboard:
  fire_beams: [Enter, LeftControl]
  wing_fire_at_will: [Shift+F]
gamepad:
  fire_beams: [RightTrigger]
  hyperspace: [LeftShoulder+A]
options:
  dead_zone: 0.15
  invert_pitch: false
  stick_layout: space
  mouse_range: 200
  mouse_invert: false

docs.title: The controls menu
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    DEV["devices.read()<br/>RawInput"] --> CM["app::controls::ControlsMenu::frame"]
    CM -- "keys, d-pad, A/B/X/Y" --> ED["editor::Editor<br/>rows, selection, capture"]
    ED --> PAINT["paint rows, cells, message"]
    CM -- "on leaving" --> AP["ctx.bindings = editor.bindings<br/>write bindings.yaml"]

Editor holds a working copy of the Bindings and the list of Rows: a Header per Group, an Action row per action, then a Setting row per device option (dead zone, invert pitch, stick layout, mouse range, mouse invert). Each action row has four cells (COLUMNS): two key slots and two pad slots. activate starts a Capture:

  • Capture::Key — capture_key(key, shift) binds the next key with Shift as a chord; a lone Shift is ignored (waiting for its key), Escape cancels.
  • Capture::Pad { first } — the capture cannot tell from the first button whether it is a plain press or a chord, so it waits: a second button pressed while the first is held makes first+second; the first released alone makes a plain binding.

assign_key / assign_pad remove the chord from every other action before setting it (the status line names the actions that lost it), so a chord is bound to at most one action. clear, reset_selected and reset_all restore defaults. The screen is a component with a frame method so the launcher and the in-flight pause menu (K) can both host it; it gives up a capture after 8 s (CAPTURE_TIMEOUT).

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is Action Every bindable action (64). ACTIONS, ActionInfo, info(action) The single table: name, action, keys, pad, group, label — one source for parsing, defaults, the menu and docs. Group Flight, Throttle, Weapons, Targeting, Power, Wingmen, Views, Camera, Interface; title(). KeyChord A key name plus optional Shift; parse, text. PadChord A button plus optional modifier button; plain, parse, text. StickLayout Space or Aircraft. Bindings keys: HashMap<Action, Vec<KeyChord>>, pad: HashMap<Action, Vec<PadChord>>, dead_zone, mouse_range, pad_invert_pitch, stick_layout, mouse_invert; from_yaml, to_yaml_text, legacy from_ini, translate. RawInput One frame of device state. Command One-shot app requests: targeting, MFD, View(View), WingMenu, wing orders (WingFireAtWill, WingAttackMyTarget, WingFormation, WingEvasive, WingRetreat, WingStatus), RepeatMessage, NextNav, Pause, Menu, MouseFlight. Power and equipment presses go to Controls::requests instead. View Cockpit, Forward, Left, Right, RearLeft, RearRight, Chase, ChaseManual; View::parse for --view. ChaseInput Chase-camera yaw/pitch/zoom/reset this frame. gamepad::PadState, gamepad::Button XInput-layout controller state and button names. THROTTLE_STEP 0.1 (10 % per press, as in the original). editor::Editor, Row, Setting, Capture, COLUMNS The controls menu's model (above). app::controls::ControlsMenu The controls menu screen component.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• OI_DEBUG_KEYS=1 openinterceptor … prints the names of keys as they are pressed.
  • One-shot inputs pressed in a frame that runs no simulation tick are carried over by Controls::carry_unconsumed, so a press is never lost on high-refresh displays.
  • An action that "does nothing": open the controls menu and look at its cells — a chord moved to another action is removed from the old one, and the status line said which. A pad button that does nothing on its own is probably used as a modifier in some chord.
  • A broken bindings.yaml cannot lock you out (a file that does not parse is reported and the defaults are used): Shift+D in the controls menu restores every default, and deleting the file recreates it on the next run.
  • A gamepad that does nothing on Linux: check /dev/input/js0 exists and is readable by your user (often the input group).

docs.title: Missions
docs.text: src/content/mission.rs (definitions) and src/mission/ (the runtime): battles described by roles, waves, objectives and outcomes, refereed on top of the simulation. The battle conditions are src/script/battle.rs, the outcome actions src/script/action.rs. Plan: Stage 3 part 1 (app 0.3.0). The modder's view is Missions.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Y["missions/*.yaml<br/>(any rules folder)"] --> RB["rules::build_at<br/>validate (files::mission), inherit, variants, per_level"]
    RB --> MP["MissionDef::parse(id, Get, pack, classes, levels)<br/>roles, waves, objectives, optional, timer,<br/>outcomes, chatter, debrief"]
    BS["script::battle::schema(role names, levels)"] --> MP
    AC["script::action::MISSION_ACTIONS"] --> MP
    MP --> TX["Content: @keys resolved<br/>(name, briefing, debrief, chatter, message args)"]
    TX --> RU["Ruleset::missions (sorted by order)"]
    RU --> ST["MissionRun::start(def, rules, shapes, player class)<br/>player + roles arriving at the start → World"]
    ST --> W["World"]

Layering. mission sits between sim and app: it reads and spawns into a World (through World::spawn_placement, the same path scenario objects take), but the simulation knows nothing about missions, so sim stays testable on its own.

docs.title: One frame of a mission
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    FS["FlightSession::frame"] --> STEP["World::step() × n ticks"]
    STEP --> UP["MissionRun::update(&mut World)<br/>after every tick"]
    UP --> L1["1. losses per role from member state<br/>(destroyed, departed, captured events)"]
    L1 --> L2["2. arrive: conditions → spawn_role;<br/>waves (once); chatter (once) → message lines;<br/>optional objectives latched"]
    L2 --> L3["3. end: retreat (player departed) →<br/>lose → win → draw → timer"]
    L3 -->|result| DB["Debrief: result, text, optional (met?),<br/>campaign actions, kills, losses, seconds;<br/>battle actions (message) run"]
    DB --> OV["debrief overlay over the frozen battle<br/>Enter: again · Esc/L: launcher"]
  • Placement (spawn_role): the count is rolled from [min, max], each member's class from the role's list; the arrival point is distance along bearing (yaw, pitch; [0, 0] = −Z from the player's start; random within ±20° pitch when absent) from the player's start or the centre of the from role's survivors; members stand side by side spread apart across the line of sight and face the player's start. Placed members get the role's faction, AI role, behaviour, protect flag, state, hull, destroyed systems and speed.
  • Counting: a member that has left the world is departed (hyperspace) if its slot still holds it (World::same_slot) and it departed, otherwise destroyed; captures come from Captured events. Kills are hostile losses, losses the player's own faction's.
  • Determinism: the mission's random choices come from its own generator seeded by starfield_seed, and condition random(p) from the same stream, so a mission replays identically with the same inputs.
  • Conditions are evaluated through BattleCx, which implements the script language's Context for this battle; role names are constants of the battle schema, compiled to indices.

docs.title: Launcher, --mission, soak
docs.text: The launcher lists missions after the scenarios (Mission: name, the briefing as the description, the ship choice when player.class is choose) and scrolls the list to keep the selection near the middle (launcher::Menu::first_visible, "^ more" / "v more" markers). Selecting one returns Next::Mission { mission, ship }; --mission <id> starts one directly. soak::run_mission plays a mission headless with the passive or AI pilot and reports the result (--soak <mission id>).

docs.title: AI changes made with missions
docs.text: Enemies now launch missiles only when closing in (within 2.5 × their attack range, at least 2 km); the first launch comes 3 s plus a random part of one interval into the attack, and each interval varies by ±25 %. Every AI pilot's random sequence is seeded per ship in World::spawn, so pilots that start together do not act together.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is content::mission::MissionDef A parsed mission: id, name, briefing, order, player_class, player_position, roles, waves, win/lose/draw, optional, timer, outcomes, chatter, debrief, starfield_seed. RoleDef, Arrival, WaveDef, ChatterDef A role (classes, count range, faction, AI, behaviour, protect, state, hull, destroyed systems, speed, at, arrive); an arrival (distance, bearing, from, spread); a wave; a radio line. mission::MissionRun The running mission: its definition, the player's id, per-role RoleRuns, wave/chatter/optional latches, its generator, kills, losses, debrief. mission::RoleRun members, arrived, destroyed, retreated, captured. mission::Debrief result, text, optional: Vec<(name, met)>, campaign actions (as text), kills, losses, seconds. mission::BattleCx The battle Context for conditions. script::battle::QUERIES, schema(roles, levels) The battle context's queries. script::action::{ActionDef, Action, Scope, MISSION_ACTIONS} Outcome actions with Battle or Campaign scope. schema::Ty::Either A schema type with two accepted forms (count, bearing, class). World::spawn_placement, World::same_slot Spawn one placed object; whether an id's slot still holds its ship. app::Next::Mission, FlightSession::start_mission Starting a mission from the launcher or --mission.

  • MissionRun::start(&MissionDef, Arc<Ruleset>, Arc<Vec<Shape>>, Option<ShipClassId>) -> Result<(World, MissionRun), String>; run.update(&mut World) -> Vec<String> (message lines); run.spawn_role(&mut World, role, count, at) -> Result<usize, String>.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• --check reports every mission problem with file, line and path (missions.x: roles.y…, unknown roles in conditions, unknown actions).
  • --mission <id> --ship <id> jumps straight in; --soak <id> --difficulty <level> [--soak-pilot ai] plays it headless and prints soak mission <id> (<level>, <pilot>): <result> after <n> s; <k> kills — the quickest way to check that a mission can be both won and lost.
  • A role that never appears: its arrive: condition never held, or its at.from role has no survivors (it then appears at the player's start). arrived(role) in a chatter line makes arrivals visible in play.
  • A "MISSION ERROR: …" message line means a role could not be spawned (an unknown slot in a station's modules, for example).

docs.title: Packs, VFS and rules
docs.text: src/content/: answers "what is in the game?". Chooses the campaign and its active set of packs, loads them in dependency order, indexes the player's original data, builds the typed Ruleset (including ship systems, power and damage rules from content::equipment), parses scenarios, and loads individual assets on demand as plain CPU data. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added mod kinds, the active set, equipment, behaviours and difficulty, and moved every mod file to YAML checked against schemas (mod format 2: formats::yaml, content::schema, content::files). The user-facing side is in Modding.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    CFG["ContentConfig<br/>pack_dirs, mods_dir, original, no_original,<br/>disabled, campaign"] --> D["pack::discover<br/>folders with pack.yaml<br/>(kind, parent, targets, format)"]
    D --> CA{"which campaign?<br/>cfg.campaign if available,<br/>else preferred_campaign"}
    CA --> AS["pack::active_set<br/>parent chain + targeting addons<br/>+ their depends"]
    AS --> DIS{"disabled in<br/>settings.yaml?"}
    DIS -->|skip + warning| W
    DIS -->|keep| SK{"requires_original<br/>and no data?"}
    SK -->|skip + warning| W["warnings"]
    SK -->|keep| O["pack::order<br/>stable topological sort"]
    CFG --> OD["vfs::OriginalData::open<br/>index files by name, open DLLs"]
    O --> RS["rules/, campaign/ and missions/*.yaml of every pack<br/>yaml::parse → Node trees"]
    RS --> B["rules::build_at(level)<br/>validate → merge → levels → inherit/variants/per_level → typed structs"]
    OD -->|"original:File.ini/Section<br/>(still INI)"| B
    B --> RU["Ruleset<br/>incl. behaviours, difficulty"]
    O --> SC["scenarios/*.yaml → validate → Scenario<br/>later pack replaces same id"]
    O --> TX["text/<language>/*.yaml (else text/en/)<br/>+ imports of original LangFile*.txt<br/>→ TextTable"]
    TX -->|"@key resolved"| B
    TX -->|"@key resolved"| SC

docs.title: From YAML text to typed rules
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T["file text"] --> Y["formats::yaml::parse<br/>strict subset → Node<br/>(every value a string + line)"]
    Y --> V["schema::validate(node, files::rules())<br/>unknown keys (did you mean), types, units"]
    V --> M["merge_into, pack by pack<br/>maps merge, lists replace,<br/>empty removes, key+ / key- edit lists"]
    M --> L["campaign.difficulty →<br/>level index"]
    L --> I["resolve inherit (ids, original: INI)<br/>apply variants[level]<br/>pick per_level[level]"]
    I --> TY["typed structs via schema::Get<br/>(num, qty with unit, list, …)"]
    I -.-> SCH["behaviours: script::parse_condition<br/>checked against the object schema"]

Logic flow of rules::build_at(sources, original, level):

  1. Validate every file against files::rules(); each problem becomes <file>:<line>: <key path>: <message>.
  2. Merge the files in load order (merge_into): definitions of the eight definition sections by (section, id), global sections by name; mappings merge recursively, values and lists are replaced, an empty value removes a key, key+ / key- edit a list (kept until there is a list to edit, so they also work on an inherited list). Each entry remembers the pack and file:line that last wrote it.
  3. Difficulty: the campaign section's difficulty list and the level asked for (else default_difficulty, else the middle level) give a level index.
  4. Resolve each definition: inherit chains (same section, section.id, or original:<file>/<section> read through the OriginalLookup and renamed by snake_case; depth limit 16 catches cycles) → variants[level] merged over it → every {per_level: […]} replaced by its entry → dropped if delete: true.
  5. Type: factions, beams, missiles (guidance, damage mode, cluster submunitions resolved by id), systems (built-ins of every SystemKind first), damage and power, the sound cue table (audio.cue_table; every cue:<Name> reference resolved), behaviours (with prefer selectors), looks — effects (the engine's explosion added if none), debris sets, model sets (texture swaps, damage levels, states) — (conditions parsed and checked against the object schema with the level names as constants; builtin_attack added if no pack defines it), then ships and objects (which refer to the others by id; model_set, or a model set made from the shorthand model/debris; class_systems resolves systems, systems+, systems-, vct; modules as (slot, class)), then missions (MissionDef::parse against the battle schema of their role names), cockpits (with anchors), flight, sounds.

Every problem is collected; a broken definition is skipped, the rest still load. Scenarios go through the same parse and files::scenario() validation (Scenario::from_yaml), and manifests through files::pack() (PackInfo::parse).

Text (content::text, Stage 2): before the rules are typed, every active pack's text/<language>/*.yaml (falling back to text/en/ for a pack without the language) is read into one TextTable, later packs replacing keys; imports: read the original's language files from the CD by reference (formats::langfile) under a prefix (orig.<KEY>). TextTable::resolve turns @key values into strings in names, descriptions and scenario titles; a missing key is an error and shows as the key.

The schemas are data (schema::Ty trees built in files.rs), so one description drives validation, the JSON Schema export (files::json_schemas, --write-schemas; the committed schemas/*.schema.json are checked by the gate) and the Mod file reference.

docs.title: Mod kinds and the active set
docs.text:
pack::PackInfo carries kind (Campaign, Addon, Library), parent (campaigns only), targets (addons) and format (newer than pack::FORMAT = 2 is refused; a folder with only a format-1 pack.ini is refused with a pointer to the docs). The player plays one campaign; Content::load picks it from ContentConfig.campaign (command line --campaign or settings.yaml game.campaign), and the difficulty from ContentConfig.difficulty, falling back with a warning to preferred_campaign: interceptor when available, else default, else the first campaign found.

flowchart LR
    ID["campaign id"] --> CH["pack::chain<br/>follow parent links,<br/>root first; error on cycle"]
    CH --> AD["+ addons whose targets<br/>name a chain campaign, *, or nothing"]
    AD --> DP["+ everything they depend on<br/>(transitively)"]
    DP --> OR["pack::order<br/>parents and depends first"]

--check and the gate run once per campaign, each with its own active set. When no pack is a campaign (a Stage 1 setup) every pack loads, as before.

docs.title: Asset loading and per-asset overrides
docs.text:
Content::load_* parses an AssetRef. Pack-relative paths resolve in the pack that defined them. An original: reference first asks find_override: every active pack is searched, highest priority (latest in load order) first, for a file at the asset's override path (vfs::override_paths); only if none exists is the CD read.

flowchart LR
    R["original:CockpitA.dll#12000"] --> OP["override_paths(Image, 'CockpitA.dll', '12000')<br/>images/cockpita/12000.png | .tga"]
    OP --> FO{"find_override:<br/>latest pack with the file?"}
    FO -->|yes| PF["decode the pack file<br/>(PNG alpha, no colour key)"]
    FO -->|no| CD["OriginalData → TARG resource<br/>(cyan colour key applied)"]
Original asset Override path in a pack mesh INTTYPEA models/inttypea.obj texture CUBETOP (named by a model) textures/cubetop.png or .tga image CockpitA.dll#12000 images/cockpita/12000.png or .tga loose image file images/<file stem>.png sound Xwinder.wav sounds/xwinder.wav

Paths are lower-case. These are exactly the paths --extract writes (Extractor), so an extracted, edited file dropped into a mod replaces the original. Whole packs can be switched off with packs.disabled in settings.yaml (Settings); a disabled pack contributes no rules, scenarios or overrides.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• --check prints every file problem as file:line: key.path: message and every rules error as file:line: section.id: message, plus model, texture, image, sound and scenario failures, per campaign. --list shows the campaigns (* = loaded) and what loaded. --check --campaign <id> checks one campaign.
  • "campaign 'x' is not available; using the default" — the id is wrong, the pack is disabled, or it needs original data that was not found. "only a campaign may have a parent", "unknown pack kind", and "needs mod format n" come from PackInfo::parse.
  • An addon that seems ignored: check its targets names the campaign being played (or the campaign's parent).
  • "pack 'x' skipped" means it needs --data (or a dependency was skipped); "pack 'x' is disabled in settings" means settings.yaml switched it off.
  • Is my override used? Open the launcher's Asset browser: overridden textures, images and sounds are marked [overridden by <pack>].
  • A key that "does nothing": check the section id prefix (ship: vs object:) and that a later pack does not override it; keys are case-insensitive, values are not.
  • A YAML error such as "tabs are not allowed" or "anchors are not supported" names the line; see the supported subset on Rulesets.
  • A value that "does nothing" may be at the wrong level: {per_level: …} and variants are resolved before typing, so check which difficulty is loaded (the launcher header shows it).

docs.title: Platform layer
docs.text:
src/platform/: the only operating-system-specific code. #[cfg(target_os = "…")] chooses at compile time which implementation is built. Plan: Stage 1 (gamepads); Stage 7 (packaging).

Platform Gamepads Window / GL / audio macOS GameController.framework via the Objective-C shim macos/shim/oi_platform.m macroquad (Cocoa, OpenGL, CoreAudio) Linux kernel joystick API /dev/input/js0, std only (linux.rs) macroquad (X11, OpenGL, ALSA) other none yet (Windows XInput planned) macroquad

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["app::devices::Devices::read"] --> G["platform::Gamepads::poll"]
    G -->|macOS| M["macos::pad_state(0)<br/>unsafe extern \"C\" oi_pad_state(index, *mut OiPad)"]
    G -->|Linux| J["linux::JoystickReader::poll<br/>non-blocking read of 8-byte js events"]
    M --> P["input::gamepad::PadState"]
    J --> P
  • macOS: build.rs compiles oi_platform.m with xcrun clang and ar (no extra crates) and links GameController and Foundation. The shim reports the first controller with an extended-gamepad profile (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro, MFi) in XInput layout. Adapted from the Looking Glass macOS port's shim (MIT).
  • Linux: the device is opened with O_NONBLOCK; each read applies all pending events (apply_event): buttons 0–10 and axes 0–7 in the common xpad layout, stick Y inverted to XInput's "up is positive", triggers rescaled to 0–255. If no device exists it retries about every two seconds; unplugging drops the device and retries.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text: src/render/: draws one frame of the 3D scene with macroquad. It only reads the simulation. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added looks (model sets with texture swaps), debris sets, effects with shock waves, station modules and their wrecks.

docs.title: Frame structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    CL["clear_background"] --> SKY["draw_sky<br/>2 500 stars + sun<br/>sky material: no depth, additive"]
    SKY --> SOL["draw_world<br/>ships, stations, debris<br/>lit material: depth test + write"]
    SOL --> GLO["draw_glows<br/>engines, bolts, missiles, sparks, explosions<br/>glow material: depth test, no write, additive"]
    GLO --> CP["draw_cockpit_model (3D cockpit, cockpit view only)<br/>flush + clear depth; 5 cm near plane"]
    CP --> HUD["2D HUD (hud::draw)"]

docs.title: Looks: which model to draw
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    SH["ship (class, hull fraction)"] --> MS["ruleset.model_set(class.model_set)"]
    MS --> SW["ModelSet::swaps_for(hull, state)<br/>set swaps → damage levels below → state"]
    SW --> MC["ModelCache::get_variant(intact, pack, scale, swaps)<br/>loaded once per distinct swap list"]
    MC --> DRAW["draw_world"]
    WR["World::wrecks"] --> WS["swaps_for(0, 'destroyed')<br/>placed at hub × offset"] --> DRAW

Renderer::ship_look picks the model a ship shows now: its model set's intact model with the texture swaps for its hull fraction (content::looks::ModelSet::swaps_for). Swaps match the model's textures by looks::texture_key (file name without folder or extension, lower-case). ModelCache::get_variant keys the cache by model, scale and swap list, so each damage level is built once and drawing it per frame costs nothing extra. Destroyed station modules with a destroyed state are drawn from World::wrecks on their hubs. OBJ slot_<name> groups are not part of the drawn mesh at all (the OBJ reader sets them aside as attachment points).

Effects (render::effects). On a Destroyed event, Effects::on_events starts an Explosion with the model set's destroyed_effect (size × radius, duration, colour, and a shock wave — a ring of glows racing outwards in the wreck's plane — when shockwave is set), and throws the debris set: pick distinct pieces chosen with the effects' generator, each starting at its place in the object's model space with the object's velocity plus a random outward push and tumble, plus the generic chunks; wreckage darkens as it cools over its last third and disappears after the set's life. Missile detonations draw the missile's explosion effect (SimEvent::MissileExploded { position, effect }; size in metres), else a 25 m, 0.8 s fireball. Point-defence tracers (SimEvent::PointDefence) are short streaks in the glow pass.

docs.title: The 3D cockpit pass
docs.text:
A cockpit definition may name a model (see Cockpits). It must always appear in front of the world and may sit centimetres from the pilot's eye, which the normal 1 m near plane would clip. So Renderer::draw_cockpit_model:

  1. flushes macroquad's batched draws (InternalGlContext::flush) so the world is on the GPU;
  2. clears only the depth buffer (quad_context.clear(None, Some(1.0), None)) — the world's colour stays, but nothing in it can hide the cockpit;
  3. draws the model with the lit material using SpaceCamera::with_near(0.05), placed at the eye plus ModelOffset (in the eye's frame), always at LOD 0.

This and the model-matrix stack are the only uses of macroquad's internal GL state (unsafe_gl_context, one documented unsafe block).

docs.title: Camera-relative rendering
docs.text: f32 loses precision far from the origin, and GPUs lose more. So no absolute world position reaches the GPU: each object's model matrix is built from position − camera.position (SpaceCamera::model_matrix), and the camera's view matrix is rotation-only (SpaceCamera::view_projection). Near plane 1 m, far plane 200 km.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
Material Shader GPU state Used for lit vertex lighting: 0.30 + 0.85 × max(n·sun, 0) × vertex colour × texture, plus a Tint uniform (hit flash); overlay depth bias depth test ≤, depth write, back faces culled (counter-clockwise = front) ships, stations, debris sky unlit depth always, no write, additive stars, sun glow unlit depth test ≤, no write, SrcAlpha + One engines, bolts, missiles, sparks, explosions

Normals reach the shader through macroquad's spare normal vertex attribute. Per-object transforms use macroquad's model-matrix stack (push_model_matrix), which breaks batches per object and snapshots uniforms per draw call — so the hit Tint is per ship.

docs.title: One-sided faces (back-face culling)
docs.text: Models are one-sided, as in the original game: the lit pipeline sets cull_face: Back with counter-clockwise front faces. The original data winds every polygon counter-clockwise around its outward plane normal, and models a surface seen from both sides as two polygons back to back (shield rings, fins). Without culling both copies drew at the same depth and flickered (z-fighting). Model::from_xmsh mirrors Z and reverses winding, so engine triangles stay counter-clockwise seen from outside; mod OBJ models follow the same rule (Models).

docs.title: Overlay layers and the depth bias
docs.text:
A decal lying exactly on another face (station panels, alien hull markings) has the same depth values as the face under it, so the depth test picks a winner at random per pixel — flicker. At load, model::assign_overlay_layers compares every pair of faces in a LOD: faces in the same plane (normals within 0.999, plane offsets within 1e-4 × radius), facing the same way, that overlap by the separating-axis test get stacked layers. Which is on top: faces flagged POLY_OVERLAY, then POLY_TRANSLUCENT, then ordinary faces; among equals the later face in the file (the original painted in that order). OBJ models use file order only. The pass takes about 8 ms for all 297 CD meshes; 119 of 17,284 LOD-0 faces get a layer above 0.

The layer travels per vertex in the spare w of the normal attribute (ModelVertex::layer). The lit vertex shader does

gl_Position.z -= normal.w * LAYER_BIAS * gl_Position.w;

which moves the face towards the camera in depth only (the image does not shift). LAYER_DEPTH_BIAS = 2⁻¹⁸ in normalised device coordinates, about 32 steps of a 24-bit depth buffer — the same idea as glPolygonOffset, done per vertex because a model is one draw call. Multiplying by w keeps the shift constant after the perspective divide. GLSL cannot read a Rust constant, so lit_vertex_source() pastes the number into the shader text at start-up.

Overlay-flagged faces are kept in their own material groups (MaterialGroup::overlay, GpuLod::overlay), so Renderer::show_overlays = false hides them (the model viewer's O).

docs.title: Texture addressing
docs.text: Original texture coordinates run outside 0..1 to tile a texture across a big face. Model textures are set to repeat (render::set_repeat, via texture_set_wrap on the internal GL context) instead of macroquad's default clamp, which smeared edge pixels across such faces (the "incomplete" Patton, the asteroids, many debris chunks). The UV varying is mediump, not lowp, so tiled coordinates keep their precision on GL ES devices.

docs.title: Bolt streaks
docs.text:
A bolt is drawn as a streak trailing behind its head. Bolt::streak_length() is min(muzzle_speed × 0.025 s, 80 m, muzzle_speed × age): never longer than the distance the bolt has flown from the gun. Without the last term, a bolt fired this frame trailed up to 80 m back past the muzzle, so in the chase view fire seemed to come from behind the ship.

LOD choice: GpuModel::lod(distance) picks the first LOD whose switch_distance exceeds the camera distance (the original values: e.g. 75 / 150 / 450 m / ∞ for the Lightning II). Objects entirely behind the camera are skipped.

docs.text: Symbol What it is Renderer Owns the three materials, a generated radial glow_texture, models: ModelCache, the star list, and reusable vertex/index buffers. camera::SpaceCamera position, rotation, fov_y, aspect, z_near; new(...), with_near(..); implements macroquad's Camera trait; project (world → screen pixels) and local_direction for the HUD. effects::Effects explosions, sparks, debris, created by on_events(&World) (from effects and debris sets) and aged by update(dt). effects::Explosion, Debris, Spark A fireball (with optional shock-wave plane), a tumbling piece with its life, a short spark. gpu::ModelCache::get_variant A model with texture swaps, cached per distinct swap list.   • draw_sky(&cam, seed, sun), begin_solid(&cam, sun), draw_model(&cam, &GpuModel, pos, rot, tint), draw_model_lod(.., force_lod: Option<usize>), draw_world(&Content, &World, &Effects, &cam, sun, hide), draw_glows(&Content, &World, &Effects, &cam, hide), draw_cockpit_model(&cam, &GpuModel, offset, sun), draw_axes, ship_model, ship_look(&Content, &World, &Ship).

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Reused buffers: draw_glows and draw_sky move their Vecs into a Mesh with std::mem::take, draw, then move them back — no allocation after the first frame.
  • If a scene is black except the HUD, check the shader compile error returned by Renderer::new (shown on the start-up error screen).
  • Engine glows come from rear-facing model attachments, else the back of the bounding box; GpuModel::engines is computed once at load, so drawing glows allocates nothing per frame.
  • A face that vanishes from one side is a back face: wind it the other way, or add a second face back to back if it must be seen from both sides. The viewer's wireframe (W) shows the missing face's outline.
  • Flicker on a flat area means coplanar faces facing the same way that the overlay pass did not pair (they are not in the same plane within tolerance); select them with [ ] in the viewer and compare their layer.
  • Stretched or single-colour faces on original models: check that the texture repeats (the face info line shows UVs beyond 0..1).
  • A 3D cockpit that is invisible usually sits behind the eye: check ModelOffset and that the model's front faces −Z.
  • A damage texture that never appears: the swap's key must be the model's texture name (no folder, no extension); open the class in the model viewer and press D to step through its looks, and --check reports swapped textures that fail to load.
  • Debris that flies from the wrong place was modelled away from the object: pieces must be in the object's own model space. The viewer's debris look pulls them apart from where they sit.

docs.title: Conditions (script)
docs.text: src/script/: the condition language that behaviours (and, from Stage 3, missions and events) use to decide things — hull < 25% and not system_damaged(engines). A complete little language implementation in four classic steps: lexing, recursive-descent parsing, type checking against a schema, and evaluation. Plan: Stage 2 item 2.9 (object context); Stage 3 adds the mission and event contexts and actions. The modder's view is on Behaviours and conditions.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T["condition text<br/>(from a rules file)"] --> L["lex<br/>tokens: Num (units applied),<br/>Name, Sym"]
    L --> P["Parser (recursive descent)<br/>or → and → not → comparison<br/>→ sum → term → unary → primary"]
    S["Schema<br/>queries (QueryDef) +<br/>constants (level names)"] --> P
    P -->|"type-checked at load"| E["Expr tree<br/>(queries by index)"]
    E --> EV["Expr::eval / test<br/>at run time"]
    CX["Context::query(id, args)<br/>sim::ai::ObjectContext"] --> EV
  • Lexing (lex): whitespace-separated numbers, names and symbols. A unit written straight after a number is applied at once (1.5km → 1500, 25% → 0.25; m, km, s, min, h, day, %). Names are lower-cased.
  • Parsing (Parser): one method per precedence level, lowest first — or, and, not, comparison (< <= > >= == !=, not chained), sum (+ -), term (* /), unary (-), primary (number, true/false, constant, query with arguments, brackets). Each method returns the sub-tree and its type (Num or Bool).
  • Checking happens while parsing, against the Schema: unknown names, wrong argument counts or kinds (system_damaged(warp)), and type errors (hull and 3, a comparison of booleans) are errors with a message; parse_condition also requires the whole expression to be true/false. Behaviours call it when the rules load, so a bad condition never reaches play.
  • Evaluation (Expr::eval) walks the tree. and/or short-circuit; == and != compare within 1e-6; division by zero gives 0. Queries are answered by a Context; arguments are evaluated first and passed as numbers (a name argument such as engines is resolved to its index while parsing).

There is no assignment, loop or user function, so evaluation cannot change the game and always finishes. random(p) draws from the asking pilot's seeded generator, so runs are deterministic.

docs.title: The object context
docs.text: script::object declares the queries a behaviour may use (QUERIES, with doc strings that the docs table is made from) and schema(levels) adds the campaign's difficulty level ids as numeric constants. sim::ai::ObjectContext implements Context for one ship: it holds &World, the ship's id, the time in its current state and the pilot's random state in a Cell<u64> — Context::query takes &self, but random must advance the generator, and a Cell allows that for a Copy value without &mut (interior mutability).

docs.text: Symbol What it is Token Num(f32), Name(String), Sym(&'static str). Expr Num, Bool, Query(u16, Vec<Expr>), Not, Neg, Binary(Op, …). Op Or, And, Lt, Le, Gt, Ge, Eq, Ne, Add, Sub, Mul, Div. Type, Value Num / Bool at check time; Value::Num(f32) / Value::Bool(bool) at run time. QueryDef, Arg A query: name, args (Arg::Num or Arg::Name(&[..])), result type, doc. Schema The queries and named constants available in one context. Context The trait a game context implements: query(id, &[f32]) -> Value. object::QUERIES, object::id, object::SYSTEM_NAMES, object::schema The object context (21 queries). sim::ai::ObjectContext The simulation's answer to object queries.

  • script::parse(&str, &Schema) -> Result<(Expr, Type), String>; script::parse_condition(&str, &Schema) -> Result<Expr, String> (must be true/false).
  • expr.eval(&dyn Context) -> Value, expr.test(&dyn Context) -> bool.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Every parse error is reported at load with the behaviour and transition it came from (--check lists them); messages say what was expected: "unknown name 'hul'", "takes 1 argument(s), given 0", "expected ',' or ')' in threats(...)", "missing ')'", "'hull' is a number, not a condition (compare it: 'hull > 0')".
  • To test a condition, write it in a behaviour and run --check; to see it fire, use a transition into an obviously different manoeuvre (do: circle) in a testbed scenario.
  • The language is pure, so new queries are unit-tested with a stub Context (see the tests in script/mod.rs) before the simulation answers them.

docs.title: Settings and data discovery
docs.text: src/settings.rs and src/cli.rs: where the player's things live, and how the engine finds the original Interceptor data without being told every time. Plan: Stage 1 (deployment layout); the launcher grows a settings screen in Stage 5.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
An installed OpenInterceptor separates what ships with the program from what belongs to the player:

OpenInterceptor-0.3.0.app/Contents/           (the program — safe to share)
  MacOS/openinterceptor
  Resources/packs/interceptor, packs/default  (built-in packs: no original content)

~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/      (macOS)
$XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/ or ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/   (Linux)
  settings.yaml    paths: original, mods; packs: disabled; game: campaign, difficulty, language
  bindings.yaml    controls (created on first run)
  original/        optional copy of the CD (tools/build_bundle.py --install-data)
  mods/            one folder per mod

Finding the original data (settings::resolve_original) — the first candidate that exists wins:

flowchart TD
    A["--data PATH<br/>(returned even if missing, so the error names it)"] -->|not given| B["OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA<br/>(merged into --data by cli::parse)"]
    B -->|not set| C["settings.yaml paths.original<br/>(relative paths are relative to the user data folder)"]
    C -->|missing| D["<user data>/original"]
    D -->|missing| E["game/ in the development checkout<br/>(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR)"]
    E -->|missing| F["no original data:<br/>only original-free packs load"]

The mods folder is --mods, else paths.mods, else <user data>/mods. packs.disabled lists pack ids to switch off (whole-pack activation, like XWVM's Game Content screen). game.campaign and game.difficulty are the campaign and difficulty level to load; the launcher's campaign switch (Tab) and difficulty switch (D) write them (app::remember_campaign), and --campaign / --difficulty override them for one run. Empty means the default choice (interceptor if its data is available, else default; the campaign's default_difficulty).

# settings.yaml
paths:
  original: /Users/me/Interceptor CD
  mods:
packs:
  disabled: [hd-cockpit-test]
game:
  campaign: default
  difficulty: ranger        # a level of game.campaign: ignored when another campaign loads
  language: en              # text/<language>/ folders (--language overrides)

Migration. Builds before the YAML formats wrote settings.ini and bindings.ini. When settings.yaml does not exist, Settings::load reads settings.ini instead (parse_legacy_ini), and the next save writes settings.yaml. bindings.ini is read once and saved straight away as bindings.yaml (app::load_bindings). The old files are left in place and ignored from then on.

tools/build_bundle.py presets paths.original to the checkout's game/ folder (or --data), so a freshly built app finds the CD at once.
