  • resolve_original(cli, env, &settings, user_dir, dev_tree) -> Option<(PathBuf, Source)> — pure apart from is_dir checks; tested with temporary folders.
  • cli::Options::content_config() assembles a ContentConfig from all of the above (campaign = --campaign, else game.campaign; difficulty = --difficulty, else game.difficulty only when the loaded campaign is game.campaign — a remembered level belongs to its campaign, so --check checks every other campaign at its default level; language = --language, else game.language, else en).

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --list shows which packs loaded; if interceptor is missing, no data folder was found — check settings.yaml or pass --data.
  • The launcher always loads the last campaign chosen there; if a campaign seems "stuck", look at game.campaign (or pass --campaign); the same for game.difficulty. --list marks the loaded campaign with *.
  • Unknown keys in settings.yaml are ignored, so a newer file still works with an older build.

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text: src/sim/: the battle as plain data, advanced by exactly TICK = 1/60 s per World::step. No rendering, no input devices, no clock reads, no macroquad — only glam maths and the Ruleset. That makes it deterministic and unit-testable (80+ tests). Plan: Stage 1 (flight, weapons, basic AI); Stage 2 (in progress) adds ship systems, power, damage to systems, special equipment, hyperspace and wingman orders (sim::systems), and will deepen the AI.

docs.title: One tick: World::step()
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["events.clear()"] --> B["ai::think<br/>AI pilots write Controls (two-phase)"]
    B --> B2["systems::handle_requests<br/>power settings, shield balance,<br/>tractor / cloak / ECM switches, hyperdrive"]
    B2 --> C["match speed resolved<br/>(sets Ship::speed_hold to the target's speed)"]
    C --> D["flight::step for every live ship<br/>throttle, turn rates, rotation, thrust/velocity, position<br/>(scaled by engine / manoeuvring / VCT efficiency)"]
    D --> D2["flight::hold_in_arena<br/>halt ships at arena_radius ('ARENA BOUNDARY')"]
    D2 --> E["combat::step<br/>lock → beams → missile controls → link mode<br/>→ point_defence → move_bolts → guidance::step"]
    E --> F["combat::ship_collisions"]
    F --> S["systems::step<br/>recharge → repair → disabled check<br/>→ tractors → countermeasures → hyperdrives"]
    S --> WR["destroyed modules with a destroyed look → wrecks"]
    WR --> MO["update_modules<br/>modules follow hubs, cascade, shield generators"]
    MO --> EX["expiring ships (doppelgangers) counted down"]
    EX --> G["clear one-shot controls and requests,<br/>since_hit += TICK, time += TICK"]

In short: AI → requests → flight → combat (incl. missile guidance) → collisions → systems → modules. Requests run before flight so a switch pressed this tick (a cloak, a power change) already counts; systems run last so that damage done this tick can knock a system out before repair and recharge look at it.

The player and the AI produce the same Controls struct and fly the same flight model.

docs.title: Flight model (sim::flight)
docs.text:
Two models, chosen per ruleset with flight.model:

flowchart TD
    C["Controls (player or AI)"] --> T["update_throttle<br/>set / delta / reverse;<br/>any manual input clears speed_hold"]
    T --> R["turn(): desired rates × turn_factor,<br/>exponential smoothing, quaternion update"]
    R --> M{"flight.model"}
    M -- newtonian --> N["brake? approach_vec(v, 0)<br/>hold? approach_vec(v, nose × hold)<br/>else thrust = nose × acceleration × throttle<br/>(reverse: −nose; afterburner: ×2)<br/>+ VCT thrust; cap at max_speed (+boost)"]
    M -- assisted --> A["forward speed → throttle × max_speed;<br/>drift damped; brake = 0"]
    N --> P["position += velocity × dt"]
    A --> P

newtonian (default). Space has no drag.

  • Throttle is thrust: acceleration × throttle along the nose. At zero throttle the ship coasts at its current velocity — it does not slow down.
  • Reverse (Z) points the thrust backwards along the nose.
  • Brake (hold B, gamepad B) retro-thrusts against the velocity at full acceleration and stops exactly at zero (approach_vec).
  • Speed limit: max_speed, or max_speed + boost while the afterburner burns (double thrust, cost energy per second). Thrust may not push past the cap; excess speed (after the burner stops) bleeds off at acceleration per second.
  • Turning changes the nose, not the velocity: a hard turn at speed makes the ship slide. VCT hulls add sideways/vertical thrust at 0.5 × acceleration (VCT_THRUST_FRACTION).
  • Flight computer (speed hold): Controls::hold_speed (set every tick by AI pilots) or Ship::speed_hold (set by match speed, M) drives the velocity towards nose × hold within the hull's acceleration — holding a forward speed and cancelling drift. Any manual throttle, reverse or brake input clears speed_hold. AI pilots therefore obey exactly the same thrust limits as the player.

assisted (the previous arcade model, kept for mods that want it): throttle sets a target forward speed (throttle × max_speed, reverse −½), the ship accelerates or decelerates towards it, sideways drift is damped, VCT slides at 25 % of max_speed (VCT_SPEED_FRACTION), brake targets zero.

Both models: pitch and yaw rates scale with turn_factor(speed, lock_speed) = clamp(1 − |speed| / lock_speed, 0, 1); roll is not reduced. Angular velocity approaches the desired value with blend = 1 − exp(−dt / τ), τ = damping_time(angular_damp) = 0.05 + 0.06 × angular_damp. Orientation is a quaternion (rotation × from_scaled_axis(ω·dt)); body axes x = pitch (+ nose up), −y = yaw right, −z = roll right. Static objects (kind: station, mines) never translate but may spin. Recharge of energy and shields moved to systems::recharge in Stage 2 (it now depends on the power settings).

System efficiencies. Thrust and the afterburner scale with efficiency(Engines) (no afterburner at 0), turn rates with efficiency(Manoeuvring), VCT slides with efficiency(Vct). A craft whose list lacks engines, manoeuvring or sensors is treated as having working ones that are not modelled; any other missing system does not work.

Arena edge. After flight, hold_in_arena(ship, arena_radius) places any ship beyond the radius back on the boundary sphere and removes its outward velocity (tangential motion is kept), emitting Message "ARENA BOUNDARY" when it first arrives. arena_radius: 0 means no limit. Default 60 000 m.

docs.title: Combat (sim::combat)
docs.text:
• Lock: the target inside the cone flight.lock_angle and within missile speed × duration for the selected missile's lock_time seconds → locked, SimEvent::LockAcquired. Leaving the cone resets it. Lock builds at efficiency(Sensors) speed, halved again while the target's ECM is on.
  • Tractor and cloak: while the tractor beam is on, beams do not fire ("BEAMS OFF-LINE: TRACTOR BEAM ON"); firing beams or a missile drops an active cloak ("CLOAK DROPPED").
  • Beams: LinkMode::Linked fires mounts in pairs, Full all at once, Unlinked one at a time; each mount has a cooldown of 1 / rate_of_fire; energy is checked for the whole group (NoEnergy event and a 0.5 s hold if short). Bolts inherit the ship's velocity; life = range / speed.
  • Bolts and missiles test the segment travelled this tick against every other ship's collision::Shape (sphere broad phase, triangle mesh for stations) so fast shots cannot tunnel.
  • Missiles are launched and flown by sim::guidance (below); impact damage on a hit; the proximity fuse detonates on a near miss (inside proximity_radius and moving away); expired missiles pop harmlessly.
  • Damage (apply_damage): fore or aft shield (by which side was hit) → armour → hull; hull ≤ 0 → alive = false, Destroyed, and every ship targeting or towing it lets go (forget_ship). Damage that gets past the armour without destroying the ship also strikes a system (systems::damage_system). A shield facing reaching zero says "FORE/AFT SHIELD DOWN".
  • Collisions: fighter–fighter spheres (60 % of radius) push apart and swap half their velocities; a fighter sweeping into a station mesh is backed out and bounced. Damage = relative speed × 0.1.

docs.title: Point defence (Stage 2)
docs.text: combat::point_defence runs before the missiles move: each ship with a PointDefence (range, rate, chance, energy) whose gun is cooled down and that has the energy fires at the nearest hostile missile within range (decoys included); chance is rolled on the world's seeded generator; a hit removes the missile. Each shot costs energy, sets Ship::pd_cooldown = 1 / rate and emits SimEvent::PointDefence { ship, from, to, hit } (tracer and sound).

docs.title: Probes and radar (Stage 2)
docs.text: systems::on_radar(world, observer, other) decides what a radar shows: detectable (a cloak hides a ship of another faction beyond its range), then within flight.radar_range — halved while systems::jammed(observer), i.e. inside the jamming radius of a live hostile probe — or within the sensors range of any live probe of the observer's faction. Objects that never move always show. Missile lock also builds at half speed while jammed. Probes are ordinary objects with a ProbeDef { sensors, jamming }.

docs.title: Missile guidance (sim::guidance, Stage 2)
docs.text:
combat fires a missile through guidance::launch, which applies the class's launch-time behaviour; guidance::step (called by combat::step every tick) steers, moves and detonates every missile, collecting blasts first and applying them after the loop (the same two-phase pattern as the AI).

flowchart TD
    L["guidance::launch(missile)"] --> CW{"guidance"}
    CW -- cloaked_wait --> D1["slow to 20 %, life × 4"]
    CW -- parallax --> D2["release decoys: harmless missiles<br/>flying away from the launcher"]
    CW -- doppelganger --> D3["spawn a fragile copy of the launcher<br/>(expires); enemies may switch to it"]
    S["guidance::step"] --> LU["lure: a missile homing on a decoy's launcher,<br/>within LURE_RANGE (2.5 km), switches to the decoy<br/>at LURE_CHANCE (0.8) per second"]
    LU --> ST["steer: homing / sidestep (2 × turn inside 600 m, weave)<br/>/ cluster (split near the target or at half fuel)<br/>/ cloaked_wait (sleep until prey in trigger_range)<br/>/ dumbfire"]
    ST --> HIT["segment test against ships → impact;<br/>proximity fuse; fuel out"]
    HIT --> BL["blasts → apply_damage_mode<br/>(normal / bypass_shields / enveloping)"]

area_blast(world, at, radius, damage, except) damages every ship in radius, falling off linearly, enveloping; mines use it (systems::handle_requests on a detonate request: radius = 4 × the warhead's proximity_radius, at least 100 m). The modder's view: Missiles and mines.

docs.title: Station modules (Stage 2)
docs.text: World::spawn_modules(hub, depth) (called by from_scenario for every placed object) spawns each modules entry of the hub's class at its attachment point — an OBJ slot_<name> or an original manipulator index, looked up in the class's collision::Shape::mounts — turned so the module's −Z follows the slot's facing, with the hub's faction and Ship::mount = (hub, offset, rotation); modules with a behaviour fly it (turret), the rest are idle; up to five levels. update_modules (every tick, after systems) puts each module back on its hub, destroys the modules of a destroyed hub, removes wrecks whose hub is gone, and zeroes a station's shields while none of its shield_generator modules survives ("STATION SHIELDS DOWN"). A destroyed module whose model set has a destroyed state becomes a Wreck { class, hub, offset, rotation } in World::wrecks, drawn by the renderer on its hub. Modder's view: Stations and modules.

docs.title: Systems (sim::systems, Stage 2)
docs.text:
Everything a pilot manages inside the ship. Data comes from the systems, power and damage sections (Rulesets); each ship has power: Power, systems: Vec<SystemState> (one per fitted system), repairing, towing, hyperspace, disabled and departed.

flowchart TD
    subgraph req["handle_requests (early in the tick)"]
      R1["F9/F10: cycle() a setting, wrapping E → A"]
      R2["; and ': raise() one setting,<br/>lowering the other to stay within Budget"]
      R3["S: balance Equal → Forward → Aft"]
      R4["tractor / cloak / ECM: toggle()<br/>needs fitting, condition > 0, free steps;<br/>tractor also a target in Range"]
      R5["H: start countdown (hyperspace_time / efficiency)<br/>or abort"]
    end
    subgraph step["step (after combat)"]
      S1["recharge(): energy × beam_recharge[level];<br/>shields × shield_recharge[level] × efficiency;<br/>excess over a facing's cap flows to the other"]
      S2["repair(): one system, worst first,<br/>repair_rate × damage-control multiplier"]
      S3["disabled = engines and manoeuvring both at 0"]
      S4["tractors(): collect Tow::Pull / Tow::Release, then apply"]
      S5["countermeasures(): sensors lose cloaked targets;<br/>missiles may lose cloaked / jamming targets"]
      S6["hyperdrives(): count down, 'JUMP IN n',<br/>depart(); a held disabled capturable ship is Captured"]
      S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> S6
    end

Conditions. SystemState::condition() is Ok above half its hit points (efficiency 1), Damaged at half or below (0.5), Inoperative once its hit points reach 0 (0) and Destroyed below −destroy_below × max (0, for the battle). SystemState::set_hp keeps an offline flag: a knocked-out system stays Inoperative until repaired back to ONLINE_AT = 25 % of its hit points, so the first moments of repair do not bring a wreck straight back. A knocked-out switchable system switches off; a knocked-out hyperdrive aborts a countdown.

Damage. damage_system strikes one random non-destroyed system with the damage that got past the armour × system_share, and emits SystemChanged when the condition changes.

Repair. repair keeps working on the current job; otherwise it takes the worst-off system (first in fitting order on a tie). Speed = class repair_rate × (1 + (repair_rate of the damage control computer − 1) × its efficiency); the computer does not speed up its own repair.

Power. raise and cycle work on a plain Power value and the PowerRules, not on the world, so they are tested exhaustively. shield_caps(shields, balance, shift) gives the fore and aft capacities shields × (1 ± shift).

Tractor. The beam holds its target on its current bearing at a distance between 1.2 × the two radii and 0.6 × range, steering the target's velocity towards the captor's by at most strength × efficiency m/s². The hold is lost beyond 1.5 × range, if the target goes, or if the tractor is knocked out ("TRACTOR BEAM RELEASED"). Because a pull changes another ship, decisions are collected as Tow values first and applied afterwards (the two-phase pattern of ai::think).

Cloak and ECM. detectable(world, observer, other) hides a cloaked ship of another faction beyond its cloak's range; targeting (targeting::cycle, nearest enemy) only offers detectable ships and a sensor that loses its target says "TARGET LOST". Each second, a missile homing on a ship loses its target with chance strength / 100 × efficiency per active cloak, plus per active ECM within range of the missile.

Hyperspace. The countdown announces the last five seconds; at zero depart removes the ship (alive = false, departed = true, Departed event). If its tractor holds a disabled, capturable ship, that ship departs too and Captured { captor, prize } is emitted.

docs.title: AI (sim::ai)
docs.text:
think reads the whole world into a list of decisions, then writes them (two-phase update). Each AI ship has a role from its scenario (ai::Behaviour): Idle, Target (slow circle, never fires), Wingman (formation and orders, below) or Enemy. A disabled AI ship does nothing but drift.

Enemies fly a behaviour from the rules (content::behaviour, modder's guide): the scenario object's behaviour, else the class's, else the engine's builtin_attack.

flowchart TD
    T["think: for each Enemy"] --> B["behaviour_of: object → class → builtin_attack"]
    B --> RB["run_behaviour"]
    RB --> CK{"check_clock ≤ 0?<br/>(4 × per second)"}
    CK -->|yes| TR["first transition with matching from,<br/>a different to, and when.test(ObjectContext)"]
    TR --> ST["state, state_time = 0"]
    CK -->|no| FL
    ST --> FL["fly(manoeuvre, params, skill)"]
    FL --> AT["attack / turret: aim_point<br/>(reaction lag, aim error ≤ (1 − aim) × 8°),<br/>in_burst (burst/pause), fire_cone"]
    FL --> OT["idle, circle, patrol, evade,<br/>retreat (jump), tow (tractor + jump)"]
    AT --> C["Controls"]
    OT --> C
  • Aim. Every skill.reaction seconds (aim_point) the pilot takes a fresh look at its target (position and velocity) and draws a new aim error, uniform over a disc of radius (1 − aim) × MAX_AIM_ERROR (8°). Between looks it assumes the target flies straight on from the last sighting. The lead point uses the target's velocity relative to the shooter (bolts carry the shooter's velocity).
  • Fire discipline. in_burst alternates burst seconds of firing with pause seconds of holding; guns fire only inside fire_cone and inside range (and 95 % of the first beam's reach). Missiles every missiles seconds when locked (0 = never).
  • Systems use. At each transition check, systems: conditions of the behaviour are evaluated (ObjectContext) and turned into ordinary Requests: cloak / ecm switched to match their condition, power_to_shields while shields_first holds and shields are below the top level, else power_to_beams while beams_first holds. The requests go through systems::handle_requests like the player's keys, and reach the ship once (they are cleared after the tick).
  • Missiles (Stage 3). An attacker launches only within 2.5 × its attack range (at least 2 km); its first launch comes 3 s plus a random part of one interval into the attack, and each interval varies by ±25 %. Every AI pilot's random sequence is seeded per ship in World::spawn (from its slot and the world's generator), so pilots that start together do not fire together.
  • Target choice. attack and turret keep the current target while it lives and stays visible; otherwise they pick targeting::preferred_hostile with the behaviour's prefer weights (a matching hostile counts as distance / weight; several matches multiply), within 8 km (attack) or range (turret).
  • Mines. The mine manoeuvre sets Requests::detonate when a hostile is within range.
  • Turrets. Controls::aim (a world direction) lets a ship with turret_arc > 0 fire its beams along the aim instead of the nose, if the aim is within the arc (combat::fire_beams); the turret manoeuvre stays put and sets it.
  • Tow. The tow manoeuvre finds the nearest disabled, capturable hostile (nearest_prize), closes in, requests the tractor within 90 % of its range and then the hyperdrive.
  • Each pilot has its own seeded random stream (AiState::rng), so random(p) and aim errors are deterministic.

Wingmen follow WingOrders from their leader (order_wingmen); they fend for themselves if the leader dies. When they engage they fly attack with the parameters and skill of their class's behaviour (its first attack state):

Order Behaviour Formation (default; "ignore my target") Hold the formation slot. AttackMyTarget Attack the leader's current target if it is hostile. FireAtWill Engage the nearest hostile near the leader. Evasive Break formation and weave near the leader for EVASIVE_TIME = 10 s, then form up. Retreat Run from the nearest hostile at full speed (afterburner while energy lasts) and start the hyperdrive.

wing_status(world, leader) returns one line per wingman: name, hull and shield percentages, current order, and DISABLED if so.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is World rules: Arc<Ruleset>, shapes: Arc<Vec<Shape>>, ships, bolts, missiles, events, time, deterministic xorshift random(). ShipId { index, generation } — a generational handle. A destroyed ship's slot can be reused; the generation changes, so old ids resolve to None. Ship Class, faction, name, position, rotation (Quat), velocity, angular velocity, throttle, reverse, afterburning, braking, speed_hold, hull/armor/shields/energy, controls, pilot, target, link mode, beam cooldowns, missile racks, lock, since_hit, alive; Stage 2: power, systems, repairing, towing, hyperspace, disabled, departed. Helpers system(kind), efficiency(kind), is_on(kind), cloaked(). Controls Pilot input for one tick: axes, slide, throttle set/delta, reverse toggle, match speed, afterburner, brake (held), hold_speed (flight computer target, m/s), aim (turret direction), fire, link/missile cycling, requests. carry_unconsumed keeps unconsumed one-shot presses across frames that run no tick. Requests Edge-triggered power and equipment presses: beam_charge, shield_charge, power_to_shields, power_to_beams, shield_balance, tractor, cloak, ecm, hyperspace, detonate (mines); merge. Wreck, World::wrecks A destroyed module left on its hub. Ship::mount, Ship::expires A module's hub and place on it; seconds left for a short-lived ship (a doppelganger). guidance::LURE_RANGE, LURE_CHANCE 2 500 m, 0.8 per second. content::rules::Guidance, DamageMode The missile's steering kind and warhead mode. Power, ShieldBalance Beam and shield level indices (0 = A) and Equal / Forward / Aft. SystemState, Condition One fitted system: id, kind, hp, max, destroyed, offline, on; set_hp, condition(), ONLINE_AT. Condition::{Ok, Damaged, Inoperative, Destroyed} with efficiency() 1 / 0.5 / 0 / 0. systems::Setting, systems::Tow Beam or shield (for raise / cycle); a tractor decision (Pull(target, velocity, max accel) or Release(captor)). ai::WingOrder, ai::EVASIVE_TIME Wingman orders (above). ai::AiState Per-ship AI memory: role (behaviour), behaviour override def, leader, offset, order and order time; behaviour state, state_time, check_clock; break_timer, missile_timer, burst_clock; reaction_clock, seen (last sighting), aim_error; home; rng. ai::ObjectContext Answers condition queries about one ship (Conditions). ai::CHECKS_PER_SECOND, MAX_AIM_ERROR, ENGAGE_RADIUS, HUNT_RADIUS 4, 8°, 3 km (wingmen engage near the leader), 8 km (enemies look for targets). FlightModel Newtonian or Assisted (flight.model), in FlightRules with arena_radius. Pilot External (the player) or Ai(AiState). SimEvent BeamFired, MissileLaunched, Hit, Destroyed, MissileExploded { position, effect }, LockAcquired, Collision, Message, NoEnergy; Stage 2: SystemChanged { ship, system, condition, repaired }, Disabled { ship }, Departed { ship, position }, Captured { captor, prize }, Switched { ship, kind, on }, PointDefence { ship, from, to, hit }. Bolt, Missile, Lock, LinkMode Projectiles and weapon state. collision::Shape, TriMesh Bounding radius plus optional triangle mesh. TICK 1.0 / 60.0.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
• World::new(rules, shapes, seed), World::from_scenario(&Scenario, rules, shapes, player_class) -> Result<(World, ShipId), String>.
  • world.spawn(class, faction, name, position, rotation, pilot) -> ShipId, get, get_mut, id_of(index), live_ids(), step().
  • flight::step(&mut Ship, &ShipClass, &FlightRules, dt), turn_factor, damping_time, approach, approach_vec(v, target, max_step), update_throttle, hold_in_arena(&mut Ship, radius) -> bool; constants VCT_THRUST_FRACTION, VCT_SPEED_FRACTION.
  • combat::step(&mut World, dt), apply_damage(world, id, amount, at), ship_collisions, rotate_towards, mount_offset.
  • combat::forget_ship(world, id) — every ship targeting or towing id lets go.
  • guidance::launch(&mut World, Missile), guidance::step(&mut World, dt, &Ruleset), guidance::area_blast(world, at, radius, damage, except).
  • world.spawn_placement(&Placement, player) -> Result<ShipId, String> (one scenario object or mission role member: class, faction, pilot, modules, starting damage and speed); world.same_slot(id).
  • world.spawn_modules(hub, depth) -> Result<(), String> (an unknown slot is an error).
  • targeting::preferred_hostile(world, me, &[(Selector, f32)]) -> Option<(ShipId, distance)> — the nearest hostile with distances divided by matching preference weights.
  • systems::handle_requests(&mut World), systems::step(&mut World, dt), raise(&mut Power, Setting, &PowerRules, switched) -> bool, cycle(...) -> bool, shield_caps(shields, balance, shift) -> (f32, f32), power_message(&Power, &PowerRules), switched_power(&Ship, &Ruleset), power_used(&Ship, &Ruleset), recharge(&mut Ship, &ShipClass, &PowerRules, dt), repair(&mut Ship, &ShipClass, &Ruleset, dt) -> Option<(index, before, after)>, damage_system(world, id, amount), detectable(world, observer, other) -> bool, on_radar(world, observer, other) -> bool, jammed(world, ship) -> bool.
  • ai::think, ai::order_wingmen(world, leader, WingOrder) -> usize, ai::wing_status(world, leader) -> Vec<String>, steer_towards, lead_point, ai::nearest_prize(world, me, within) -> Option<ShipId>.
  • targeting::cycle, nearest_hostile, in_sights(world, me, max_angle_deg), off_nose_angle.
  • collision::segment_sphere, segment_triangle (Möller–Trumbore), segment_shape.
  • sim::euler(Vec3 degrees) — yaw/pitch/roll to a quaternion (positive yaw turns left).

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• To compare the two flight models, set flight: {model: assisted} in a mod's rules (or a small addon to the default campaign) and fly the same scenario; the HUD status line shows BRAKE while braking and HOLD n while a speed hold is active.

  • Because step is deterministic, a bug can be reproduced as a unit test: build a world with sim::test_support::world() (a tiny in-memory ruleset), place ships, set controls, call step in a loop, assert. Most tests in sim/ are written exactly this way.

  • --view chase or --view chase-manual shows the player's own ship to check orientation and engine glow; the MFD Status page shows shields, armour, hull and energy live, and the Systems page each system's condition.
  • The systems-trial scenario (both campaigns) exercises power, tractor tow and capture, cloak and hyperspace. Scenario objects with destroyed_systems = engines, manoeuvring start disabled, and hull = 0.3 starts them damaged, so a system state can be set up without fighting for it.
  • Every power or equipment refusal is a pilot message ("INSUFFICIENT POWER FOR …", "NO TARGET IN TRACTOR RANGE", "… INOPERATIVE"); the message line and L (repeat) show why a switch did nothing.
  • An enemy that "does nothing": check its role (ai: enemy in the scenario) and that its behaviour's states can act (an attack state with a range its beams reach). --check reports behaviours whose conditions do not parse.
  • Balance by numbers: --soak <scenario> --ship <id> --difficulty <level> [--soak-pilot ai] plays the battle without a window and reports how long the player lasted, hits taken and enemies destroyed; the default campaign's balance promise is held by a unit test of the same runner (soak).
  • Missions sit above the simulation: mission::MissionRun::update runs after each World::step and spawns through World::spawn_placement (Missions); sim itself knows nothing about them.

docs.title: Testbed
docs.text: src/app/: the interactive program — a small state machine of screens sharing one AppContext. Every stage adds scenarios here so its features can be play-tested. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added the controls menu, the campaign switch, the wingman comms menu, system and hyperspace messages, and --screenshot.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Launcher
    [*] --> FlightSession: --scenario id
    [*] --> ModelViewer: --model name
    Launcher --> FlightSession: Enter on a scenario (Next::Fly)
    Launcher --> FlightSession: Enter on a mission (Next::Mission)
    [*] --> FlightSession: --mission id
    Launcher --> ModelViewer: Enter on Model viewer (Next::Viewer)
    ModelViewer --> Launcher: Esc
    Launcher --> AssetBrowser: Enter on Asset browser (Next::Assets)
    AssetBrowser --> Launcher: Esc
    Launcher --> Controls: Enter on Controls (Next::Controls)
    Controls --> Launcher: Esc (save bindings.yaml)
    Launcher --> Launcher: Tab or D (Next::Reload) reloads Content for another campaign or difficulty
    FlightSession --> Launcher: Esc menu → L
    FlightSession --> FlightSession: Esc menu → K (controls menu inside the session)
    FlightSession --> FlightSession: Esc menu → R, or Enter after death
    Launcher --> [*]: Esc
  • app::run(options) loads Content, creates the Renderer, loads sounds (async), reads the bindings, then loops: the current screen's frame returns a Next, then next_frame().await. A start-up failure shows an error screen instead of crashing.
  • --screenshot <png> (with --scenario or --model) runs the starting screen for --frames frames (default 120), saves what was drawn as an opaque PNG and exits — a way to check a cockpit or model on several window sizes without playing.
  • Launcher (launcher.rs): the header names the loaded campaign and difficulty level; Tab (pad Y) switches to the next campaign (launcher::next_campaign) and D (pad X) to the next difficulty level (launcher::next_difficulty), each returning Next::Reload { campaign, difficulty }: the app reloads Content (the ruleset is rebuilt at that level), saves the choice in settings.yaml (game.campaign, game.difficulty), and shows any load error on the launcher. Entries: the model viewer, the asset browser, Controls, every scenario, then every mission (Mission: name, its briefing as the description; Missions). The list scrolls to keep the selection near the middle (Menu::first_visible, "^ more" / "v more"). Scenarios are sorted by order (the first scenario is selected at start). For player: choose scenarios, Left/Right picks among playable ship classes, previewed as a turning model with name, description and stats. Keyboard, mouse (click to select, click again to start) and gamepad (D-pad, A/Start, Back to quit). Skipped-pack warnings and start errors are shown.
  • Model viewer (viewer.rs): every ship class's model, then every original mesh. Orbit with arrows or mouse drag, zoom with +/− or the wheel, PgUp/PgDn (or B/N) to change model, L to cycle LOD (auto, 0–3), Space to stop spinning, Esc back. The camera is fitted to each model's radius and never enters it; viewer::wheel_steps turns wheel movement into zoom steps. The near plane follows the orbit (viewer::near_plane: just in front of the model, at least 1% of the distance, never under 5 cm), so depth precision suits a 600 m station as well as a 2 m debris chunk. Mesh-debugging keys: W cycles Display::Solid / SolidWire / Wire (each original face's outline as 3D lines, pulled 0.3% towards the camera over a solid model, plus a dot on every vertex of faces towards the camera); [ / ] select a face (Shift ×10), outlined and numbered, with viewer::face_info on the info line (index, corners, texture, flags, overlay layer, UVs); I numbers every face towards the camera; O toggles Renderer::show_overlays (restored on Esc). D (class entries) cycles the class's looks (viewer::looks_of: intact, each damage level, each named state, and the debris pieces pulled apart from the centre), named on the info line (look_label). --model NAME opens the viewer on a model (viewer::find_entry: ship id or mesh name, whole names, case-insensitive).
  • Asset browser (assets.rs): every original texture, image (cockpits, HUD, menus, sprites) and sound, loaded exactly as the game loads them — so a pack override shows its replacement, and the entry is marked [overridden by <pack>]. Tab switches between Textures, Images and Sounds; Up/Down (Shift: ×10) or B/N move; Enter or Space plays a sound; Esc back. Images are drawn over a checkerboard so transparency is visible. Its frame is async because loading a sound for playback is (macroquad's API); the app loop .awaits it.
  • Controls (controls.rs): the controls menu component (ControlsMenu), used from the launcher and from the flight pause menu; see Input.
  • Missions in a flight session: FlightSession::start_mission builds the battle with MissionRun::start; after each tick MissionRun::update referees it and its lines go to the message display; when it ends, the battle freezes behind the debrief (result, text, kills, losses, time, optional objectives, campaign actions; long text wrapped). Enter (pad A) flies it again, Esc or L returns to the launcher; the pause menu's R also restarts the mission.
  • Flight session (flight.rs): see the frame loop on the overview. Views F1–F8; after death the camera orbits the wreck; Esc opens a menu (Esc resume, R restart, K controls, L launcher); P pauses. The player's cockpit may have 2D art, a 3D model, or both; the HUD uses the cockpit's design space in the cockpit view and the default glass layout in the other views. A 3D cockpit on a window narrower than its design widens the field of view (cockpit_fov), and its anchored instruments are drawn on the dashboard in perspective (draw_anchored). Stage 2 additions:
    • Cockpit layout editor (F12 in the cockpit view; the battle pauses): LayoutEditor holds the selected instrument, the drag in progress and a status message; edit_layout handles Tab, 2D drags and nudges, 3D ray picks on the cockpit model's top LOD, resizing by wheel or +/-, and S, which save_layout writes as an addon <user data>/mods/<campaign>-cockpit-<id>/ (pack.yaml + rules/cockpit-layout.yaml). See Cockpits.
    • Wingman comms menu (], pad LB + left stick click): the six WING_MENU entries (fire at will, attack my target, ignore my target, evasive, retreat, status report), chosen with digits 1–6 or the d-pad and A; B or ] closes it. While open, the d-pad and A belong to the menu, not to throttle, MFD and afterburner. A status report puts one line per wingman on the message line.
    • Messages (event_messages): system damage and repair ("… DAMAGED: HALF EFFICIENCY", "… INOPERATIVE: REPAIRS UNDERWAY", "… BACK ON-LINE", "… REPAIRED", "… DESTROYED"), "ENGINES AND THRUSTERS OUT: SHIP DISABLED", "TARGET DISABLED", "… JUMPED OUT", "… CAPTURED", "HYPERJUMP COMPLETE". L repeats the last message.
    • Jumped-out end screen: "JUMPED TO HYPERSPACE", with the captured prizes listed; Enter flies again, Esc returns to the menu.

docs.title: Scenarios shipped
docs.text:
Id Pack What it tests flight-test interceptor Stage 1 exit scenario: player (any hull), X-COM base, two Lightning wingmen, one of every alien and pirate type flying practice circles; nav points base, aliens, pirates (N cycles). combat-test interceptor The same arena (and nav points) with every alien and pirate hostile. gunnery-range interceptor Six drones circling ahead; beams, link modes and missile locks. station-tour interceptor Every station type in a row, a Patton cruiser and a freighter. systems-trial interceptor Stage 2: power controls, a disabled Wraith (destroyed_systems) to tow with the tractor beam and capture by jumping out, a cloaking Shade, a Harbinger that tries to tow you; wingman orders. rocket-vs-saucer default No original data: choice of Guard rocket flown from the 3D cockpit guard, two wingmen, the Guard station, a flight of Dominion saucers. The basic dogfight. dominion-raid default A Dreadnought disc, raider saucers and robot sentinels attack the Guard station; three wingmen. black-comet-ambush default Escort a Prospector hauler past a cosmium asteroid while Black Comet hot-rods attack; neutral Senate and Cartel ships nearby. systems-trial default The default campaign's systems trial: a crippled raider saucer to tow and capture (Meteor or Thunderbolt), power controls, the Thunderbolt's cloak ("invisibility screen"), a Grappler that tries to drag the prize off. duel-<enemy> both You against one enemy type (default: scout saucer, raider saucer, dreadnought, robot sentinel, grappler, hot-rod; interceptor: wraith, spectre, phantasm, shade, harbinger, drone, pirate Lightning, Firestar and Avenger) — how it flies and fights at each difficulty. mixed-dogfight both Several factions at once, everyone hostile to someone. escort interceptor Escort an X-COM freighter against Wraiths and a Spectre. debris-showcase both Every class at 2 % hull in a row: damage textures at once, then one shot each shows explosion, shock wave and debris. Nothing shoots back. base-assault interceptor An alien base with plasma gun pods and shield pods; two wingmen. outpost-strike default A Dominion outpost with death-ray pods and a shield pod: shields drop with the pod, the pods die with the hub. probe-net both A friendly sensor probe 7 km ahead shows enemies on your radar early; a hostile jamming probe on the way halves your radar range and slows locks until you shoot it down. construction-defence default A research station at 60 % (state: build_60, protected, no guns yet) and a manufacturing frame at 25 %; Dominion raiders try to wreck them. convoy-ambush default Escort two cargo clippers (protected) from the mining facility while Black Comet hot-rods and a saucer pounce; a lost clipper loses its cargo.

The Stage 1 sample-arena scenario (pack sample) was retired when the sample pack became the default campaign; rocket-vs-saucer takes its place in the manual tests.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is AppContext content, renderer, sounds, bindings, devices. Next Stay, Launcher, Viewer, Assets, Controls, Reload { campaign, difficulty }, Fly { scenario, ship }, Mission { mission, ship }, Quit. launcher::next_campaign(&Content), next_difficulty(&Content) -> Option<String> The campaign / difficulty level after the current one (wrapping), if there is another. controls::ControlsMenu The controls menu component (new, frame). assets::AssetBrowser, assets::Tab, assets::entries(&Content, Tab) The asset browser; entries (pure) lists assets with their override pack. launcher::Menu Pure menu state: entries, selected, ship, playable; move_selection, move_ship, choosing, activate. viewer::Look, looks_of, look_label The D key's looks of a model set: Intact, Damage(i), State(i), Debris. viewer::Orbit, viewer::wheel_steps Orbit camera maths (pose, update) and mouse-wheel steps. flight::FlightSession World, player, view, MFD page, chase orbit, nav, pause/menu flags, accumulator, cockpit texture, 3D cockpit model and offset, design space, instruments. flight::view_pose(View, pos, rot, radius, &ChaseOrbit) Camera placement per view (pure). flight::apply_command, flight::event_messages Targeting/wing-order commands and pilot messages (pure). flight::WING_MENU The wingman menu entries (label, Command), in the original's order. flight::cockpit_fov(design_aspect, aspect) Vertical field of view for a 3D cockpit: 60°, widened on screens narrower than the design (pure, tested). flight::MAX_FRAME 0.25 s cap on time fed to the simulation per frame.

docs.text:

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --data <cd> --scenario flight-test --ship firestar --view chase jumps straight into a scenario; add --campaign default (or interceptor) to pick the campaign.
  • openinterceptor --no-original --scenario rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --screenshot shot.png saves the cockpit view after 120 frames. The window opens at 1280×960 (4:3), so this shows the widened 3D-cockpit field of view; compare with a manual run in a 16:9 window (MT-2-14).
  • Scenario errors (unknown class, faction or leader) are shown in orange on the launcher and printed to standard error.
  • openinterceptor --campaign default --soak rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --difficulty cadet plays the scenario headless and prints the player's fate (src/soak.rs): how long a passive ship survives, or whether an AI-flown one wins (--soak-pilot ai), per difficulty level.
  • A layout saved by F12 that seems ignored: the addon targets the campaign that was loaded when it was saved; check --list shows <campaign>-cockpit-<id> and that it is not disabled.
  • openinterceptor --mission defend_station --ship comet starts a mission directly; --soak defend_station --soak-pilot ai --seconds 400 plays it headless and prints the result.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
Game data is never inside a build

The app contains the engine and the built-in packs (which hold no original content). The player's CD, settings and mods live in the user data folder.

docs.title: Plain build
docs.text: cargo build --release produces target/release/openinterceptor. It finds the original data automatically (Settings and data discovery).

docs.title: macOS app
docs.text:
python3 tools/build_bundle.py                    # app + settings.yaml pointing at ./game
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --data /Volumes/CD # settings point at another copy
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --install-data     # clone the CD into <user data>/original
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --no-settings      # leave settings.yaml alone
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --skip-build       # reuse the last release build

tools/build_bundle.py (standard-library Python) builds the release binary, assembles dist/OpenInterceptor-<version>.app (dist/ is git-ignored), and signs it ad hoc:

OpenInterceptor-0.3.0.app/Contents/
  Info.plist                 identifier io.github.bbogovich.openinterceptor, version, game category
  MacOS/openinterceptor
  Resources/packs/           interceptor and default packs
  Resources/LICENSE-MIT

Then it prepares the user data folder ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/: settings.yaml paths.original is set to ./game (or --data), keeping any other settings; --install-data instead clones the CD into original/ (an APFS clone costs almost no disk) and points the settings there; mods/ is created. The program finds its packs at ../Resources/packs relative to the executable, so it works when Finder starts it with / as the working directory (verified: the bundled binary run from / loads both packs and the CD, --check 0 errors).

docs.title: Build numbers
docs.text:
Like ArenaVM's per-phase apps, versions follow the implementation stages: 0.<stage + 1>.<build>. The version is Cargo.toml's; bump the last number for each new build of a stage. From Stage 2 on, a stage's in-progress deliveries continue the previous stage's numbering and the stage's own 0.<stage + 1>.0 marks it complete: the first Stage 2 delivery is 0.2.2, and 0.3.0 marks Stage 2 complete (it also carries Stage 3 part 1).

Stage Versions Builds 0 Foundation 0.1.x (no app; analysis, formats, docs) 1 Flight simulator 0.2.x 0.2.0 — first app: newtonian flight, overrides, --extract, HD/3D cockpits, asset browser; 0.2.1 — mesh rendering fixes (tiled textures, back-face culling, overlay layers), viewer mesh tools and --model, bolt streaks, radar alignment 2 Combat, objects and behaviours 0.3.x 0.2.2 — mod kinds and campaign choice, ship systems, power, damage and repair, tractor, cloak, ECM, hyperspace, wingman orders, controls menu and gamepad chords, power/systems instruments, default campaign Perils of the Void, --screenshot, then YAML mod files, behaviours, looks, guidance, modules, probes, text keys; 0.3.0 — Stage 2 complete, plus Stage 3 part 1 (missions) 3 Missions, environments and conditions 0.4.x part 1 shipped in 0.3.0 4 Strategy layer 0.5.x — 5 Campaigns 0.6.x — 6 Presentation 0.7.x — 7 Modding toolkit and Remastered 0.8.x — 8 Platforms and release 1.0.0 —

docs.text: A tarball with the binary, packs/ and a .desktop file. AppImage is under consideration.

docs.title: Windows

docs.text:
cargo run --release -- --data game          # launcher
cargo test                                  # unit tests
cargo clippy --all-targets                  # lints (kept at zero warnings)

docs.title: Deviations
docs.text:
Where OpenInterceptor knowingly differs from the original game, or uses an engine value where the original's is unknown, and why. A deviation on the record is a decision; an undocumented one looks like a bug.

ID Deviation Why Stage DEV-001 Default keys for actions the original left undocumented: M match speed, W cycle missile, Kp4/6/8/2 VCT slides, Q/E roll, LeftControl also fires beams, C mouse flight. These actions exist in the original's bindable list but their release defaults are not documented anywhere found; Q/E and LeftControl help keyboards without a keypad. 1 DEV-002 Navigation points in scenarios (nav: {<name>: …}), cycled with N, shown on the MFD Nav page and as an on-screen marker. The original has no in-mission nav points (travel happens on the strategy map). Mods need them; the test arenas use them to find the alien and pirate groups. 1 DEV-003 Gamepad support with an XInput-style layout. The original supported DirectInput joysticks and rudders only. 1 DEV-004 Mouse controls are rebindable (beams/missile via the bindings; steering range via mouse_range in bindings.yaml) and mouse flight is a toggle (C). The original fixed them; a toggle avoids the mouse fighting the menus. Steering direction follows the readme (cursor down = nose down). 1 DEV-005 Hardware 3D with per-vertex lighting instead of the 16 shade palettes. The shade palettes served the 1998 software renderer; palette 0 (full brightness) gives the texture colours. 1 DEV-006 Wide-screen: a cockpit's design space (640×480 for the originals) is scaled as large as fits and centred; the 3D view fills the window. Cockpits may declare their own design (e.g. 1920×1080) and may be 3D models. Modern displays are not 4:3; modders replace cockpits with HD, widescreen or 3D ones. 1 DEV-007 Multiplayer deferred, possibly never implemented. Not needed for single player or modding. 7 DEV-008 Original beam Range read as kilometres (Range=4 in GameSettings.ini → 4 000 m, when inherited through inherit: original:…). Since mod format 2 a mod's range takes a unit (2.4km, 350m; a plain number is metres), replacing the Stage 1 RangeMetres key. The original's 1–6 values have no documented unit; kilometres matches the documented sensor ranges (3–5 km). 1 DEV-009 Missile TurnRate and LockTime are engine values set in the Interceptor pack. The original stores no turn rate per missile; lock time depends on the targeting system (Stage 4 equipment). 1 DEV-010 Proximity fuse fires on a near miss: inside ProximityRadius and moving away from the target. A hit inside the target's collision shape deals ImpactDamage. Firing as soon as the radius was entered meant impacts never happened. 1 DEV-011 Hull Shields, Armor, Energy, EnergyRecharge, Acceleration are engine values per hull in the Interceptor pack. In the original they come from fitted equipment (ShieldType, ArmorType, EngineType*), which arrives with the equipment system. 1 → 4 DEV-012 Alien, freighter and capital flight values are estimates (MaxSpeed, turn rates, acceleration). The original file has flight values only for the three X-COM hulls; the others were coded per class. 1 → 2 DEV-013 Missile lock cone is 10° (flight.lock_angle). The original's SensorsSetting LockAngle units are not decoded. 1 DEV-014 Cockpit ↔ hull mapping A = Lightning II, B = Firestar, C = Super Avenger. Derived (one cockpit per hull), not confirmed. 1 DEV-015 One-shot inputs are carried across frames that run no simulation tick (Controls::carry_unconsumed). On high-refresh displays some frames run no tick; a key press would otherwise be lost. Not an original behaviour, an engine correctness fix. 1 DEV-016 Esc opens a pause menu (resume, restart, back to launcher) instead of resetting the MFD. The testbed needs a way back to the launcher; MFD pages cycle with </>. 1 DEV-017 Keyed cockpit pixels become transparent black, not transparent cyan. Filtering would otherwise blend cyan into the edges of the art. Visual result matches the original. 1 DEV-018 ~~"Ignore my target" and "retreat" wingman orders both mean "form on me"; "evasive" is not bound.~~ Resolved in Stage 2: every wingman order has its own behaviour (formation, attack my target, fire at will, 10 s evasive weave, retreat and hyperspace out) and evasive is bound (Shift+E). Distinct behaviours arrived with the Stage 2 AI. 1 → 2 DEV-019 Newtonian flight model by default: throttle is thrust, ships coast at zero throttle, Z reverses thrust, a held brake (B) retro-thrusts to a stop, MaxSpeed caps speed, turning does not steer the velocity. flight: {model: assisted} restores the arcade model (throttle = target speed, automatic slowing, drift damped). The original's flight model is not documented and felt arcade-like; the project owner chose physics where deceleration only comes from thrust. Keeping both as data lets each campaign choose. 1 DEV-020 Flight computer (speed hold): match speed (M) and every AI pilot fly a held forward speed through hold_speed, which thrusts and brakes within the hull's own acceleration and also cancels sideways drift. Under newtonian physics AI pilots need a way to manage speed that obeys the same limits as the player; cancelling drift keeps AI dogfights readable. 1 → 2 DEV-021 Arena edge: ships reaching flight.arena_radius (default 60 km) are halted against it ("ARENA BOUNDARY"). Under newtonian physics a coasting ship would otherwise drift away for ever; outside testing this should rarely be reached. 1 DEV-023 Overlay polygons are depth-biased instead of drawn in BSP order; coplanar overlapping faces are found geometrically, the original overlay flag only decides which is on top. Translucent-flagged polygons are drawn opaque for now. A depth-buffered renderer cannot use painter's order per model; the same pass then also serves mod OBJ decals, which have no flag. The opacity meaning of the flag is not confirmed. 1 DEV-022 Per-asset overrides and --extract: any original model, texture, image or sound is replaced by a pack file at its override path; the extractor writes every original asset at those paths in OBJ/PNG/WAV. The modding objective: HD and 3D replacements without touching or redistributing the originals (compare XWVM, Modding). 1 DEV-024 Power budget and start levels are engine values: the beam and shield charge settings plus switched-on equipment share power.budget: 6 steps; ships start at beam D / shield C (interceptor) or C / C (default); tractor, cloak and ECM use 2, 3 and 1 steps. The original's charge-rate tables are verified (BeamRechargeRate, ShieldRechargeRate), but how many levels may be high at once and what equipment costs is not in the data (derived). All are power / systems data. 2 DEV-025 Firing drops the cloak (beams or a missile), with the message "CLOAK DROPPED". Prevents an invisible ship from attacking with impunity; the original's exact rule is unknown. Cloak lock-break by difficulty level waits for 2.8. 2 DEV-026 Hyperspace countdown of flight.hyperspace_time seconds (10 in interceptor, 8 in default), doubled while the hyperdrive is damaged; pressing H again aborts. The original's countdown length is not documented (derived). 2 DEV-027 Default keys for tractor, cloak and ECM: Shift+T, Shift+C, Shift+J. The original's key list has no documented default for these; Shift chords keep the plain T, C and J free. Rebindable in the controls menu. 2 DEV-028 Gamepad modifier layer: holding the left shoulder (LeftShoulder) switches the pad to a second layer (LeftShoulder+A hyperspace, LeftShoulder+DpadUp power to beams, …); a button used as a modifier does nothing on its own. A controller has far fewer buttons than the keyboard has keys; chords make every action reachable from the pad (extends DEV-003). 2 DEV-029 System condition thresholds: above half its hit points a system works fully, at half or below at half effect, at zero it stops until repaired back to 25 %, below −destroy_below × hit_points (−50 %) it is destroyed for the battle. Repair takes the worst system first. The original shows damaged / inoperative / destroyed systems and repairs them, but its thresholds and repair order are not in the data (derived). Thresholds below zero and the repair rate are damage data. 2 DEV-030 Mod files are a strict subset of YAML, read by an in-crate reader (formats::yaml): no tabs, anchors (&a), aliases (*a), tags (!!str), multiple documents, complex keys (?) or plain scalars continued over several lines — each rejected with its line number. Every scalar stays text until the schema types it. Mod files moved from INI (format 1, no longer read) to YAML (format 2). YAML gives modders nesting, lists and comments that INI lacked, and is what OpenXcom modders know. A full YAML library was not taken: the project's dependency policy avoids dependencies for what the codebase can do, serde_yaml is unmaintained, and full YAML's implicit typing (no → false, 1.10 → 1.1) and anchors surprise modders. The subset covers every construct the mod files need; the original game's own INI files are still read as INI. 2 DEV-031 AI skill model: enemies aim with an error of up to (1 − aim) × 8°, re-picked every reaction seconds, fire in burst/pause cycles inside a fire_cone, and check behaviour transitions 4 times a second. The original's AI is hard-coded and its accuracy model unknown; this model is data, so each campaign tunes it per difficulty level. 2 DEV-032 Interceptor enemy behaviours and per-level values are derived (Wraith, Spectre, Phantasm, Shade, Harbinger, drones, pirates, corporates, X-COM wingmen; skill, bursts, missile intervals and flee thresholds for beginner … superhuman). The original's AI code is not data; the behaviours follow the strategy guide's descriptions of each class and were tuned in the testbed (and with --soak). What each original difficulty level changes in combat is unknown. 2 DEV-033 3D cockpit instruments drawn in perspective on the dashboard (anchors) and an in-game cockpit layout editor (F12) that saves an addon. Engine extensions for modding: the original has only 2D cockpits. XWVM's 3D cockpits show instruments on in-cockpit screens the same way. 2 DEV-034 Explosions are engine fireballs (size, duration, colour, optional shock-wave ring per effect) instead of the original's XSPT sprite animations; which original wreck set each class uses follows the set names. XSPT pixel runs are not decoded yet; the 28 wreck sets' names and chunk meshes are verified from Interceptor.exe, the class mapping is derived. Effects are data, so sprite explosions can replace the fireballs later without rule changes. 2 DEV-035 Module placement on the original bases is derived: which of the X-COM base's 33 and the alien base's 28 attachment points carries a turret, shield generator, hangar or pod. Hit points come from the original M_XCOM* / M_ALIEN* sections (verified); a station's shields fail once all its shield-generator modules are destroyed, and destroying the hub destroys its modules. The original assembles bases on the strategy layer (Stage 4), so their battle layout is not stored; the shield and cascade rules follow the strategy guide's descriptions (derived). Placement is modules: [{slot, class}] data. 2 DEV-036 Special missile behaviours are engine models of the original's descriptions: Sidestep turns twice as hard inside 600 m and weaves; Parallax decoys lure at 80 % per second within 2.5 km; Passive Cloaking waits for prey within 800 m; Doppelganger copies are fragile and short-lived; mines blast four times their fuse radius. The original's guidance code is not data; names and one-line descriptions are all that is known (derived). Every number is a missile key or an engine constant documented on Missiles and mines. 2 DEV-037 Shield rings on the radar scopes (front scope = fore shield, rear = aft; green / amber / red, blinking when down) and top-bar text placement in the interceptor cockpits (message in the lit band, throttle line, power and systems in the two strips below). The rectangles are measured from the cockpit art (verified pixel bounds); what the original showed in each strip and the ring thresholds are derived from the player's description of the original HUD. 2 DEV-038 Point-defence data is derived: which ships carry point defence (the Patton, the X-COM freighter, the bases; the dreadnought and the stations) and its numbers (range 900 m–1.2 km, 3–4 shots/s, 35–40 % kill chance, 3–4 energy per shot). Point defence also shoots at decoys. The original's point-defence behaviour is not data; the values are engine estimates tuned in the testbed. All are point_defence keys. 2 DEV-039 Probes act in battle: a sensor probe extends its side's radar to 8 km around it; an ECM / jamming probe halves hostile radar range and missile-lock speed within 2.5 km. The original launches probes from the strategy map; their battle effects and numbers are derived (mesh names SENSPROB, ECMPROB verified). Data: probe: {sensors, jamming}. 2 DEV-040 Mission arrivals belong to the role (at: {distance, bearing, from, spread} and arrive: <condition>) instead of a separate arrivals: map as first designed. One place per group keeps a role's composition, position and timing together; a role without arrive: enters at the start. Waves add members later. 3 DEV-041 Interceptor mission compositions are derived: the five implemented mission types (xcom_base_defense, defend_freighter_convoy, deep_space_encounter, attack_alien_outpost, destroy_alien_probe) use the original's own names, briefings and debriefs by key (@orig.*, read from the CD), but which classes appear, how many, where and in what waves are estimates, sized early-war so every level is winnable and losable (checked with --soak). The original composes battles in code and grows them with campaign progress (Stage 4); compositions are missions: data. %s in original briefings awaits the strategy layer. 3 DEV-042 Process: Rapid Prototyping run as an implementation project. The project follows the Rapid Prototyping workflow (SpecItOut proposal P65), but until sio supports a prototype kind the manifest declares kind: implementation, with spec pointing at this worktree's docs/specification (Definition and Specification 1.0.0). The sio client does not yet support the prototype kind; the implementation kind lets issues cite requirement IDs now. Process

docs.title: Implementation plan
docs.text:
An iterative, staged plan. Each stage ends with a playable build of the testbed: a launcher listing live test environments (scenarios) that show the stage's features and let a tester playtest one component at a time. Later stages add scenarios; none are removed.

Stage Version Delivers Status 0 Foundation 0.1.0 Repository, SpecItOut, docs site, format analysis, feasibility Done 1 Flight simulator 0.2.0 Packs and rules, model loading, rendering, cockpits and HUD, controls, flight model, weapons, targeting, wingmen, testbed Done (signed off 2026-11-10) 2 Combat, objects and behaviours 0.3.0 Mod kinds and parent; model sets (damage, construction states, debris); full damage, power and special systems; behaviours with difficulty variants; missiles, mines, probes, stations; effects, sound Done (deferred items listed) 3 Missions, environments and conditions 0.4.0 Condition/action language; mission types; space and atmospheric/ground environments with terrain; comms; hyperspace; debrief; Tier 2 script decision In progress 3 interlude: feedback and control console 0.4.0 Drift display, shot physics, visibility, base-defence balance, action catalogue and overlay; the tablet control console (server, protocol, components, target viewport, map; Arduino later) Planned 4 Strategy layer 0.5.0 Interactive star map, squadrons and sensors, economy, research, bases and modules, logistics (mining, research and manufacturing facilities, supply convoys, surveys — default campaign), ships and loadouts, pilots, functional screens, saves Planned 5 Campaigns 0.6.0 Events, arcs, rival plans, strategist, dynamic relations, endings: both campaigns playable start to finish Planned 6 Presentation 0.7.0 Screen layouts and skins, menus, video, interactive music, voices Planned 7 Modding toolkit and Remastered 0.8.0 Full validator, recipes (upscale, mesh patch), interceptor-remastered, modding guide Planned 8 Platforms and release 1.0.0 macOS app, Linux packages, Windows, release process Planned

docs.title: Three campaigns
docs.text:
The plan delivers three campaign mods, designed in Game design and mod format:

Campaign Grows in stages Complete interceptor: the full original campaign from the player's CD — the primary test case 2–6 Playable start to finish at Stage 5; presentation at Stage 6 default: Perils of the Void, a 1950s film-serial campaign with original content — runs without a CD 2–7 Playable start to finish at Stage 5; finished at Stage 7 interceptor-remastered: extends interceptor with locally generated upscaled textures and an enhanced Lightning 7 Stage 7

Every stage's features must work in both interceptor and default before the stage is done (the project's modding-first rule), so neither campaign can fall behind.

docs.title: Feasibility
docs.text: Confident. Every asset type stages 1–2 need was decoded and checked against the data: all 297 meshes parse; hulls and a saucer rendered correctly with their own textures; textures, cockpit images, sound effects and music loops are understood; all balance data is plain INI. The remaining unknowns (XSPT pixel runs, a few mesh fields, mfdanim.mps, the CD audio codec) have fallbacks and do not block any stage. The original simulator is far simpler than an id Tech 3 game: no levels, no skeletal animation, no scripting VM to reproduce.

docs.title: Ground rules
docs.text: Rule In practice The player supplies the game Original data is read from the player's own CD copy at run time. No original content in the repository game/, dist/ and every original asset type are git-ignored; the gate fails if one is tracked. Engine, not game Nothing Interceptor-specific is hard-coded: it lives in the interceptor pack as rules and scenarios. Original programs are data Interceptor.exe and the DLLs are parsed, never executed. Modding first Each feature is reachable from a pack before it is called done; the original-free default campaign (the sample pack in Stage 1) exercises it without original data. Tests before done Unit tests for every module; manual cases for what only a playtest shows (testing policy).

docs.title: Checks for every stage
docs.text:
• scripts/check.sh (unit tests, release build, --check on all packs, asset-tracking guard).
  • The stage's manual test cases, recorded as passed.

docs.title: Delivered
docs.text:
• Repository OpenInterceptor (MIT) with the SpecItOut manifest (implementation, specVersion: null), labels, .gitignore safety net, README and scripts/check.sh.
  • This site on the docs branch, with docs.sh.
  • Analysis of the CD: layout and formats.
  • Prototype decoders (outside the repository) that parsed all meshes and rendered models with their textures, used to confirm the formats before engine code was written.
  • Research into the original's gameplay and controls.
  • The architecture, the dependency decision (macroquad only) and this plan.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Decision Why Rust, one crate, macroquad 0.4.14 Proven in ArenaVM and Looking Glass on this machine; OpenGL 3 on macOS and Linux; small. All format readers in-crate Each is a few hundred lines; no crate exists for these formats anyway. INI for rules The original uses INI, so original sections import directly; no parser dependency. Revised in Stage 2: mod files moved to a YAML subset with schemas (DEV-030); original INI sections are still imported through inherit: original:…. OBJ + PNG/TGA for mod art Universal export targets; OBJ is trivial to parse. Gamepad without a crate macOS GameController shim (pattern from Looking Glass) and Linux joystick API with std.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Flight simulator
docs.text: Version 0.2.0. Status: done — signed off by the developer's playtest on 2026-11-10 (status). The core of the application: fly any playable ship in a live arena with the original's cockpit, controls, navigation, speed management and weapons.

docs.title: Exit scenario
docs.text: The testbed scenario Flight test: station patrol (flight-test) contains: the player's ship (any of the three playable hulls, chosen in the launcher), an X-COM base, two wingmen in formation, and one of each enemy type (Wraith, Spectre, Phantasm, Shade, Harbinger with its container, Spirit, Drone; pirate Lightning, Firestar and Super Avenger, Rogue Freighter) flying practice circles, plus nav points base, aliens, pirates. combat-test is the same arena with hostile AI. The player can fly with the cockpit controls, manage speed, target, and fire beams and missiles that damage and destroy targets.

docs.text:
# Item Module 1.1 PE resource reader; XMSH, XTXR, TGA, WAV (PCM, MS and IMA ADPCM), INI, OBJ readers, each with unit tests formats 1.2 Packs, VFS (pack files + original DLL resources), rules with inherit and layering, scenarios content 1.3 Asset cache: original/OBJ models to GPU meshes per texture, all LODs; textures with colour key model, render::gpu 1.4 Rendering: camera-relative transform, per-vertex sun lighting, LOD selection, starfield, sun render 1.5 Flight model from hull rules: newtonian default (thrust, coasting, reverse, brake, speed cap) and assisted option; afterburner; speed-hold flight computer (match speed, AI); VCT; arena edge sim::flight 1.6 Beams (energy, rate of fire, link modes) and missiles (lock time and cone, homing) sim::combat 1.7 Targeting (next/prev/closest/in-sights), collisions, damage, destruction sim 1.8 Wingmen formation; basic enemy pursuit; idle objects sim::ai 1.9 Cockpits A/B/C, reticle, radar, target MFD, gauges, message line; views F1–F8 hud, render::camera 1.10 Keyboard, mouse, gamepad (macOS shim, Linux joystick API), bindings.ini input, platform 1.11 Testbed launcher: scenario list, ship selection, model viewer app 1.12 sample pack with original-free models and a scenario packs/sample 1.13 --check headless validation check 1.14 Settings and data discovery: user data folder, settings.ini, automatic CD discovery settings, cli 1.15 Per-asset overrides of original models, textures, images and sounds; pack switch-off content 1.16 --extract: original assets → OBJ/PNG/WAV at their override paths extract 1.17 Cockpits with their own design space, HD art and 3D cockpit models; a 3D cockpit in the sample pack hud, render, packs/sample 1.18 Asset browser in the testbed app::assets 1.19 macOS app bundle with stage build numbers (0.2.x) tools/build_bundle.py

Items 1.14–1.19 were added at the project owner's request after the first playtest: the CD was not found without --data, the arcade flight model slowed ships without thrust, and modding needed extraction and per-asset replacement (HD and 3D cockpits) in the XWVM manner.

docs.text:
Launcher entry Id Shows Model viewer — Every ship class's model and every original mesh; orbit camera, LOD forcing, attachment points Asset browser — Every original texture, image and sound, with pack overrides marked; sounds play Flight test: station patrol flight-test The exit scenario above Combat test: hostile arena combat-test The same arena with every alien and pirate hostile Gunnery range gunnery-range Six drones circling ahead: beams, link modes, energy, missile lock Station tour station-tour Every station type, a Patton cruiser and a freighter: models, LODs, station collision Sample pack arena (no original data) sample-arena Original-free ships and station from the sample pack, a 3D cockpit, hostile raiders

docs.title: Stage 2 — Combat, objects and behaviours
docs.text:
Version 0.3.0. Status: complete (app 0.3.0, main d7553f5, 2026-11-11), except the deferred items below — XSPT sprite explosions and the model-set extras — and the manual passes, which are still to be recorded. docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Dependencies. The server (HTTP, WebSocket framing) and the console page are to be written in-crate and with plain web components; anything else needs the dependency evaluation first.

Voices planned. 3.8 Hyperspace out with countdown; retreat outcomes; debrief screen (results, salvage, score) mission, app Partial: hyperspace out with countdown (Stage 2) — the player jumping out is the retreat result; the debrief screen (result, text, kills, losses, time, optional objectives, campaign actions). Salvage and score are applied by the strategy layer (Stage 4). 3.9 Simulator missions with a setup screen app Planned. 3.10 Tier 2 script language decision (Lua via mlua recommended): dependency evaluation recorded on the dependency page, then hooks (do: script, do: ["script(...)"]) and the sandboxed API script Planned. 3.11 interceptor: the 27 mission types, the simulator types and the final mission's two parts as mission definitions (compositions from the guide, else derived estimates) packs/interceptor Started: 5 of 27 — xcom_base_defense, defend_freighter_convoy, deep_space_encounter, attack_alien_outpost, destroy_alien_probe; original names, briefings and debriefs by @orig key; compositions derived (DEV-041). 3.12 default: the 11 generated mission types (2 on surfaces) and chapter missions 1, 2, 4, 5 playable from the testbed; terrain and sky assets generated packs/default, tools Started: 4 missions — defend_station, convoy_ambush, construction_defence, intercept_scouts — with text in text/en/missions.yaml. 3.13 Logistics missions (default campaign, design): convoy_ambush (generated when a supply convoy reaches the attack point chosen at random at its launch; protect it; cargo lost if destroyed, stored by the enemy if captured) and construction_defence (from 50 % construction, at most three per location; the facility in its construction-stage state); roles from the strategy situation; auto-resolve when the player does not fly; the campaign context queries they need mission, script Partial: construction_defence and convoy_ambush exist as missions flown from the launcher; generation from the strategy layer is Stage 4.

Testbed adds (so far: missions on the launcher with scrolling, --mission, --soak <mission>): a mission browser (every mission type of both campaigns, with difficulty and force choices), a terrain flight sandbox (atmospheric handling on several worlds), and a condition-language console.

Exit: every mission type winnable and losable in the testbed; atmospheric flight feels distinct from space (manual test); the language fully unit-tested (parser, types, evaluation, error messages).

docs.title: Stage 4 — Strategy layer
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0. Status: planned. The real-time strategy game around the battles: the interactive star map, bases, research, the economy, ships and loadouts, pilots — with functional screens and saves. Story and the rival's planning come in Stage 5.

Design: strategy layer, interface.

docs.title: Work items
docs.text:
# Item Module 4.1 Campaign clock: dates, time speeds, auto-pause; the campaign and starts definitions; starting a new game with a chosen campaign and difficulty campaign (new) 4.2 Star map: generated (classes, bodies, names, hidden black holes; seeded) and fixed maps; free and lane travel; endurance and stranding campaign::map 4.3 Squadrons, convoys and probes on flight plans; sensor coverage; contact detection; mission generation when they meet campaign 4.4 Economy: resources, income and expense expressions, markets (buy/sell), factories and queues with priorities, deliveries and losses, storage campaign::economy 4.5 Research: download and labs models, discovery by prerequisites, salvage and capture, unlocks campaign::research 4.6 Bases: types, placement rules, templates, module construction (build times and construction states), limits, effects, destruction consequences, dismantling campaign::bases 4.7 Ships and equipment: hulls, items, slots and fitting rules, power draw, stock designs, purchase and manufacture of craft campaign 4.8 Pilots: generation, ranks, experience, training, injury and healing, bravery, recruiting, salaries, voices campaign::pilots 4.9 Patron funding and evaluations; score and ratings; periodic reports campaign 4.10 Screens (functional, plain skin): star map, bases with the 3D base view, research, hangar, market, pilots, reports, messages, briefing/debriefing; battle hand-off and return app::strategy (new) 4.11 Saves: the full campaign state plus the mod list and versions; load refuses missing mods campaign::save 4.12 interceptor: map generation tables, economy, the 71 research topics with authored unlocks, 68 modules with effects, items, pilots, salvage, funding evaluation, score names packs/interceptor 4.13 default: the fixed six-system map, economy, both research trees, Guard modules and Dominion pods, items, pilots packs/default 4.14 Logistics (default campaign, design): resources, components and deposits (campaign data); facility_types mining facility, research station, manufacturing center with placement conditions, build cost, time and three construction stages; the economy tick (extraction, recipes that start only when their inputs are in store, research, construction progress) campaign::economy 4.15 Supply and demand: the order book (main base ← manufacturing ← mining; research ← mining once per project), automatic government supply convoys on fixed lanes (several vessels, even cargo shares), the attack point chosen at random at launch, delivery and loss/capture rules; mission-generation hooks for ambushes and construction strikes campaign::logistics, campaign::convoys 4.16 Survey ships (a separate mission profile and craft; within the launching station's radar range; 25 % attack roll at launch; suitability per facility type), research sites and station-only tech branches (lab:, site:, start_cost — materials only to begin), facility fighter pools (built at main bases, transferred, movable) campaign 4.17 Facility, survey and supply-traffic screens (functional); default: resources, components, deposits, facility types, recipes, research sites and branches (the stage models, facility objects and supply craft exist since Stage 2) app::strategy, packs/default

Testbed adds: a strategy sandbox for each campaign with a debug clock, money and research cheats (the original's own cheat list — payday, knowitall, quickbase — as debug actions), and "jump to battle" from any contact.

Requested logistics for the default campaign (4.14–4.17) are an engine capability that the interceptor campaign deliberately does not use (it stays faithful to the original; an addon could add it). It is all YAML data and a campaign may leave it out. Decisions and the one open question (cargo capacity): Logistics.

Exit: both campaigns' strategy layers run for 6 game months without errors, with economy, research and bases behaving as specified; save/load round-trips (unit tests on synthetic campaigns; manual long-run test).

docs.title: Stage 5 — Campaigns
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0. Status: planned. Story, rivals and relations: what turns the strategy layer into a campaign with a beginning, middle and end. At the end of this stage both campaigns are playable from start to finish.

Design: campaign and game flow, events, relations and strategist.

docs.title: Work items
docs.text:
# Item Module 5.1 Events: conditions, chances per check, actions, choices, offers (accept/refuse), cooldowns; news campaign::events 5.2 Arcs: ordered steps, arc state in conditions campaign::events 5.3 Rival plans: stages, budgets, shipments by convoy, visibility, grants, completion, warnings campaign::plan 5.4 The strategist: budgets, aggression, exploration, expansion, outposts, offence ladder, defence priorities, tech levels, cheats, build priorities campaign::strategist 5.5 Factions: patrons, independents, hostiles; dynamic relations with relation rules, drift, stances and their battle and strategy effects; stance-change events; relations screen campaign::relations, app 5.6 Victory, defeat and endings (total/partial victories) campaign 5.7 Encyclopaedia (functional) with unlock conditions app 5.8 interceptor: the Doomsday arc (five messages and their gates), the Doomsday plan per difficulty, MacArthur and the final mission, the seven side missions, the alien strategist from Think.ini and the guide, news and report triggers packs/interceptor 5.9 default: the 12-chapter serial arc with progress-based triggers, the Eclipse Engine plan, the Dominion strategist, dynamic relations among the six factions (Senate, Cartel, Prospectors, raiders), chapter title cards (plain), narrator text packs/default 5.10 Fidelity: the open items closed or recorded as derived packs/interceptor, docs 5.11 Rival logistics (default campaign): the Dominion's mines, cosmium shipments (the Eclipse Engine's convoys) and supply depots storing captured cargo (the player seizes a destroyed depot's stock); raids on the Guard's lanes and strikes on facilities under construction; third-party convoys: Prospector expeditions (to a system under investigation, pause, home) and Cartel runs to random destinations, with relation effects campaign::strategist, packs/default

Testbed adds: an event and arc debugger (fire events, set flags and plan progress, view relations), and campaign start-at-chapter for the default campaign.

Exit: a full play-through of each campaign at a middle difficulty (manual tests, with a log of milestone dates); automated soak test running each campaign for a simulated year with the player's battles auto-resolved, checking invariants (money accounting, no orphan references, arc progress monotonic).

docs.title: Stage 6 — Presentation
docs.text:
Version 0.7.0. Status: planned. The campaigns look and sound finished.

Design: interface, text and media.

docs.title: Stage 7 — Modding toolkit and Interceptor Remastered
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0. Status: planned. The tools that make mods easy, and the proof that a mod can extend a campaign.

Design: mod structure, Interceptor Remastered.

docs.title: Work items
docs.text:
# Item Module 7.1 --check --campaign <id> grown into the full validator: every definition, reference, condition and text key; JSON report; per-addon checks check 7.2 Recipes: the generated-asset system (cache keyed by recipe, version and input hash; --build-recipes; build on first use with progress) recipe (new) 7.3 upscale generator: de-dither, edge-directed ×2 steps, sharpen, alpha re-application, wrap-aware borders recipe::upscale 7.4 mesh-patch generator: inset, extrude, bevel, cut along UV lines, subdivide, relief from texture, LOD copy; input mesh check recipe::meshpatch 7.5 recolour and composite generators recipe 7.6 Viewer: patch hot-reload and before/after comparison; model-set state browser app::viewer 7.7 interceptor-remastered: parent = interceptor; ×4 textures and ×2 images; the enhanced X-1A Lightning II mesh patch packs/interceptor-remastered 7.8 default: balance pass, complete encyclopaedia packs/default 7.9 Modding guide finished: tutorials from "change one number" through "an addon" and "a campaign that extends another" to "a new campaign", built on the default campaign docs
