  defend_station:
    name: "@mission.defend_station.name"
    briefing: "@mission.defend_station.brief"
    order: 1
    starfield_seed: 101
    player: {class: choose}
    roles:
      station: {class: guard_station, ai: idle, protect: true, at: {distance: 1.2km, bearing: [0, -8]}}
      wing: {class: comet, ai: wingman, count: 2, at: {distance: 0m, spread: 80m}}
      raiders:
        class: [scout_saucer, raider_saucer]          # each member picks one at random
        count: {per_level: [[2, 3], [3, 4], [4, 5], [5, 6]]}
        at: {distance: 6km, from: station, bearing: random}
      robots:                                          # a late arrival
        class: robot_sentinel
        count: 2
        arrive: "time > 75s and alive(station)"
        at: {distance: 5km, from: station, bearing: random}
    waves:
      - {role: raiders, when: "count(raiders) < 2 and time > 30s", count: [1, 2]}
    objectives:
      lose: destroyed(station) or not player_alive
      win: destroyed_all(raiders) and destroyed_all(robots)
    optional:
      station_untouched: hull(station) > 90%
      no_losses: count(wing) == 2
    outcomes:
      win: [score(station_defended), salvage, "relation(guard, +5)"]
      lose: [lose(guard_station), score(station_lost)]
      retreat: [score(station_abandoned)]
    chatter:
      - {when: "time > 3s", line: "@chat.saucers_inbound"}
      - {when: arrived(robots), line: "@chat.robots"}
      - {when: "hull(station) < 50%", line: "@chat.station_hurt"}
    debrief:
      win: "@debrief.defend_station.win"
      lose: "@debrief.defend_station.lose"
      retreat: "@debrief.retreat"

docs.title: The mission
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Shown in the launcher (usually a @key). briefing text empty The briefing, shown in the launcher. order number 100 Sort key among the launcher's missions. starfield_seed number 1 The star field; also seeds the mission's random choices (counts, classes, random bearings). sun 3 numbers default sun Direction towards the sun. player {class, position} choose, [0, 0, 0] The player's ship class (or choose: picked in the launcher, --ship) and start position. roles mapping name: role — Groups of craft (below). player is reserved. waves list none Reinforcements (below). objectives {win, lose, draw} none Conditions that end the battle (below). optional mapping name: condition none Optional objectives, latched when first met and reported on the debrief. timer {after, then} none A time limit: after after (a time) the result is then (win, lose, draw or retreat; default draw). outcomes mapping result: list of actions none What each result does (below). Results: win, lose, draw, retreat. chatter list of {when, line} none Radio lines, each said once when its condition first holds. debrief mapping result: text none The debrief text for each result (usually @keys).

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning class id, or list of ids required A class, or a list: each member picks one at random (repeat an id to weight it). count number or [min, max] 1 How many; a range is rolled when the role spawns. Per level: {per_level: [[2, 3], [3, 4], …]}. faction id the class's Side. ai enemy, wingman, target, idle enemy How it is flown (wingmen follow the player). behaviour id the class's A behaviour to fly instead of the class's. protect bool false An objective the player must keep alive (marked on the HUD, skipped by nearest-enemy targeting). state id none Model-set state, e.g. a construction stage (build_60): no modules or point defence. hull fraction 100 % Starting hull. destroyed_systems ids none Systems that start destroyed. speed number 0 Starting speed, m/s. at arrival the player's start Where it enters (below). arrive condition at the start When it enters: the role spawns the first time this holds.

Arrival (at:).

Key Type Default Meaning distance distance 0 m From the reference point. bearing [yaw, pitch] degrees, or random random Direction from the reference point; [0, 0] is straight ahead of the player's start (−Z), positive yaw to the left. Random picks any yaw and a pitch within ±20°. from role name the player's start Place it relative to a role (the centre of its surviving members). spread distance 120 m How far apart the members are, side by side across the line of sight.

Members face the player's start. A role placed from another role that has not arrived (or has no survivors) is placed relative to the player's start.

docs.title: Waves
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning role role name required The role that gets more craft (they count as members of that role). when condition required Fires once, the first time it holds. count number or [min, max] the role's count How many. at arrival the role's at Where.

docs.title: Objectives and results
docs.text:
Every tick after the simulation step the mission checks, in this order:

  1. the player jumped out (hyperspace) → retreat;
  2. lose → lose (checked first, so a simultaneous win and loss is a loss);
  3. win → win;
  4. draw → draw;
  5. the timer → its then.

The battle then freezes behind the debrief: the result, the debrief text, kills, losses and time, the optional objectives (met or not), and the outcome's campaign actions. Enter (pad A) flies the mission again; Esc or L returns to the launcher.

docs.title: The battle context
docs.text:
Mission conditions (objectives, optional, waves.when, arrive, chatter.when) use the condition language with the battle context. The mission's role names are constants, so alive(raiders) is checked when the rules load — a misspelled role is an error with file and line. Difficulty level names are constants too.

Query Type Meaning time number Seconds since the battle began. alive(role) true/false Any of the role is still in the battle. count(role) number How many of the role are still in the battle. destroyed_all(role) true/false Every member that has arrived was destroyed. destroyed(role) true/false The same as destroyed_all (reads better for one object). destroyed_any(role) true/false At least one member was destroyed. retreated_all(role) true/false Every member has left the battle by hyperspace, none destroyed. captured_any(role) true/false A member was captured (towed out by a tractor beam). hull(role) number The lowest hull fraction among the role's survivors (1 if none). near(role, d) true/false A member is within distance d of the player: near(attackers, 2km). arrived(role) true/false The role has entered the battle. player_alive true/false The player's ship is still in the battle. player_hull number The player's hull fraction. player_retreated true/false The player jumped out. difficulty number The difficulty level's index (compare with level names). random(p) true/false True with probability p per check (seeded).

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
outcomes lists actions, written as calls: score(station_defended), relation(guard, +5), or a bare name (salvage). They are checked when the rules load — an unknown action or a wrong argument is an error. Battle actions run in the battle; campaign actions are listed on the debrief now and will be applied by the strategy layer (Stage 4).

Action Arguments Scope Meaning message(text) text (a @key or words) battle Show a line on the message display. score(name) id campaign Add a mission score entry. money(n) number campaign Add (or take) money. relation(faction, n) id, number campaign Change a faction's relation. salvage — campaign Collect salvage from destroyed enemies. capture — campaign Keep the craft captured by tractor beam. lose(asset) id campaign The player loses an asset (an outpost, a facility). set_flag(name) id campaign Set a campaign flag. cargo_lost — campaign The convoy's cargo never arrives. cargo_captured — campaign The enemy takes the cargo to a supply depot.

Quote an action that contains a comma or a + sign in a YAML flow list: [score(x), "relation(guard, +5)"].

docs.title: The missions shipped
docs.text:
Campaign Missions default defend_station, convoy_ambush, construction_defence, intercept_scouts (missions/missions.yaml; text in text/en/missions.yaml). Construction defence and convoy ambush are the logistics missions; the strategy layer will generate them. interceptor xcom_base_defense, defend_freighter_convoy, deep_space_encounter, attack_alien_outpost, destroy_alien_probe — five of the original's 27 types, with the original's own names, briefings and debriefs by key (@orig.BRIEFING_TYPE_1, @orig.DEBRIEF_XBASE_WIN …, read from the CD); the force compositions are derived (DEV-041). %s in an original briefing is filled by the strategy layer later and shows as written for now.

--soak <mission id> plays a mission without a window and prints its result (soak mission defend_station (ranger, ai): lose after 132 s; <n> kills); see Validating a mod.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Message Cause missions.x: roles.y.class: needed (a class id or a list) A role without class. roles: 'player' is reserved (the player's craft) A role named player. unknown name 'raider' (in a condition) A misspelled role or query; role names are checked. waves[0]: unknown role 'z' / at.from: unknown role 'z' A wave or arrival names a role that does not exist. roles.y.ai: 'x' is not enemy, wingman, target or idle A bad ai. timer.then: 'x' is not win, lose, draw or retreat A bad timer result. outcomes.x: results are win, lose, draw and retreat An unknown result name. outcomes.win: unknown action 'teleport' (known: …) An unknown action, or a wrong argument. chatter[2]: needs line: A chatter entry without its line.

docs.title: Models and textures
docs.text:
Asset Mod format Notes Model Wavefront OBJ + MTL v, vt, vn, f (forms 1, 1/2, 1//3, 1/2/3, negative indices), usemtl, mtllib. Polygons are fan-triangulated, so keep them convex. Groups and objects are ignored. Material MTL newmtl, Kd r g b (flat colour, 0–1), map_Kd file (texture, relative to the .mtl; options before the file name are allowed). Texture PNG or TGA Any size; RGBA honoured. Cockpit art PNG or TGA Any resolution; stretched over the cockpit's design space (640×480 unless design says otherwise). Use alpha for the window. See Cockpits. 3D cockpit OBJ + MTL Metres around the pilot's eye at the origin, +Y up, looking along −Z. Replacement of an original asset OBJ / PNG / WAV at its override path See Overrides and extraction; --extract produces starting files.

The original formats (XMSH meshes, XTXR textures, TGA cockpits) are read straight from the CD behind the same interfaces, so original and mod assets can be mixed freely.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Units: metres. Use model_scale in the ship's rules if your file uses other units.
  • Axes: right-handed, +Y up, the nose pointing along −Z (the engine's convention). Blender's OBJ exporter with "Forward: −Z, Up: Y" produces this.
  • Texture coordinates: standard OBJ (v up); the loader flips them for the engine.
  • Normals: used if present; otherwise each face gets a flat normal.
  • Faces are one-sided. A face is visible only from the side where its corners run counter-clockwise (the OBJ and Blender convention for an outward face); from behind it is culled, exactly like the original models. A surface that must be seen from both sides — a fin, a shield, a sign — needs two faces back to back, one wound each way. If a face vanishes when you orbit it in the model viewer, it is wound the wrong way (Blender: Mesh → Normals → Flip or Recalculate Outside).
  • Decals. To lay a marking over a hull face, put a second face exactly in the same plane, facing the same way, later in the file than the face it covers. The engine detects such overlapping coplanar faces and draws the later one on top (a tiny depth bias), so there is no flicker and no need to lift the decal off the surface. Original models mark their decals with a polygon flag instead (XMSH).
  • Texture coordinates repeat: a UV of 0..4 tiles the texture four times across the face.
  • One LOD per OBJ model in Stage 1 (original models keep their four LODs). Multiple LOD files are planned for Stage 6.
  • Attachment points. A group (or object) named slot_<name> is not drawn: it marks where a station module mounts — at the centre of its faces, facing along its first face's normal. One small square, wound counter-clockwise seen from where the module should point, is enough. Modules are turned so their −Z follows that normal; model a module standing on its base at the origin and extending along −Z. See Stations and modules. Original models' attachment points are their manipulators, addressed by index. OBJ models get one engine glow at the back of their bounding box.
  • Looks. Damage textures, named states, debris pieces and explosions belong to the model set, not the model: see Looks. Debris pieces are modelled in the object's own space so they reassemble it.
  • Collision: craft collide as spheres (bounding radius); stations (kind: station) collide against their triangles, so model the station's real shape.

docs.title: Re-skinning original models
docs.text: A model's textures are looked up by name in every pack's textures/ folder (<name>.png, then <name>.tga, newest pack first) before the original XTXR texture. To re-skin, export your image with the original texture's name — the model viewer lists the models, and --check reports texture names that fail to load.

docs.title: Checking a model
docs.text: Open it straight in the viewer: openinterceptor --model <ship id or mesh name>. In the viewer, W cycles solid / solid + wireframe / wireframe, D cycles the class's looks (intact, damage levels, states, debris pulled apart), [ ] select faces (Shift: ten at a time) and show each face's number, corner count, texture, flags, overlay layer and UVs, I labels every face towards the camera, and O hides overlay-flagged faces.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: Every model of the default campaign — rockets, saucers, the robot sentinel, freighters, stations, rubble, debris pieces and the Guard 3D cockpit — is written by the Python scripts in tools/default_assets/ (models.py, with textures.py for hull paint and its scorched and burnt damage variants — and wrecked for station modules — and sounds.py for synthesised effects). Run python3 tools/default_assets/make_all.py to rebuild them, or make_all.py --check to build twice and prove the output is byte-identical. The scripts use only the Python standard library, seed every random choice, and validate every model before writing it (closed solids wound counter-clockwise from outside, no degenerate faces, within a triangle budget). Look at them to see how a model, its .mtl materials and its textures are written programmatically.

docs.title: The generator's conventions
docs.text: Convention In tools/default_assets/ Debris Each model is cut by planes into its <name>_debris<n>.obj pieces, in the model's own space. Attachment points slot(name, at, normal) adds one small square face in a group slot_<name>, centred on at and wound so its normal is normal; slots are open parts, so the validator checks them for degeneracy only, and debris cutting leaves them out. Station modules Stand on their base at the origin and extend along −Z (the slot's normal), e.g. the Guard ray turret and force-field generator, the Dominion death-ray pod and shield pod. Damage textures <texture>_scorched.png, <texture>_burnt.png; modules also <texture>_wrecked.png for their destroyed state. Instrument placement The Guard cockpit's rectangles and anchors, written to models/guard_cockpit.instruments.yaml.

docs.title: Overrides and extraction
docs.text:
Any original asset can be replaced one file at a time: put a file at the asset's override path inside an active pack, and the engine uses it instead of the CD's version. Everything you do not replace still comes from the CD. The highest-priority pack wins (the last one in load order), so several mods can stack.

Original asset Override path in your pack Format mesh INTTYPEA (any original:NAME model) models/inttypea.obj (+ its .mtl) Wavefront OBJ, metres, +Y up, nose along −Z texture CUBETOP (named by an original model) textures/cubetop.png or .tga any size image CockpitA.dll#12000 (cockpits, HUD art, menus, sprites) images/cockpita/12000.png or .tga any size; alpha = see-through sound Xwinder.wav sounds/xwinder.wav WAV (PCM or ADPCM)

Names are lower-case; the image folder is the DLL's name without .dll. Replacement images are used as they are — the original cockpits' cyan colour key is not applied, so mark see-through areas with PNG alpha.

docs.title: Extracting the originals
docs.text:
You do not need to know the names: the engine converts the whole CD for you, writing every asset at its override path:

openinterceptor --extract ~/Desktop/interceptor-extracted
# extract: 297 models, 799 textures, 3244 images, 792 sounds, 27 reference files; 0 errors

interceptor-extracted/
  README.txt, pack.yaml     (id interceptor-extracted; personal use only)
  models/<name>.obj, .mtl   most detailed LOD; textures referenced as ../textures/<tex>.png
  textures/<name>.png
  images/<dll>/<id>.png     cockpit cyan already turned into transparency
  sounds/<name>.wav         16-bit PCM (sound effects and music loops)
  original-data/            the original INI and text files, for reference (read-only data)

The extracted files are converted copies of copyrighted content from your CD: use them to make your own art, keep them to yourself, and never put them in a mod you share. A shared mod should contain only files you made.

To find which file you want, open the launcher's Asset browser: it lists every texture, image and sound under the same names, and marks the ones a pack already overrides.

docs.title: Walkthrough: repaint the cockpit in HD
docs.text:
The original Lightning II cockpit is 640×480. Here is how to replace it with a modern repaint, without touching any rule.

  1. Extract (once): openinterceptor --extract ~/interceptor-extracted.
  2. Find the image: the Lightning II uses cockpit a, whose rules say image: original:CockpitA.dll#12000. Its extracted copy is ~/interceptor-extracted/images/cockpita/12000.png.
  3. Paint a new version at any resolution with the same 4:3 proportions — for example 2560×1920. Keep the windows transparent (alpha 0) and keep the instruments' screens where they were, scaled up: the instrument rectangles are given in the 640×480 design space, so a 4× repaint lines up automatically.

  4. Make a mod:

    ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/mods/hd-cockpit/
  pack.yaml
  images/cockpita/12000.png      ← your repaint

    id: hd-cockpit
name: HD cockpit
kind: addon
targets: [interceptor]
requires_original: true
format: 2

  5. Check and fly: openinterceptor --check (no errors), then the Asset browser shows CockpitA.dll #12000 [overridden by hd-cockpit], and any flight with the Lightning II uses the new art.

This was verified with a 2560×1920 test repaint: it replaced the original in game and every instrument stayed in place. To compare with the original, add hd-cockpit to packs: {disabled: [...]} in settings.yaml.

A widescreen redesign (16:9 art rather than 4:3) needs new instrument positions too: add a cockpits: {a: …} entry to your mod with design: [1920, 1080] and new instruments rectangles in that space — only the keys you change; the rest is inherited by layering. For a 3D cockpit the in-game layout editor (F12) writes such an addon for you. See Cockpits.

docs.title: Other common overrides
docs.text:
• New ship model: export from Blender as OBJ (metres, +Y up, forward −Z) to models/<original mesh name>.obj — e.g. models/inttypea.obj — and every Lightning II uses it. For a ship of your own, add a ship under ships: instead, with model: models/....
  • Re-skin: textures/<texture name>.png changes that texture on every model using it.
  • Sounds: sounds/xwinder.wav replaces the X-Winder launch sound.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Nothing changed: the file name or folder does not match — compare with the extracted path or the Asset browser label (all lower-case). Is the pack disabled in settings.yaml, or does its targets miss the campaign being played?
  • Black or cyan edges: the image needs real alpha; the cyan key is only applied to the original files.
  • Model faces the wrong way: the engine's forward is −Z; rotate the model 180° before export.

docs.title: Packs
docs.text:
A pack is a folder of content with a pack.yaml manifest. The engine loads the built-in packs (the packs/ folder next to the program, or --packs <dir>), then every mod in the user mods folder (or --mods <dir>). Within a folder, packs are found in folder-name order and then ordered so that every pack comes after the packs it depends on (otherwise keeping that order). Later packs override earlier ones, key by key.

Since Stage 2 not every pack found is loaded: the player plays one campaign, and only the packs that belong with it load — see Mod kinds and the active set.

Default mods folder: macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/mods/, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/mods/ (default ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/mods/), or settings.yaml paths: {mods: …} (Settings).

docs.title: Mod kinds and the active set
docs.text:
Every pack is one of three kinds (kind: in pack.yaml; from src/content/pack.rs):

Kind What it is Extra keys campaign A complete, playable game (default, interceptor). parent — the campaign it extends. addon (the default) Changes to one or more campaigns: a balance mod, a new ship, an HD cockpit. targets — the campaign ids it applies to (["*"] = all; none = all). library Shared content, loaded only when another pack depends on it. —

When campaign C is played, the active set is:

  1. C's parent chain — its parent, that campaign's parent, and so on (root first);
  2. every addon whose targets names a campaign in the chain (or *, or nothing);
  3. every pack any of those depends on (libraries and others), transitively.

Everything else stays out. The active set then loads parents and dependencies first; later packs override earlier ones key by key, so a campaign with parent: interceptor is "the Interceptor campaign plus my changes".

flowchart LR
  subgraph found["Packs found"]
    D["default<br/>campaign"]
    I["interceptor<br/>campaign"]
    R["remaster<br/>campaign, parent: interceptor"]
    A1["hd-cockpits<br/>addon, targets: interceptor"]
    A2["faster-comet<br/>addon, targets: default"]
    L["shared-art<br/>library"]
  end
  A1 -. depends .-> L
  subgraph active["Active set when playing remaster"]
    direction LR
    L2["shared-art"] --> I2["interceptor"] --> R2["remaster"] --> A12["hd-cockpits"]
  end

docs.title: Choosing the campaign
docs.text:
Where How Launcher The header shows Campaign: …; Tab (pad Y) switches to the next campaign and reloads content. settings.yaml game: {campaign: default} — the launcher writes the last choice here. Command line --campaign <id>. None of these interceptor when the player's data makes it available, otherwise default, otherwise the first campaign found.

An unknown or unavailable campaign falls back to that default with a warning. --list lists the campaigns (* marks the loaded one); --check checks every campaign separately, each with its own active set, so an addon must pass with each campaign it targets. If no pack is a campaign at all (a Stage 1 set-up), every pack loads as before.

docs.title: Mod-format version
docs.text:
format: 2 records the mod-format version the pack was written for. A pack with a higher format than the engine reads (pack::FORMAT, currently 2) is refused with a message asking for a newer OpenInterceptor; a missing format means the current one.

Format Since Files 1 Stage 1 INI: pack.ini, rules/*.ini, scenarios/*.ini. No longer read: a folder with only a pack.ini is reported ("pack.ini is the old INI mod format (format 1) …") and skipped. 2 Stage 2 YAML: pack.yaml, rules/*.yaml, campaign/*.yaml, scenarios/*.yaml (Rulesets).

Converting a format-1 mod by hand: section [ship:comet] becomes ships: / comet:, keys become snake_case (MaxSpeed = 620 → max_speed: 620), comma lists become [a, b], yes/no become true/false, Systems.add = ecm becomes systems+: [ecm], and ; comments become #. The built-in packs in packs/ show the result for every section.

docs.title: Switching packs on and off
docs.text:
A pack in the active set loads unless its id is listed in settings.yaml:

packs:
  disabled: [hd-cockpit-test, balance-tweak]

A disabled pack contributes nothing — no rules, no scenarios, no asset overrides — so removing an id from the list restores the mod, and adding it restores the originals. Packs that depend on a disabled pack are skipped too. (XWVM offers the same whole-pack switch in its launcher's Game Content screen; a launcher screen for this is planned for Stage 5.)

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
my-campaign/
  pack.yaml             the manifest (required)
  rules/*.yaml          ships, beams, missiles, objects, factions, cockpits, systems,
                        behaviours, modelsets, debris, effects, flight, power, damage,
                        sounds, audio
                        (all files loaded, in file-name order)
  campaign/*.yaml       campaigns: the campaign ruleset (name, difficulty levels)
  text/<lang>/*.yaml    player-visible strings by key; imports of the original's text
  scenarios/*.yaml      playable arenas (all files loaded)
  models/*.obj, *.mtl   models (any folder works; paths are written in the rules)
  textures/*.png, *.tga textures; also how a pack re-skins a model texture by name
  images/<dll>/<id>.png replacement original images (cockpits, HUD art) — see Overrides
  sounds/*.wav          sounds; sounds/<name>.wav also replaces an original sound

Only pack.yaml is required; every folder is optional. Every rule file may live in any of rules/ or campaign/; the split is a convention.

docs.title: pack.yaml
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/pack.schema.json
id: my-campaign            # letters, digits, - and _ only; must be unique
name: My Campaign
version: "1.0"             # quoted: text, not a number
description: A new war on the frontier
kind: campaign             # campaign | addon (the default) | library
parent: default            # campaigns only: the campaign this one extends
# targets: [default]       # addons only: campaigns it applies to (["*"] = all)
depends: []                # ids that must load first
requires_original: false   # true = needs the player's Interceptor data (--data)
format: 2                  # mod-format version it was written for
Key Default Meaning id — (required) Unique id. name the id Shown on the launcher. version 0 Free text. description empty Free text. kind addon campaign, addon or library (above). Anything else is an error. parent none Campaigns only (an error on other kinds): the campaign this one extends. A missing parent or a parent cycle is an error. targets all Addons only: a list of campaign ids, or ["*"]. format current Mod-format version; newer than the engine's is an error. authors, licence — Informational. depends none Packs that must be installed and load first. A missing dependency is an error; a cycle is an error. requires_original false true skips the pack (with a warning) when no original data is loaded; packs depending on it are skipped too.

docs.title: Built-in packs
docs.text: Pack Needs original data Contents default no Campaign Perils of the Void: the original-free default campaign — 1950s film-serial rocket ships of the Interplanetary Guard against the flying saucers of the Umbral Dominion. Seven factions, six beams and two missiles, playable rockets comet, meteor, thunderbolt flown from the 3D cockpit guard, saucers, a robot sentinel, freighters, stations, systems and power rules, behaviours with four difficulty levels, and the scenarios rocket-vs-saucer, dominion-raid, black-comet-ambush, systems-trial. Models, textures and sounds are generated by tools/default_assets/. Copy this to start a mod — see Make your first mod. interceptor yes Campaign. Rules that inherit the original GameSettings.ini sections, the class → mesh mapping, cockpits, systems and power rules (rules/systems.yaml), the campaign ruleset with the original's five difficulty levels, event sounds, and the test scenarios flight-test, combat-test, gunnery-range, station-tour, systems-trial. No assets: every model, texture, image and sound is an original: reference into the player's CD.

docs.title: Asset references
docs.text:
Rules refer to assets with a reference string:

Written as Means models/scout.obj A file in the pack that wrote the reference. \ is accepted; . and .. are normalised inside the pack (models/../textures/a.png = textures/a.png); a path that would leave the pack, starts with / or contains : is refused. original:INTTYPEA A named resource in the original DLLs; the kind comes from the key (model → an XMSH mesh). original:CockpitA.dll#12000 Resource 12000 of a specific original DLL (cockpit image). original:GameSettings.ini, original:target lock.wav An original file, found by name anywhere in the data folder (any case).

Textures named inside a model are looked up as textures/<name>.png then .tga in every pack, latest pack first, before falling back to the original XTXR texture of that name. Dropping textures/cubetop.png into a mod therefore re-skins every original model that uses cubetop. The same rule covers every original asset — meshes, cockpit and HUD images, sounds — see Overrides and extraction.

docs.title: Mod file reference
docs.text:
Every key of every mod file type, from the schemas in src/content/files.rs (the same definitions produce the editor JSON Schemas in schemas/ and validate files on load). Types:

Type Written as number 620, 0.5; any number may also be {per_level: [a, b, …]} (difficulty) distance / time / angle / fraction a number with an optional unit: 2.4km, 1.5s, 12deg, 40% (plain = metres, seconds, degrees, 0..1) text free text; quote it if it contains : or starts with a symbol. Player-visible names and descriptions may instead be a text key, "@ship.comet.name", resolved from text/<language>/ (Text and translation) id a lower-case id (blaster) ids a list of ids: [a, b] asset an asset reference: models/comet.obj, original:INTTYPEA, none where allowed bool true / false RGB three numbers 0..1: [1.0, 0.55, 0.15] condition a condition in quotes

Every definition (an entry under ships, beams, behaviours, … and the global sections) may also use inherit, delete: true, variants: {<level>: {…}} and list edits <key>+: […] / <key>-: […] (Rulesets). "—" in the Default column means no default (the key is optional unless marked required).

docs.title: pack.yaml
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning id id required Unique id: a-z, 0-9, - and _. name text the id Shown in the launcher. version text 0 The pack's own version (quote it: "1.0"). description text empty One or two sentences for the launcher. kind campaign / addon / library addon See Packs. parent id — Campaigns: the campaign this one extends. targets ids all Addons: campaigns it applies to (["*"] = all; quote the *). depends ids none Packs that must load first. requires_original bool false true when the pack reads the player's Interceptor CD. format number current (2) Mod-format version the pack was written for. authors, licence text — Informational.

docs.title: Rules files (rules/*.yaml, campaign/*.yaml)
docs.text: Top-level sections: factions, beams, missiles, ships, objects, systems, cockpits, behaviours, modelsets, debris, effects, missions (definitions by id), and flight, power, damage, sounds, audio, campaign (global).

docs.title: factions
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. color RGB 0.8, 0.8, 0.8 Radar and HUD colour. hostile ids none Faction ids this faction fights. Hostility is symmetric: either side declaring it is enough.

docs.title: beams
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. damage number 25 Damage per hit. energy_cost number 10 Energy per shot. rate_of_fire number 2 Shots per second per mount. speed number 2000 Bolt speed, m/s. range distance 3000 m Reach (2.4km, 2400m; a plain number is metres). An original Range inherited from GameSettings.ini is read as kilometres (DEV-008). color RGB 1, 0.2, 0.2 Bolt colour. sound asset none Firing sound.

docs.title: missiles
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. speed number 1000 Top speed, m/s. duration time 10 s Flight time before self-destruct. impact_damage number 300 Damage on a direct hit. proximity_damage number 200 Damage from the proximity fuse. proximity_radius distance 25 m Proximity fuse radius. turn_rate number 90 Degrees per second while homing. lock_time time 2 s Seconds in the lock cone to lock on. color RGB 1, 0.8, 0.4 Trail colour. sound asset none Launch sound (or cue:<Name>). explosion id a 25 m, 0.8 s fireball Effect of its detonation (effects); its size is in metres, and its sound, if any, plays instead of the explosion event sound. guidance homing, dumbfire, sidestep, parallax, cloaked_wait, cluster, doppelganger homing How it steers (Missiles and mines). damage normal, bypass_shields, enveloping normal How the warhead's damage lands. decoys number 2 parallax: decoys released at launch. cluster {missile, count, at} count 6, at 600 m cluster: the submunition missile id, how many, and how close to the target it splits. trigger_range distance 800 m cloaked_wait: it wakes when a hostile comes this close.

docs.title: ships and objects
docs.text:
The same keys; objects defaults to kind: station.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. description text empty One line for the launcher and viewer. kind fighter, freighter, capital, drone, station, probe, mine, debris fighter / station What sort of object it is. station and mine never move. faction id neutral Owning faction; must exist. model_set id — The look: a model set. Either model_set or model is required. model asset — Shorthand for a model set of its own: models/x.obj or original:MESH. model_scale number 1 Model units to metres. playable bool false The player may fly it (offered in the launcher). cockpit id none Cockpit for the player's view; without one, glass instruments. hit_points number 100 Hull points. armor number 0 Armour points, absorbed after shields. shields number 0 Shield points per facing (fore and aft). shield_recharge number 5 Shield points per second per facing at full charge. max_speed number 400 Top speed, m/s (0 for static kinds). acceleration number 150 m/s². roll_rate, pitch_rate, yaw_rate number 120, 70, 70 Degrees per second (pitch and yaw at rest). angular_damp number 3 0 tight … 10 loose. lock_speed number 1000 Speed at which pitch and yaw rates fall to zero, m/s. vct bool false Fitted with vector control thrusters (adds the vct system). energy number 500 Beam capacitor. energy_recharge number 40 Capacitor recharge per second at full beam charge. beams ids none One beam id per mount: [laser, laser]. missiles mapping id: number none Racks: {xwinder: 5, sidestep: 4}. systems ids by kind Fitted systems, replacing the default list; usually edit it instead: systems+: [ecm], systems-: [vct]. repair_rate number damage.repair_rate Hit points per second the crew repairs. capturable bool true for fighter, drone, probe, debris Can be captured with a tractor beam when disabled. behaviour id none (armed AI ships fly builtin_attack) AI behaviour (Behaviours). turret_arc angle 0 Beams can aim this far off the nose (turrets). debris list of assets none Shorthand (with model): wreckage models. With a model set, its debris set is used instead. modules list of {slot, class} none Stations: modules mounted at the model's attachment points — slot is an OBJ slot_<name> group's name or an original mesh's attachment index (quoted: '0') (Stations and modules). shield_generator bool false Modules: while one survives, its station's shields work. point_defence {range, rate, chance, energy} none Guns that shoot down hostile missiles (and decoys): range (distance, default 800 m), rate (shots per second, default 3), chance (fraction a shot destroys the missile, default 35 %), energy (per shot, default 4). probe {sensors, jamming} none Probes: sensors (distance) — its side's radar sees every contact this close to the probe; jamming (distance) — hostile ships this close have half radar range and lock missiles at half speed. engine_color RGB 0.5, 0.7, 1.0 Engine glow colour.

docs.title: systems
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning kind engines, manoeuvring, sensors, shields, hyperdrive, vct, tractor, cloak, ecm, damage_control the id The built-in effect. Required when the id is not a kind name. name text built-in name Display name. hit_points number per kind Damage before it stops working. power number per kind Power steps while switched on. range distance per kind Tractor hold range, ECM radius, cloak detection range. strength number per kind Tractor pull m/s²; ECM and cloak: chance per second, in %, that a homing missile loses its target. repair_rate number per kind (4 for damage control) Damage control: repair speed multiplier.

Built-in values per kind: Rulesets.

docs.title: cockpits
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning image asset or none — 2D cockpit art, stretched over the design space. design 2 numbers 640, 480 Width and height of the instrument coordinate space. model asset none 3D cockpit model around the pilot's eye. model_offset 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Metres from the eye: x right, y up, −z ahead. model_scale number 1 Model units to metres. instruments mapping name: [x, y, w, h] — Instrument rectangles in the design space. Names: message, radar_front, radar_rear, mfd, gauge1–gauge4, power, systems. anchors mapping name: {at, normal, size} none 3D cockpits: instruments drawn in perspective on the model's surface (below).

An anchor:

Key Type Meaning at 3 numbers Centre of the instrument on the cockpit model, metres. normal 3 numbers The surface's outward normal. size 2 numbers Width and height on the surface, metres.

A cockpit needs an image, a model, or both. Guide: Cockpits.

docs.title: behaviours
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning start id the first state The first state. states mapping state name: state required (at least one) Manoeuvre and parameters (below). systems {cloak, ecm, shields_first, beams_first} none When the pilot uses its ship's systems: each a condition, checked with the transitions. cloak / ecm on while it holds, off otherwise (if fitted); shields_first moves power to shields one step at a time while it holds; else beams_first moves it to beams. prefer mapping selector: weight none Target preferences: a hostile matching a selector counts as if weight times nearer when the AI picks a new target (several matches multiply). Selectors: player, a ship kind (fighter, freighter, station, …), class:<id>, faction:<id>; weights above 0. transitions list of {from, to, when} none Tried in order; the first whose from matches and whose condition holds wins. from is a state name or "*" (any, the default); when is a condition. skill {aim, reaction} aim 0.5, reaction 0.7 s aim: fraction, 0 wild … 1 perfect; reaction: time between looks at the target.

A state:

Key Type Default Meaning do idle, circle, patrol, attack, evade, retreat, turret, tow, mine required The manoeuvre. range distance 2000 m Attack: open fire inside it (and inside 95 % of the first beam's reach); patrol: radius around the spawn point; turret: reach; tow: search radius (at least 5 km); mine: trigger distance. fire_cone angle 5° Fire when the aim point is within this angle of the nose. burst time 1.5 s Seconds of firing. pause time 1 s Seconds holding fire between bursts. duration time 3 s Evade: how long. speed fraction 100 % Fraction of top speed. missiles time 10 s Seconds between missile launches (0 = none). jump bool false Retreat: start the hyperdrive.

docs.title: modelsets
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning intact asset required The normal model (all its LODs). scale number 1 Model units to metres. textures mapping texture name: asset none Swaps always applied. damage list of {below, textures} none Damage levels: while the hull is below below (a fraction), its swaps apply; cumulative, the worst level wins. states mapping state: {model, debris, textures} none Named conditions: construction stages (build_25 …), destroyed (a mounted module's wreck). model replaces the intact mesh in that state; debris is the debris set used when destroyed in that state; textures swaps. debris id none Debris set thrown when destroyed. destroyed_effect id explosion Effect of its explosion.

Texture names match a model's textures by file name without folder or extension, case-insensitively. Guide: Looks.

docs.title: debris
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning pieces list of assets none Piece models, in the object's own model space. pick [min, max] all pieces How many pieces are thrown, chosen at random. speed [min, max] 20, 60 Outward speed, m/s. spin [min, max] 30, 120 Tumble, degrees per second. life time 15 s How long the pieces last. chunks {models, count, speed} none Generic rubble: models, how many, [min, max] m/s (default 40, 120).

docs.title: effects
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning size number 2.5 Fireball size: × the object's radius (a missile's explosion: metres). duration time 1.6 s How long it lasts. color RGB 1, 0.6, 0.25 Fireball colour. shockwave bool false An expanding ring of light. sound text none Played with the effect: an event name from sounds: (big_explosion) or an asset. Without one, destructions play the explosion / big_explosion event sounds and missile blasts explosion.

docs.title: flight
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning model newtonian / assisted newtonian Flight model (Simulation). arena_radius distance 60 km Ships are halted at this distance from the centre (0 = none). boost number 150 Afterburner speed bonus, m/s. cost number 50 Afterburner energy per second. lock_angle angle 10° Missile lock cone half-angle. radar_range distance 6000 m Mobile contacts beyond it are hidden from the radar. hyperspace_time time 10 s Hyperdrive countdown (doubled while the hyperdrive is damaged). radar_colors map see below Radar blip and target-marker colours by relation to the player: friendly (own faction, default green), hostile (either side hostile, red), neutral (yellow), objective (objects with protect: true, cyan). Each is [r, g, b], 0..1.

docs.title: power
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning beam_recharge list of numbers 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 Per level A, B, …: fraction of the ship's energy_recharge. 1 to 26 levels. shield_recharge list of numbers 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 Per level: fraction of the ship's shield_recharge. As many levels as beam_recharge. budget number 6 Power steps shared by both settings (level index, A = 0) and switched-on systems. start_beam number 3 Starting beam level (0 = A). start_shield number 3 Starting shield level. balance_shift fraction 50 % With shields balanced forward the fore shield holds 1 + shift times its normal capacity and the aft 1 − shift.

docs.title: damage
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning system_share fraction 100 % Share of the damage past the armour that also strikes one system. destroy_below fraction 50 % A system this far below zero hit points is destroyed for the battle. repair_rate number 2 Default crew repair rate, hit points per second.

docs.title: sounds
docs.text: <event>: <asset> for the events the engine plays: explosion, big_explosion, shield_hit, hull_hit, lock, missile_launch, afterburner, target, denied, collision, system_damage, tractor, cloak, ecm, hyperspace, point_defence (a point-defence shot). Beam and missile sounds are set on each weapon. Any sound reference may be cue:<Name>, a cue of the audio cue table.

docs.title: audio
docs.text: Key Type Meaning cue_table asset A table of named sound cues: original:<file>/<section> — the original's soundfx.ini (original:soundfx.ini/InterceptorSounds). Each entry Name = "path\file.wav" makes cue:Name mean original:file.wav. Cue names ignore case; an unknown cue, or a missing table, is a load error.

docs.title: campaign
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text — Campaign title. difficulty ids none Difficulty level ids, easiest first. default_difficulty id the middle level The level a new game starts at.

docs.title: missions
docs.text:
Battles defined by roles, waves, objectives and outcomes. Rules folders: rules/, campaign/ and missions/ (the convention for missions). Full reference, battle-context queries and actions: Missions.

Key Type Default Meaning name, briefing text the id, empty Launcher title and briefing (@keys). order number 100 Launcher sort key. starfield_seed number 1 Star field and the mission's random choices. sun 3 numbers — Direction towards the sun. player {class, position} choose, origin The player's craft and start. roles mapping name: {class, count, faction, ai, behaviour, protect, state, hull, destroyed_systems, speed, at, arrive} — Groups of craft. class: an id or a list (random per member); count: n or [min, max]; at: {distance, bearing, from, spread}; arrive: a condition. waves list of {role, when, count, at} none Reinforcements, each once. objectives {win, lose, draw} none Conditions; lose is checked before win. optional mapping name: condition none Latched optional objectives. timer {after, then} none Time limit and its result. outcomes mapping result: actions none Results win, lose, draw, retreat. chatter list of {when, line} none Radio lines. debrief mapping result: text none Debrief texts.

The schema type either (Ty::Either) lets a key take one of two forms: count: 3 or count: [2, 4]; bearing: [10, 5] or bearing: random; class: comet or class: [a, b].

docs.title: Text files (text/<language>/*.yaml)
docs.text:
Key Type Meaning text mapping key: text The strings by key; "@<key>" in rules and scenarios refers to them. imports list of {file, prefix} The original's language files, read from the player's CD at run time: file (original:LangFile1.txt), prefix (default orig) — every original key K becomes <prefix>.K.

Schema: schemas/text.schema.json. Guide: Text and translation.

docs.title: Scenario files (scenarios/*.yaml)
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning id id required Unique scenario id; used by --scenario. A later pack's scenario with the same id replaces it. title text the id Launcher title. description text empty Launcher description. order number 100 Launcher sort key (lower first; ties by title). player text choose A ship id, or choose to let the launcher pick among playable classes. player_position 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Metres. player_rotation 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Yaw, pitch, roll in degrees (positive yaw turns left). sun 3 numbers −0.4, 0.5, −0.8 Direction towards the sun. starfield_seed number 1 Background stars; the same seed gives the same sky. music asset none Read but not played yet (Stage 5). objects mapping name: object none Placed objects (below). nav mapping name: {position: [x, y, z]} none Navigation points (engine extension, DEV-002).

An object:

Key Type Default Meaning class id required Ship or object id. faction id the class's Overrides the side. position 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Metres; −z is ahead of the player's start. rotation 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Yaw, pitch, roll in degrees. ai wingman, enemy, idle, target idle How it is flown. leader id none Wingmen: the object to follow (player = the player). offset 3 numbers −60, 0, 30 Wingmen: formation slot relative to the leader (x right, y up, +z behind). speed number 0 Starting speed, m/s (also sets the throttle). destroyed_systems ids none Systems (kinds or ids) that start destroyed; [engines, manoeuvring] starts it disabled. protect bool false An objective the player must keep alive: drawn in the objective radar colour with a ring, labelled PROTECT on the target brackets and the MFD, and never picked by "nearest enemy" (R) for the player or the player's wingmen. T can still select it. hull fraction 100 % Starting hull. behaviour id the class's Behaviour to fly instead of the class's. state id none Model-set state to show it in (a construction stage such as build_60); an object placed in a state gets no modules or point defence.

docs.title: Rulesets and layering
docs.text:
Rules are YAML files in a pack's rules/ folder (and the campaign ruleset in campaign/). Every active pack's files are merged in load order into one ruleset; this page explains the format and how files from several packs combine. Every key of every section is listed in the Mod file reference; behaviours have their own page, Behaviours and conditions.

Since mod format 2 (Stage 2), mod files are YAML; the INI files of format 1 are no longer read. The player's original GameSettings.ini is still INI: a definition reuses one of its sections with inherit: original:GameSettings.ini/<section> (below).

docs.title: The YAML subset
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../schemas/rules.schema.json
# comments start with #
ships:                          # a section: definitions by id
  comet:                        # a definition (ids: lower case a-z, 0-9, _ and -)
    name: Comet                 # plain text
    description: "Quick: and nimble"   # quote text that contains ': ' or starts with a symbol
    beams: [blaster, blaster]   # a list on one line …
    debris:                     # … or one item per line
      - models/comet_debris1.obj
      - models/comet_debris2.obj
    missiles: {seeker: 4}       # a mapping on one line
    playable: true              # true / false
flight:                         # a global section (no ids)
  model: newtonian

The reader (src/formats/yaml.rs) accepts a strict subset of YAML and rejects the rest with an error naming the line: no tabs for indentation, no anchors (&a) or aliases (*a), no tags (!!str), one document per file, no complex keys (?), and plain text may not continue over several lines (use quotes, or | / > block text). Why a subset: DEV-030.

Values with units. Distances, times, angles and fractions may carry a unit; a plain number is in the base unit.

Kind of value Units Base unit Examples distance m, km metres 2.4km, 350m, 350 time s, min, h seconds 1.5s, 2min angle deg degrees 12deg, 12 fraction % 0..1 40%, 0.4

Checked on load. Every file is validated against its schema: an unknown key (with a "did you mean" suggestion), a wrong type or a bad value is reported with file, line and key path, for example rules/ships.yaml:12: ships.comet.max_sped: unknown key (did you mean 'max_speed'?). --check lists every such problem; see Validating a mod.

Editor support. A first line # yaml-language-server: $schema=<path>/rules.schema.json points editors that use the YAML language server (for example VS Code's YAML extension) at the JSON Schema of the file type, which gives completion, hover documentation and live checking. The schemas are in the repository's schemas/ folder (pack.schema.json, rules.schema.json, scenario.schema.json; the built-in packs point there with a relative path); openinterceptor --write-schemas <dir> writes them anywhere, for a mod kept elsewhere. The gate fails if the committed schemas differ from the engine's.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Section Defines ships Craft by id (default kind: fighter). objects Stations and other large objects by id (default kind: station, never moves). beams Beam weapons. missiles Missiles and torpedoes. factions Sides. cockpits Cockpit art and/or 3D model, design space, instrument positions and anchors. systems Damageable ship systems and special equipment (Stage 2). behaviours AI state machines (Behaviours and conditions). modelsets Looks: model, damage-level texture swaps, states, debris set, explosion (Looks). debris Debris sets: pieces, how many, speed, spin, life, rubble. effects Explosions and other effects. flight Global flight and sensor settings. power Global power-sharing rules: beam and shield charge levels, budget. damage Global rules for damage to systems and repair. sounds Event sounds (assets, or cue:<Name> from the cue table). audio The sound cue table (cue_table: original:soundfx.ini/<section>). campaign The campaign ruleset: name and difficulty levels (usually in campaign/campaign.yaml).

Any other top-level key is an error ("unknown key").

docs.title: Layering, inherit, delete and list edits
docs.text:
1. All packs' rules files are merged in load order. A later pack's definition with the same id merges key by key into the earlier one: mappings merge recursively, other values and lists are replaced, new keys and definitions are added. Global sections merge the same way.
  2. An empty value removes a key that an earlier pack set (cockpit: with nothing after it), so the engine default applies again.
  3. inherit: <id> copies another definition of the same section first, and the definition's own keys override; inherit: ships.<id> names another section. inherit: original:GameSettings.ini/Ship_IntType1 copies a section of the player's original INI file: original keys become field names by spelling (HitPoints → hit_points, RateOfFire → rate_of_fire), except Side → faction, a beam's Range (kilometres in the original, DEV-008) → range in km, and LockAngleDegrees → lock_angle. Chains are allowed; a cycle (or a chain deeper than 16) is an error.
  4. delete: true removes a definition (a mod removing a ship it does not want).
  5. List edits: <key>+: [items] appends to the inherited or earlier list and <key>-: [items] removes items from it, so a mod need not restate the list (systems+: [ecm], beams-: [laser_cannon]). For systems the edits apply to the default list when no pack sets one.

A definition with an error is skipped and reported; everything else still loads.

# mods/lightning-variants/rules/ships.yaml
ships:
  lightning:
    max_speed: 700            # every other key keeps the interceptor pack's value
    systems+: [tractor]       # fit a tractor beam as well
  lightning_mk3:
    inherit: lightning        # a variant: the Lightning plus changes
    name: Lightning Mk III
    hit_points: 140

docs.title: Difficulty levels
docs.text:
A campaign lists its difficulty levels, easiest first, in its campaign ruleset:

# packs/default/campaign/campaign.yaml
campaign:
  name: Perils of the Void
  difficulty: [cadet, ranger, captain, space_ace]
  default_difficulty: ranger

The game is played at one level, chosen on the launcher (D, pad X), with --difficulty <id>, or remembered in settings.yaml (game: {difficulty: …}); without a choice it is default_difficulty, else the middle level. Two things vary by level:

  • Per-level values: any number may be written {per_level: [80, 100, 120, 150]} — one entry per level, in order; a shorter list repeats its last entry.
  • Variants: a definition's variants: mapping gives, per level id, only the keys that differ at that level; they are merged over the definition when that level is played.
behaviours:
  saucer_scout:
    states:
      engage: {do: attack, burst: {per_level: [0.6s, 0.8s, 1s, 1.2s]}}
    skill: {aim: 0.4, reaction: 0.9s}
    variants:
      cadet: {skill: {aim: 0.2, reaction: 1.4s}}

Conditions can also test the level: difficulty >= captain (Behaviours). The levels of the two campaigns:

Campaign Levels (default bold) Source interceptor beginner, experienced, veteran, genius, superhuman the original's five levels (GameSettings.ini has a section per level; verified). What each level changes in the original beyond those sections is unknown. default cadet, ranger, captain, space_ace this project

An unknown level in variants, --difficulty or settings.yaml is reported (the middle level is then used). Both campaigns give their enemies behaviours with skill and fire discipline per level (rules/behaviours.yaml); the interceptor values are derived from the strategy guide's descriptions of each class and tuned in the testbed, since the original's AI is hard-coded.

docs.title: Ship systems and equipment
docs.text:
Every ship carries a list of systems. Each one has hit points and can be damaged; the switchable ones (tractor, cloak, ECM) draw power while on. What a system does is fixed by its kind (engine code); everything a modder tunes is data, so a mod can define any number of systems of one kind (ecm, advanced_ecm) with different numbers. Keys: reference.

Kind Effect Built-in hit_points / power / range / strength engines Thrust and afterburner scale with its efficiency. 100 / 0 / 0 / 0 manoeuvring (or maneuvering) Turn rates scale with its efficiency. 100 / 0 / 0 / 0 sensors Target lock builds at its efficiency's speed. 60 / 0 / 0 / 0 shields Shield recharge and the fore/aft transfer scale with it. 50 / 0 / 0 / 0 hyperdrive Leaving the battle (H); a damaged drive takes twice as long. 100 / 0 / 0 / 0 vct Vector-control slides. 150 / 0 / 0 / 0 tractor Holds and drags the target; beams cannot fire while it is on. 250 / 2 / 250 m / 60 cloak Hidden from enemy sensors beyond range; firing drops it. 100 / 3 / 400 m / 25 ecm Incoming missiles within range may lose their lock; halves enemy lock speed. 100 / 1 / 250 m / 10 damage_control Multiplies repair speed by repair_rate (default 4). 150 / 0 / 0 / 0

A kind that no pack defines under systems: uses its built-in definition. Built-in hit points follow the original equipment table (verified: EngineType1 100, SensorTargetingSystem1 60, ShieldType1 50, VectorControlThrusters 150, TractorBeam 250, ShipDamageControlComputer 150); ranges, strengths and power steps are engine estimates (derived; the ECM values echo ECMPodType1).

Without a systems key a class gets what any craft of its kind obviously contains: engines and manoeuvring (unless it is a static kind), sensors, shields (if shields > 0), and hyperdrive for fighters, freighters and capital ships. Special equipment is added with a list edit; vct: true (the Stage 1 key) still fits vector-control thrusters:

ships:
  meteor:
    systems+: [ecm, damage_control, tractor]
systems:
  advanced_ecm:                 # a second ECM with longer reach
    kind: ecm
    name: Advanced ECM pod
    range: 500m
    strength: 25

docs.title: How systems behave in flight
docs.text:
Condition When Efficiency OK above half its hit points 1 Damaged half its hit points or less 0.5 Inoperative hit points reached 0 — stays off until repaired back to 25 % 0 Destroyed hit points below −destroy_below × hit_points; for the rest of the battle 0
  • Damage that gets past the shields and armour also strikes one working system at random (times damage.system_share). A knocked-out switchable system switches off; a knocked-out hyperdrive aborts a countdown.
  • The crew repairs one system at a time, worst first, at the class's repair_rate; a working damage control computer multiplies it (by less when it is itself damaged).
  • A ship whose engines and manoeuvring are both out is disabled: it drifts, and if its class is capturable it can be towed away as a prize.

docs.title: Power and damage rules
docs.text:
Each ship has a beam charge and a shield charge setting, both chosen from the same list of levels (the original's A–E). The two settings plus every switched-on system may not use more than budget steps together: raising one setting can force the other down, and switching on a cloak needs free steps. Damage to systems and repair follow the damage section. Keys: reference.

power:
  beam_recharge: [0, 0.32, 0.45, 0.68, 1]    # fraction of the ship's energy_recharge per level
  shield_recharge: [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 1]
  budget: 6
  start_beam: 3                               # D
  start_shield: 2                             # C
  balance_shift: 50%
damage:
  system_share: 100%
  destroy_below: 50%
  repair_rate: 2

The interceptor campaign restates the original BeamRechargeRate (0, 7, 10, 15, 22) and ShieldRechargeRate (0, 1, 2, 3, 5) tables as fractions of their top level (verified from GameSettings.ini); its budget, start levels and system power steps are engine values (derived — the original data does not say how many levels may be high at once, see DEV-024).

docs.title: Example: a small balance addon
docs.text:
# mods/faster-lightning/pack.yaml
id: faster-lightning
kind: addon
targets: [interceptor]
requires_original: true
format: 2

# mods/faster-lightning/rules/ships.yaml
ships:
  lightning:
    max_speed: 700          # every other key keeps the interceptor pack's value

docs.title: Sounds and the cue table
docs.text:
sounds: maps the engine's event names to sounds; beams and missiles name their own sound. Any of these may be an asset (sounds/blaster.wav, original:Xwinder.wav) or a cue, cue:<Name>, looked up in a cue table — the original game's soundfx.ini, which names every sound effect:

audio:
  cue_table: original:soundfx.ini/InterceptorSounds
sounds:
  explosion: cue:SmallExplode
  hyperspace: cue:WarpOut
beams:
  laser_cannon: {sound: cue:Beam1}

Each table entry's file name becomes an original: reference (sounds are found on the CD by name). Cue names ignore case; an unknown cue or a missing table is a load error naming the key. The interceptor pack uses the original's cue names throughout (Stage 2 item 2.12); a mod can replace any cue's sound by a file at its override path (Overrides).

docs.title: Scenarios and missions
docs.text: A scenario is a playable arena in a pack's scenarios/*.yaml. The testbed's live test environments are scenarios; Stage 3 missions extend the same format with objectives and scripts. A later pack's scenario with the same id replaces the earlier one. Every key, with type and default: Mod file reference › scenario files (from src/content/files.rs, read by src/content/scenario.rs).

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Key Meaning id Unique id (required); used by --scenario. title, description, order Launcher title, text and sort key (lower first). player A ship class id, or choose (default) to let the launcher pick among playable classes. player_position, player_rotation Metres; yaw, pitch, roll in degrees (positive yaw turns left). sun Direction towards the sun. starfield_seed The same seed always gives the same sky. music Read but not played yet (Stage 5). objects Placed objects by name (below). nav Navigation points by name: {position: [x, y, z]} (an engine extension, DEV-002). N cycles them; the selected one shows on the MFD Nav page and as a blue diamond on screen.

docs.title: Objects
docs.text: Key Meaning class Ship or object class id (required). faction Override the side. position, rotation Metres (the player starts facing −Z, so negative Z is "ahead"); yaw, pitch, roll in degrees. ai wingman (formation on leader), enemy (flies its behaviour), target (slow circles, never fires), idle (default, does nothing). The player is set with player:, not on an object. leader Another object's name, or player. offset Formation slot relative to the leader, in the leader's frame (x right, y up, +z behind); default [-60, 0, 30]. speed Initial speed, m/s (also sets the throttle). destroyed_systems System kinds or ids that start destroyed. [engines, manoeuvring] starts the ship disabled — a capture target. protect true marks an objective to protect: shown in the objective colour with a radar ring and a PROTECT label, and skipped by nearest-enemy targeting. Use it on a capture target so it is not shot by accident. hull Starting hull fraction (40% or 0.4). behaviour A behaviour id to fly instead of the class's (Behaviours) — an ambush, a guard that only patrols. state Show the object in a model-set state, e.g. a construction stage (state: build_60); such an object has no modules or point defence (Looks).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Using the default campaign's classes:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../schemas/scenario.schema.json
id: ambush
title: Ambush at the station
player: comet
starfield_seed: 4
objects:
  station:
    class: guard_station
    position: [0, 0, -2000]
  wing: {class: comet, ai: wingman, leader: player, offset: [50, 0, 30]}
  s1:
    class: scout_saucer
    ai: enemy
    position: [600, 200, -4000]
    speed: 300
  patrol:                       # a saucer that only circles until you come close
    class: scout_saucer
    ai: enemy
    behaviour: lurker           # defined in this mod's rules/behaviours.yaml
    position: [-800, 0, -3000]
  wreck:                        # a crippled saucer to tow home with the tractor ray
    class: raider_saucer
    position: [0, 0, -900]
    destroyed_systems: [engines, manoeuvring]
    hull: 50%
nav:
  station: {position: [0, 0, -2000]}

# rules/behaviours.yaml of the same mod
behaviours:
  lurker:
    start: wait
    states:
      wait: {do: patrol, range: 400m, speed: 30%}
      strike: {do: attack, range: 1.5km}
    transitions:
      - {from: wait, to: strike, when: "threats(2km) > 0 or hit_recently(1s)"}

--check spawns every scenario (with every playable ship when player: choose) and reports unknown classes, factions, leaders or behaviours.

docs.title: Scripting (design)
docs.text:
Behaviour and logic are designed in Behaviours and scripting:

  • Tier 1 (Stages 2–3): behaviours as state machines, missions and events as definitions, and a small built-in condition and action language — enough for both shipped campaigns. Implemented in Stage 2: behaviours and the condition language in the object context — see Behaviours and conditions. Actions, and the mission and event contexts, come with Stage 3.
  • Tier 2 (decided at the start of Stage 3): optional scripts called through hooks, with Lua 5.4 via mlua recommended, subject to the dependency policy.

docs.title: Stations and modules
docs.text:
A station can carry modules — turrets, shield generators, hangars, pods — each a separate object with its own hit points, weapons and behaviour, mounted at an attachment point of the station's model. Modules can be shot off one by one; destroying a station destroys its modules with it. Implemented in Stage 2 (item 2.11; src/sim/mod.rs, src/formats/obj.rs).

objects:
  dominion_outpost:
    model_set: dominion_outpost
    hit_points: 6000
    shields: 1200
    modules:
      - {slot: pod1, class: dominion_turret_pod}      # OBJ group slot_pod1
      - {slot: pod2, class: dominion_turret_pod}
      - {slot: shield1, class: dominion_shield_pod}
  dominion_turret_pod:
    name: Death-ray pod
    model_set: dominion_turret_pod
    hit_points: 280
    beams: [death_ray]
    turret_arc: 180            # its beams swivel up to 180° off its nose
    behaviour: station_turret  # a behaviour with do: turret
  dominion_shield_pod:
    name: Shield pod
    model_set: dominion_shield_pod
    hit_points: 450
    shield_generator: true     # while one survives, the hub's shields work

docs.title: Attachment points
docs.text:
Model Attachment points slot: written as Mod model (OBJ) Every group or object named slot_<name> (g slot_turret1). Its faces are not drawn; the slot sits at the centre of its faces and faces along its first face's normal (counter-clockwise winding seen from outside, as for any face). One small square per slot is enough. the name after slot_: turret1 Original mesh (XMSH) The mesh's manipulators (attachment points in its first LOD). They have no names. their index: '0', '1', … (quoted)

A module is turned so that its −Z axis (its front) follows the slot's normal, pointing out of the hull: model a module standing on its base at the origin and extending along −Z. A slot name or index that the model does not have is an error when the scenario spawns.

In the default-campaign generator (tools/default_assets/models.py) a slot is made with slot(name, at, normal): one small square face in a slot_<name> group, centred on at and wound so its normal is normal. Slots are left out of debris cutting and of the solid-model checks. The Guard station has slot_turret1–slot_turret6 and slot_shield1–slot_shield2; the Dominion outpost slot_pod1–slot_pod6 and slot_shield1. The module models (Guard ray turret, force-field generator, death-ray pod, shield pod) stand on their bases and extend along −Z, with debris pieces and scorched, burnt and wrecked textures.

docs.title: In battle
docs.text:
• Spawning. When a station is placed, each modules entry spawns its class at its slot, with the station's faction, named <station>.<n>. A module class with a behaviour fights (a turret behaviour aims its swivelling beams within turret_arc); one without sits idle. Modules may carry modules of their own (up to five levels deep).
  • Unfinished stations. A station placed with state: (a construction stage) spawns no modules and fires no point defence.
  • Following. Every tick each module is placed back on its hub's attachment point, so it moves and turns with the station.
  • Shield generators. A station with shield_generator modules keeps its shields only while at least one of them survives; when the last one goes, its shields drop to zero and stay down ("STATION SHIELDS DOWN").
  • Cascade. When the hub is destroyed, all its modules are destroyed with it (each with its own explosion and debris).
  • Wrecks. A destroyed module whose model set has a destroyed state stays on the station as a wreck drawn in that state (Looks); the wreck goes with the station.

docs.title: The two campaigns
docs.text:
Campaign Station Modules default Guard station six ray turrets, two force-field generators default Dominion outpost six death-ray pods, a shield pod interceptor X-COM base (XBASE7, 33 attachment points) beam-defence turrets, shield generators, a hangar interceptor Alien base (AL-BASE01, 28 attachment points) plasma gun pods, shield pods

The interceptor modules' hit points come from the original module sections (M_XCOM*, M_ALIEN* in GameSettings.ini, verified); their meshes are the original turret and pod meshes; which attachment point holds which module is derived (the original builds bases from the strategy layer, Stage 4) — see DEV-035.

Testbed arenas: outpost-strike (default) and base-assault (interceptor) — knock out the shield modules to bring the hub's shields down, silence the guns, then destroy the hub.

docs.title: Mines
docs.text:
A kind: mine object flies the mine manoeuvre: it waits and, when a hostile comes within the state's range, detonates its first missile rack as the warhead. The blast reaches four times the warhead's proximity_radius (at least 100 m), deals the warhead's proximity_damage falling off linearly with distance, spread over both shield facings, and destroys the mine.

missiles:
  mine_warhead: {guidance: dumbfire, speed: 0, impact_damage: 0, proximity_damage: 250, proximity_radius: 40m}
objects:
  space_mine:
    kind: mine
    model_set: robot_sentinel
    hit_points: 30
    missiles: {mine_warhead: 1}
    behaviour: space_mine
behaviours:
  space_mine:
    states:
      wait: {do: mine, range: {per_level: [100m, 120m, 140m, 160m]}}

The default campaign's dominion-raid scenario lays Dominion space mines.

docs.title: Probes
docs.text:
An object with kind: probe and a probe: entry changes what the sides can see:

objects:
  sky_eye_probe:
    kind: probe
    faction: guard
    model_set: sky_eye_probe
    hit_points: 50
    probe: {sensors: 8km}       # the Guard's radar sees every contact within 8 km of it
  jammer_buoy:
    kind: probe
    faction: dominion
    model_set: jammer_buoy
    hit_points: 80
    probe: {jamming: 2.5km}     # hostile ships within 2.5 km: half radar range, half lock speed
  • Sensors. A side's radar shows every contact within any of its own probes' sensors range, however far from the ship looking.
  • Jamming. A ship within a hostile probe's jamming radius has half its radar range and locks missiles at half speed (on top of a target's ECM).
  • Cloaks still win. Since this change the radar also hides cloaked ships of other factions beyond their cloak's range — probes do not reveal them.
  • Stations and mines (objects that never move) always show on radar.

Probes are ordinary objects: they can be shot (they have hit points and a look) and placed in scenarios. The interceptor probes use the original SENSPROB and ECMPROB meshes (verified names); their battle effects and numbers are derived, because the original launches probes from the strategy map (DEV-039). The default campaign has the Guard's Sky-Eye sensor probe and the Dominion jamming buoy. Testbed arena: probe-net (both campaigns).

docs.title: Text and translation
docs.text:
Player-visible strings are named by text key in the rules and scenarios, and the strings themselves live in text/<language>/*.yaml in any pack. A translation, a rename or a re-voiced campaign is then an addon with only the keys it changes. Stage 2 item 2.1 (src/content/text.rs, src/formats/langfile.rs).

# rules/ships.yaml
ships:
  comet:
    name: "@ship.comet.name"
    description: "@ship.comet.desc"

# text/en/ships.yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../../schemas/text.schema.json
text:
  ship.comet.name: "Comet"
  ship.comet.desc: "Light interceptor rocket: quick, nimble and lightly armed."

docs.title: How keys resolve
docs.text:
• A value that starts with @ is a key; anything else is used as written, so a small mod can skip text files entirely.
  • Keys work in the names of ships, objects, beams, missiles, factions and systems, ship and object descriptions, and scenario titles and descriptions. They are resolved when the content loads.
  • Packs load in order and a later pack's key replaces an earlier one's.
  • The game reads each pack's text/<language>/ folder for the chosen language, falling back to text/en/ for a pack that has no folder for it.
  • A missing key shows as the key itself and is a --check error. --check also counts the strings loaded ("… texts").

The language is chosen with --language <code> (the folder name: en, de, fr …) or settings.yaml game: {language: …}; the default is en. Editors check text files against schemas/text.schema.json.

docs.title: The original's text, by reference
docs.text:
The interceptor pack does not copy any of the original game's text. Its text/en/original.yaml imports the original language file from the player's CD at run time:

imports:
  - {file: "original:LangFile1.txt", prefix: orig}

Every string of LangFile1.txt (3 645 on the reference CD) becomes available as @orig.<KEY> — for example @orig.S_XCOM. The original format is plain text, one string per line: a key, whitespace, then the text between the first and last double quote; ~ is a line break and lines starting with / are comments (original formats).

docs.title: A translation addon
docs.text:
# mods/default-de/pack.yaml
id: default-de
name: Perils of the Void — Deutsch
kind: addon
targets: [default]
format: 2

# mods/default-de/text/de/ships.yaml
text:
  ship.comet.name: "Komet"
  ship.comet.desc: "Leichte Abfangrakete: schnell, wendig und leicht bewaffnet."

Run with --language de: translated keys come from the addon, every other key falls back to the default campaign's English. To rename a ship without translating, put the key in the addon's text/en/ instead.

The default campaign keeps all its player-visible names and descriptions in text/en/ (factions, objects, scenarios, ships, systems, weapons).

docs.title: Validating a mod
docs.text:
openinterceptor --check --mods ~/my-mods            # original-free mods
openinterceptor --check --mods ~/my-mods --data /path/to/interceptor-cd
openinterceptor --list  --mods ~/my-mods            # what loaded: packs, playable ships, scenarios

--check loads everything without opening a window and reports:

  • every file that is not valid YAML or does not match its schema, with file, line and key path: rules/ships.yaml:12: ships.comet.max_sped: unknown key (did you mean 'max_speed'?), scenarios/t.yaml:2: unbalanced …, a wrong type or unit (range: 2.4kn → "unknown unit 'kn' … (use m, km)");
  • every rules definition that failed (ships.x: unknown beam 'y', bad inherit, unknown faction or kind, missing model, cockpit without image or model, a behaviour whose condition does not check, an unknown difficulty level in variants);
  • every ship model, debris model and texture that does not load, and unknown cockpit ids;
  • every cockpit image and every referenced sound that does not load;
  • every scenario that cannot spawn (with each playable ship for player: choose), including unknown object behaviours;
  • with original data, every original mesh and texture that does not decode.

It ends with a summary line and exits with status 1 if there were errors, so it can run in a script or CI. Warnings (such as a pack skipped for lack of original data) do not fail it.

The repository's own gate (scripts/check.sh) runs --check --no-original on every build, so the default campaign — the template for mods — always validates. --check checks every campaign separately, each with its own active set of packs (its parent chain, the addons that target it and their dependencies), so an addon is validated with each campaign it applies to; --check --campaign <id> checks just one.

Validation happens at the difficulty level being loaded (the default unless --difficulty is given), so a typo inside one level's variants entry is reported whichever level is played. For balance across levels, --soak <scenario> --difficulty <level> plays a battle without a window and reports the player's fate.

In your editor. Point each file at its JSON Schema (# yaml-language-server: $schema=…, see Rulesets) and most of these mistakes are underlined as you type.

docs.title: Missiles and mines
docs.text:
Every missile class chooses how it steers (guidance) and how its warhead's damage lands (damage). Both are fixed engine behaviours (src/sim/guidance.rs); everything else — speeds, turn rates, damage, decoy counts, split distances — is data. Stage 2 item 2.10. Every key: Mod file reference › missiles.

missiles:
  cluster_rocket:
    name: Cluster rocket
    guidance: cluster          # splits into six seekers near the target
    cluster: {missile: seeker, count: 6, at: 700m}
    impact_damage: 120
    proximity_damage: 50
  decoy_rocket:
    guidance: parallax         # two flares that draw enemy rockets
    decoys: 2
  permeator:
    damage: bypass_shields     # straight to armour and hull

docs.title: Guidance
docs.text:
guidance: Behaviour homing (default) Turns towards its locked target at turn_rate. dumbfire Never steers. sidestep Its own thrusters: turns twice as hard inside 600 m of the target and weaves, so it is hard to dodge. parallax Homing; at launch releases decoys (default 2) that enemy missiles may chase instead of the launcher. cloaked_wait Dropped behind the launcher; drifts to a stop and waits, hidden, until a hostile comes within trigger_range (default 800 m), then strikes. cluster Homing; near the target (cluster.at, default 600 m — or when half its fuel is spent) it splits into cluster.count (default 6) submunitions of cluster.missile, which carry on to the target. doppelganger Launches a decoy copy of the launcher's ship: a short-lived, fragile double that enemy ships and missiles may chase instead.

Decoys. A decoy is a harmless missile flying away from its launcher. An enemy missile homing on the launcher, within 2.5 km of one of its decoys, may become lured (80 % chance per second) and from then on chases the nearest decoy; when the decoys are gone it returns to its target.

Every missile still detonates on impact, on a near miss (the proximity fuse: inside proximity_radius and moving away) or when its fuel (duration) runs out. Its blast is the explosion effect it names (Looks) — size in metres, with the effect's sound — or a 25 m, 0.8 s fireball.

docs.title: Damage modes
