docs.title: The original game, system by system
docs.text:
Status: analysis, 2026-11-10. What X-COM: Interceptor does, how it decides it, and where the data lives — the requirements the mod format must meet. Facts are marked V verified (seen in the CD data), D derived (inferred from data, strings or a source), U unknown.

Sources.

  • [CD]: the player's CD. Files used:
    • GameSettings.ini (259 sections)
    • Think.ini
    • MPSettings.INI and NetSettings.ini
    • soundfx.ini
    • Text/LangFile1.txt, with 3,782 keyed strings
    • Text/starcorp1.txt, Names1.txt, news1.txt and short1.txt
    • Animations/mfdanim.mps
    • the Loops/*.wtl music tables
    • strings and constants in Interceptor.exe
  • [G]: X-COM Interceptor Official Strategies & Secrets (Sybex, 1998), the designer-written strategy guide.
  • [UR] UFOpaedia: Research, Background and Hypernews pages.
  • [F]: a GameFAQs walkthrough.

Nothing here reproduces original text or art; names and numbers are cited as facts.

docs.title: Summary: data versus code
docs.text:
The original keeps numbers in data and rules in code.

In data (V) Hard-coded in the executable (V/D) Prices, build times, maintenance, hit points, weapon and missile stats, hull handling, research sizes and prerequisites, module stats and size classes, rank thresholds, salvage chances, sensor tables, mission score values, alien budget priorities, Doomsday defence counts, all text, names, news, sound cue table Star map generation; every mission's composition, waves and objectives; all AI (strategic, financial, tactical, Doomsday, "fluff" encounters, 32 agent classes); the campaign arc (messages, components, final mission); research yields (what a topic unlocks: all Yield keys are 0); the meaning of each score index; funding and evaluation formulas; report and news triggers; the debris table; module meshes and textures; star and planet visuals; limits (85 systems, 20 bases (8 in the UI), 33 modules per base, 8 players)

Consequence: the interceptor mod must express everything in the right-hand column as data. That column is therefore the hard part of the format, and each row has a section below.

docs.title: Campaign arc
docs.text: Element Rule Src Start 1 Jan 2067. X-COM: 1 base, 3 corporate outpost systems nearby, 3 Lightning II, 5 pilots, cargo of 5 Sensor Probes and 10 X-Winders. Aliens: 2 bases, 6 outposts, at least 1 parsec away G (D) Starting base Cargo, Communications, Hangar, 2 laser turrets, Personnel, Probe Launcher, Standard Downlink, Standard Sensor G Story gate chain Alien Message 1 (not before 1 Feb; chance per combat 7/7/5/5/4% by difficulty, or automatic later) → aliens ship Structural Components → Message 2 (≥1 Mar; needs Msg 1 + a captured Structural Component + Wraith examined) → Message 3 (≥1 May; + Spectre examined; Weapon Components start) → Message 4 (≥1 Jul; + Phantasm examined + Weapon Component; Drive Components start) → Message 5 (≥1 Oct; + Drive Component; gateway map) G (D) Doomsday components Built one type at a time. Totals per difficulty: 25/25/25/20/18 components, split Structural/Weapon/Drive (e.g. Beginner 8/8/9, Superhuman 7/6/5). Convoys pass near X-COM space with probability 65→45%. On the three easiest levels, a fully shipped Structural or Weapon type you never captured is granted. All Drive Components delivered = loss G (D) Final preparation Alien Hull Alloys (Super Avenger), Message 5, Dimension Jump Drive, Nova Bomb researched; gateway (a black hole) found by probes; "Summon MacArthur" (arrives in about 1 week) G Final mission I Outside the black hole vs a large fleet. Fail if the MacArthur dies or no Nova-armed Super Avenger survives G, CD strings FINAL1_MACDEAD, FINAL_NOVASGONE Final mission II Inside the "pocket universe": 7 squadrons, a base, maybe mines; Doomsday weapon untargetable; ships rearmed (repaired on low levels). Total victory: Nova Bomb delivered and you return to within 1 km of the MacArthur; partial victory: bomb delivered, you are lost G Defeat Doomsday completed (DD_TOOLATE), last base destroyed (S_LASTBASEDEAD), final mission failed CD V, G Warnings DD_WARNING1..3; MacArthur prompts MAC_PROMPT1..7 CD V

docs.title: Strategy map
docs.text: Element Rule Src Generation Procedural each campaign (universe.cpp); no map file. Star names from a pool of 100. Limits: 85 systems, 2D grid of 60000 units CD V Stars d100 spectral class: red giant 1–2, blue giant 3–6, black hole 7–10, white dwarf 11–13, blue 14–24, white 25–35, yellow 36–70, orange 71–85, red dwarf 86–100. At least one black hole (the gateway). Black holes hidden; probes lost in them G Bodies 0–5 satellites in 5 orbit slots; asteroid fields mostly inner; planet size small/medium/large/huge; mineral richness low/medium/high by spectral class G Locations DEEPSPACE{x,y}, SYSTEM{id,x,y,orbit}, BASE, OUTPOST, OPP{outpost,opp}, DOOM_PORTAL, POCKET, FLIGHTPLAN CD V Travel Free hyperjumps on the 2D map (no lanes). Range limited by engine endurance: 24/36/48 h. Ships stranded without fuel are lost. Ambush chance grows with distance from home G Time Real time, 6 speeds, auto-pause on events; weekly reports (WEEKLY1..40); monthly evaluation G, CD Sensors Rings around bases (long), ships, outposts, probes. Sensor Probe 0.75 ly, 4–6 weeks; Hunter Probe roams, 3–4 weeks. Destroyed base sensor → about 0.25 ly G Orders in flight Need a Communications module at the squadron's base G

docs.title: Factions and relations
docs.text: Party Mechanics Src X-COM The player — Aliens Full strategic opponent with the same rules plus cheats (rough knowledge of X-COM's start, off-the-shelf equipment, outposts always rebuilt). Five races, lore only G, CD Corporations 87 names; each outpost system's corporation sets a funding share 0–95%, moved monthly by evaluation; at 0% it leaves for good. Only source of money, supplies, manufacturing, recruits. Corporate fighters guard outposts; escorts can be hired (10% of an order) G, CD Kabron pirates Hostile; one base. Either destroy the base ($1M) or defend it from aliens; both end organised piracy G Cult of Sirius Rogue freighter side mission G Arms dealer Secret buyer of everything sold; resells to aliens; one bust mission G GSC Research body; science stations; provides the MacArthur G

docs.title: Economy
docs.text: Element Rule Src Treasury Starting 5.0/4.75/4.5/3.75/3.0 M by difficulty (CD StartingTreasury values V) CD, G Outpost yield Kilotons/month by richness × planet size (200–1300; asteroid OPP 800–1600) × ExchangeRate (250→150 $/kt by difficulty) × 0.75 X-COM share × funding % CD, G (D) Evaluation Monthly per system: (X-COM activity here + overall/10) − (alien activity here + overall/5) → funding change bands (±1…±20%) G (D) New outposts Sum of evaluations → number of d10 rolls (none/one/two/three); +1 per won Recon mission G (D) Expenses Module maintenance; hull upkeep 12k/18k/22k; pilot salaries (formula from stats and rank); recruitment fees CD, G Buying Items with ProdTime=0 bought outright; else manufactured by outpost technicians (10 + 10 per OPP) on one global queue with priorities 10/25/50/100% G Delivery One freighter per outpost, 100 CSU; a lost freighter loses its cargo G Selling To the arms dealer; interceptors and Nova items never resold; ships sell at 0.8 × (hull + parts) G Storage Cargo module 1000 CSU; full storage blocks orders and jettisons loot G Score MissionScores S0–S99 (−5000…+4500); index meanings hard-coded; ratings Phenomenal … Dismal by monthly total CD V, G

docs.title: Research
docs.text: Element Rule Src Topics 71 R_* sections; tech ids 0–73 (3 placeholders), 74–100 alien ships and installations, 127 = special. Level 0–3, FileSize 8–75 (k TQ), Prereq1..3 CD V Process Research happens on Earth; each base downloads one topic through up to 3 downlinks (30/35/40 TQ/h); switching loses progress; jammer probes pause a downlink G Discovery Prerequisites; salvage (per-item survival chance by difficulty, *Goodies); capture of disabled ships (Wraith, Spectre, Phantasm mandatory); alien messages CD, G Yields What each topic unlocks is hard-coded (the Yield keys are all 0); the guide's tree gives it CD V, G Text short1.txt: per topic a found name, a researched name and a description CD V

docs.title: Bases and modules
docs.text: Element Rule Src Limits 8 bases (UI); 33 attachment points: 15 small, 12 medium, 3 large (hangars), 3 special (downlinks); per base 1 shield, 1 sensor, 1 comms, 3 hangars, 3 downlinks, 10 weapons G, CD New base Within 1.5 ly of an existing base; cost (1.5M + standard modules) × 0.75; build time = slowest module + 1 week; dismantle refunds 50% G Modules 68 M_* sections (35 X-COM, 33 alien): Cost, ProdTime (days), SizeClass, Maintenance, HitPoints, tech requirements, Rounds for missile defence CD V Effects Hangar 3 ships, Personnel 5 pilots, Medical heals ×2, Training raises stats, Cargo 1000 CSU, Comms, Probe Launcher, Downlinks, Shields 2000/3000/4000, Sensors (range, which weapons the base fields), ECM 1/2 km, Damage Control ×2 repair, Tractor, beam and missile defence G Destruction Hangar destroyed → ships inside lost; Personnel/Medical → occupants die; Cargo → contents lost G Visuals Generic module mesh retextured per type with normal / construction / destroyed textures; alien pods normal / -b CD V

docs.title: Ships, equipment and pilots
docs.text: Element Rule Src Hulls 20 Ship_* sections (player, freighters, 6 alien types, drone, pirate, corporate, Patton): handling, mounts (MaxBeamWeapons, MaxMissileWeapons, SpecialSystemMounts), hit points, cost, upkeep CD V Slots Beam and missile hardpoints; one armour, engine, sensor, shield slot; special systems; missiles need a launcher G Equipment 23 sections: armour ×3, shields ×4, engines ×3 (power 75/175/300, endurance), ECM ×2, sensors ×3 (lock range, time, cone; which missiles), cloak, jump drive, damage control, tractor, VCT, 3 probes CD V, G Power 100 points shared between engine, beam recharge, shield recharge, specials (tractor 33, ECM 25, cloak 50 + 5%/s); capacitor 1000; afterburner 50/s G, CD Stock designs Named configurations; stock price = hull + 0.9 × parts G Pilots 8 stats with generation ranges; rank rolled d100; experience from kills and missions; rank thresholds by difficulty (RankAdvancement* V); training; injury and health; bravery and fleeing; 10 voice sets, MFD talking heads CD, G Missions Up to 5 ships; player picks which to fly; wingman orders G

docs.title: Missions
docs.text: Element Rule Src Types 27 briefing types + 3 Doomsday; 56 debrief outcomes; 12 combat-simulator types; 7 side missions CD V Generation From the strategic simulation: alien squadrons on flight plans meeting X-COM assets, corporate and GSC requests. Squadron sizes Small 1–3 … Huge 10+ G Defensive Deep-space ambush, probe, freighter (win if it jumps out), OPP, outpost, base (corporate fighters and station guns help); refusing costs score G Offensive Intercept, attack probe (later with mines and hidden escorts), freighter convoy (drones from about month 6), mining platform, outpost, base (damage = one pod; destroy = all; hangars grounded about 20 days) G Side missions Hyperwave anomaly (Doomsday freighter), corporate recon (+1 outpost), rogue freighter ($250k), Kabron pirates ($1M base), pirate base rescue, arms dealer, hijacked Nova Bomb; cheat codes confirm discrete triggers G Leaving Hyperspace out with countdown (no salvage) G Outcome Win/draw/lose; salvage roll; capture; score; pilot experience, injury G, CD

docs.title: Alien strategy
docs.text: Element Rule Src Priorities Exploration, expansion, aggression (rises when X-COM is passive or losing) G New bases On several conditions; each brings 2 outposts; a lost last base is replaced G Outposts Monthly roll, more likely later; cap 16 G Offence ladder Attack probe → freighter → OPP → outpost → cripple base → destroy base → decoy-and-strike G Economy 100% of outpost yield; spending Doomsday > ships and bases > research; Think.ini budgets (ResearchDefault, GoodsDefault, DoomsdayDefault, 15-day periods) and per-module priorities CD V, G Tech 3 levels bought with money (≈0.8–4 M); data receptor pods fund up to $20k/week G Gateway defence Think.ini MaxPortalDefenses*, MaxDoomsdayDefenses* per type and difficulty CD V

docs.title: Space objects and models
docs.text: Element Rule Src Class → mesh String table in the exe (21 entries) CD V Debris 28 named sets × up to 5 chunk meshes; generic chunks; alien corpse parts; shokwave CD V Damage No ship damage textures; modules: destroyed texture CD V Effects Three-ring meshes per hull size (1ASH*, 1SH3*, FRSH*…: shield or jump effect, U); explosion sprites CD Liveries DM1–8 A/B/C: multiplayer colours of the three hulls CD V Stations X-COM base (hub + modules), corporate outpost, OPP, alien base (hub + pods; damage zones), alien outpost, alien mining platform, pirate base, arms dealer, science station, Nova station, Doomsday weapon, landing pad CD, G Station HP 11 charts HP1..HP4, SD (parts and a value of unknown meaning) CD V

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: Screen Function Src CSD (star map) Sensor rings; zoom map/system/object; time controls; object info and squadron reports; Launch Probe; Launch Mission (pick ships, destination; Summon MacArthur); event prompts G Bases 3D base view with attachment points; add/dismantle modules; build/dismantle bases; base status (overlays normal/defences/damage) G, CD Research Topics, current download, size, progress, ETA, jammed downlinks G Equip Ship Hardpoint editor; stock designs; Assign Pilots (training, medical, sack) G Equipment & Personnel Purchase/manufacture per base; production queue with priorities and destination; escorts; selling; recruiting G Status Reports Monthly rating and funding, player status, alien activity, outpost data G, CD UFOpedia 9 categories, about 150 entries (DATABANK_* strings) CD V Briefing / debriefing, Hypernews, combat simulator, load/save, configuration, difficulty, multiplayer — CD Comms Wingman orders; MFD talking-head clips (113 Smacker clips in mfdanim.mps); interactive music sets with cruise/threat/battle states CD V

docs.title: Difficulty
docs.text: Five levels: Beginner, Experienced, Veteran, Genius, Superhuman. They change: starting money, exchange rate, alien ship counts and tiers, alien shields, armour, weapons, rate of fire, skill and aggression, cloak-breaks-lock chance (50→30%), alien tech speed, Doomsday size, salvage survival, message chance, convoy visibility, rank thresholds, final-mission repair, auto-granted components (G; CD tables V where noted above).

docs.title: Formats
docs.text:
How each file type on the CD is stored, as worked out for OpenInterceptor. Every field is marked verified, derived or unknown (see the original game). All numbers are little-endian. Offsets are hexadecimal.

Format Where Page State Win32 PE resources Resources/*.dll PE resource container verified XMSH mesh xobjects*.dll XMSH meshes verified (layout), derived (some fields) XTXR texture xobjects*.dll XTXR textures verified TARG / .tga image cockpit, sprite and wrapper DLLs; 3DObjects/ TGA verified XSPT sprite animation xobjects2.dll XSPT partly derived WAV (MS-ADPCM, PCM), AIFF-C SoundFX/, Loops/, CD Audio/ Audio verified (WAV) Smacker video Animations/*.smk Smacker public format INI ProgramFiles/*.ini INI rule files verified Object and ship table strings in Interceptor.exe Object table derived

docs.title: Audio
docs.text:
Files Format Confidence SoundFX/**/*.wav RIFF WAVE, Microsoft ADPCM (format 2), mono, 22,050 Hz verified Loops/*.wav RIFF WAVE, PCM 16-bit stereo, 22,050 Hz verified CD Audio/*.aiff (extracted by the player) AIFF-C (compressed; codec to check) verified container

MS-ADPCM is decoded in-crate (formats::wav): per block, a predictor index and initial delta per channel, two seed samples, then 4-bit nibbles using the seven standard coefficient pairs from the fmt chunk. The decoded PCM is handed to macroquad's audio.

soundfx.ini maps game events to sound files (Stage 2).

docs.text: Plain Windows INI: [Section], Key=Value, ; comments (also after values), tabs as whitespace, some empty values. Section and key names are case-insensitive. verified

docs.title: GameSettings.ini
docs.text:
Section group Content [Beginner] … [Superhuman] Starting money, exchange rate per difficulty Beam weapons ([LaserCannon], …) Side, class, cost, size, range, damage, energy cost, rate of fire, speed (m/s), recharge, tech required Missile launchers and missiles Ammo type, rounds; speed, range, duration, proximity/impact damage Mines Beam, explosive, missile mines R_* Research topics: the tech tree Equipment (ArmorType*, EngineType*, ShieldType*, sensors, ECM, cloak, tractor, VCT, probes) Per item stats M_XCOM*, M_ALIEN* Station modules Ship_* Hulls: mounts, hit points, and for human hulls the flight model (roll/yaw/pitch rate, angular damping, LockSpeed, MaxSpeed) Rank, recharge, detection, sensor lock, afterburner, "goodies" Real-time tables MissionScores, *HP Scores; station hit points

The engine reads this file as data: the Interceptor pack's rules import its sections with inherit: original:GameSettings.ini/<Section> in their YAML rules; original key names become field names by spelling (HitPoints → hit_points; Side → faction) — see Rulesets. Mod files themselves are YAML since mod format 2.

docs.text: Think.ini (alien strategic AI), soundfx.ini (sound table), MPSettings.INI and NetSettings.ini (multiplayer).

docs.title: Language files (LangFile1.txt)
docs.text:
The original's player-visible text is in plain-ASCII language files (verified):

/ a comment line starts with a slash
KEY_NAME        "The text~second line"

A key, whitespace (tabs or spaces), then the text between the first and last double quote on the line; ~ is a line break; anything else is skipped. formats::langfile reads them from the player's CD at run time when a pack's text file imports: them; the strings become @orig.<KEY> text keys and are never copied into a pack (Text and translation).

docs.title: PE resource container
docs.text: The asset DLLs are ordinary 32-bit Windows PE files whose .rsrc section holds the data. Their code is a stub; the engine never runs it. verified

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
1. e_lfanew at 0x3C → PE header; number of sections at +6; optional-header size at +20.
  2. Data directory 2 (resources) gives the .rsrc RVA; the section table maps RVAs to file offsets.
  3. The resource directory is a three-level tree: type → name → language. Each directory has 16 bytes of header, then named + id entries of 8 bytes: a name (high bit set → offset of a UTF-16 length-prefixed string) and an offset (high bit set → subdirectory, else data entry).
  4. A data entry gives the RVA and size of the resource bytes.

Names are stored with surrounding double quotes in these DLLs ("INTTYPEA"); the engine strips them and compares case-insensitively. Language is always 1033 (US English).

docs.title: Resource types used
docs.text:
Type Holds DLLs Count (approx.) XMSH 3D meshes xobjects1, xobjects2 147 + 150 XTXR Textures xobjects1, xobjects2 461 + 338 XSPT Sprite animations (explosions, flak, laser) xobjects2 10 TARG TGA images, numeric IDs Cockpit*, Sprites, Wrappers 170–1,733 per DLL

Each XMSH, XTXR and XSPT resource begins with a 12-byte lowercase name (NUL-padded with 0xCD, the MSVC debug fill) and a 4-byte tag MSH\0, TXR\0 or SPT\0, then a u32 0 and padding to 0x20.

docs.title: In the engine
docs.text: formats::pe parses the tree once per DLL and keeps (type, name) → byte range. The packs VFS exposes each resource as a virtual file, e.g. xmsh/inttypea, so the rest of the engine never knows the data came from a DLL. See Formats layer.

docs.text: Animations/*.smk are RAD Game Tools Smacker files (SMK2/SMK4): the intro, alien transmissions, endings and credits. The Smacker format is publicly documented (palette chunks, Huffman-coded block types, audio tracks). A decoder will be written in-crate in Stage 5; the original SMACKW32.DLL is never used.

docs.title: TGA images and cockpits
docs.text:
TARG resources and the files in 3DObjects/ are standard Truevision TGA. verified

  • Type 2 (uncompressed true-colour), 16 bits per pixel (RGB555, with an attribute bit), 18-byte header, no image ID. Descriptor bit 5 clear: rows bottom-up.
  • Some wrapper screens are type 10 (RLE true-colour).

docs.title: Cockpits
docs.text:
CockpitA.dll, CockpitB.dll and CockpitC.dll each hold a 640×480 cockpit frame (resource IDs 12000, 12200, 12400) and many smaller parts: gauge needles, MFD and radar elements, damage states. One DLL per player hull (derived: the game has exactly three hulls).

The frame uses cyan, RGB555 0x03DF, as its colour key: those pixels are the window onto space. The engine converts the key to transparent alpha at load.

The frame shows (from the art): a message strip across the top, two round scopes (radar), a centre MFD, four small gauges above it, and two lower dials. What each scope shows (fore/aft or range modes) is derived and refined in Stage 1–2.

docs.title: Other images
docs.text: 3DObjects/ holds reticles (five variants), lens-flare elements, sun and star sprites. SpritesDLL.dll holds ~1,700 small sprites; WrappersDLL.dll the full-screen menus.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here

docs.title: XMSH meshes
docs.text: Every 3D object (ships, stations, debris, asteroids, nebula billboards, planets) is an XMSH resource. Coordinates are Direct3D-style (left-handed, Y up); the engine converts to its own right-handed frame at load. Units appear to be metres (a fighter has a bounding radius of about 10). All 297 meshes parse with this layout. Rendering three hulls and a saucer with their original textures confirmed positions, UVs and texture binding.

docs.title: File header
docs.text: Offset Type Field Confidence 0x00 char[12] name, lowercase, NUL then 0xCD fill verified 0x0C char[4] tag MSH\0 verified 0x10 u32 0 verified (always 0) 0x20 f32 bounding-sphere radius verified 0x28 f32[6] bounding box min xyz, max xyz verified 0x40 u32 flags; 1 on hulls with a manipulator, 0 on many others unknown 0x44 i32[4] −1 unknown 0x54 i32[4] offsets of up to 4 LOD blocks, −1 = none verified

docs.title: LOD block
docs.text:
All offsets inside a LOD block are relative to the block's start.

Offset Type Field Confidence +0x00 f32 switch distance: use this LOD while closer than this (last LOD: 1e8) derived +0x04 u32 0 — +0x08 u32 vertex count verified +0x0C u32 vertex offset verified +0x10 u32 edge count (includes unused edge 0) verified +0x14 u32 edge offset verified +0x18 u32 texture-name count verified +0x1C u32 texture-name offset verified +0x20 u32 manipulator count verified +0x24 u32 manipulator offset verified +0x28 u32 BSP root node offset verified

docs.title: Vertex — 32 bytes
docs.text: f32 x, y, z, nx, ny, nz, u, v. Vertices are duplicated where UVs differ. verified

docs.title: Edge — 16 bytes
docs.text:
u32 v0, u32 v1, u32 (0xCDCDCDCD), u32 0. Edges are 1-based: entry 0 is unused filler. verified

Some edges have the same vertex at both ends (zero length): about 3% of polygons (1,014 of 33,012 across the CD) contain one, giving a repeated corner such as 11, 24, 24, 9. They are in the original data, not a decoding error, and are harmless — the fan triangulation turns the repeated corner into a zero-area triangle. verified

docs.title: Texture name — 32 bytes
docs.text: NUL-terminated lowercase name of an XTXR resource, 0xCD fill. verified

docs.title: Manipulator — 64 bytes
docs.text:
f32[12] (a 3×4 transform) then two i32. The original program's strings call these XCGEN_MANIP_OBJECT and "dummy" manipulators: attachment points such as gun mounts or engine positions. derived — the meaning of each one per model is not yet known.

On the X-COM base (XBASE7) the 34 LOD-0 manipulators are module mount points: the first i32 (kind) runs 0–50 and the positions sit on the ring and spine. The modules themselves are separate meshes (XMMOD02, XMMODHUB, XLANDPC1–4, GUNTURRET2, SCICENTER02, …), so a station under construction is the base mesh plus whichever modules are attached. derived

docs.title: BSP node — 64 bytes
docs.text:
Offset Type Field Confidence +0x00 f32[4] splitting plane (normal, distance); zero in a leaf derived +0x10 f32[6] node bounding box verified +0x28 i32 front child offset, −1 = none verified +0x2C i32 back child offset, −1 = none verified +0x30 i32 0 unknown +0x34 i32 polygon count verified +0x38 i32 −1 unknown +0x3C — 0xCD fill —

The node's polygons follow immediately after its 64 bytes.

docs.title: Polygon — 40 + 4·n bytes
docs.text:
Offset Type Field Confidence +0x00 f32[4] face plane (normal, distance) verified +0x10 u32 flags (see below); 0 on most polygons derived +0x14 u32 colour, 0xAARRGGBB-like; used when untextured derived +0x18 u32 / f32 0, or an opacity-like float when 0x80000000 is set derived +0x1C f32 small value (≈0.03–0.05) unknown +0x20 u32 texture index into the LOD's name list verified +0x24 i32 edge count n verified +0x28 i32[n] signed edge references verified

A positive reference e walks edge e from v0 to v1; a negative one walks edge |e| backwards, so the polygon's corner is v0 for positive and v1 for negative references. Polygons are convex fans with 3 to 36 corners (most are triangles and quads).

The corner order is counter-clockwise around the face plane's normal (by the right-hand rule, in file coordinates) for 32,893 of 33,012 polygons; the rest are degenerate. The plane normals point outward (every asteroid face does), so faces are one-sided and the original culled back faces. Thin surfaces seen from both sides — shield rings (1ASHA…3SH3C), the Avenger's fin, ALORBOUT — are modelled as two polygons back to back. verified

Texture coordinates may lie outside 0..1 (the Patton CPAT has 564 such corners, ROID100 172): textures tile (Direct3D's default wrap addressing). verified by rendering.

docs.title: Polygon flags (+0x10)
docs.text:
Bits Meaning Count (LOD 0, whole CD) Confidence 0x20000000 overlay: a decal lying exactly on a larger base polygon in the same plane (station panels, alien hull markings) 32 alone, 53 with 0x80000000 derived 0x80000000 translucent? — always with a float 0..1 at +0x18 (0.33, 0.60, 0.65) 569 alone, 101 with other bits derived 0x00200000, 0x00020000, 0x00008000, low 9 bits (0x115–0x11E on station overlays) not decoded — unknown

Evidence for the overlay bit: of 124 same-facing overlapping coplanar pairs, 72 have the flag on the later polygon and 8 on the earlier one. The original drew polygons in BSP order, so the later polygon painted over the base; a depth-buffered renderer must instead be told which one wins — the engine's overlay layers (see Rendering). The opacity float is read but not used yet.

docs.title: Typical sizes
docs.text: A fighter: four LODs from ~310 to ~140 vertices and ~200 to ~35 polygons. The X-COM base: ~2,450 vertices and ~660 polygons at LOD 0.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• The flag at 0x40, and the undecoded polygon flag bits.
  • Whether 0x80000000 really is translucency, and how the float is applied.
  • Whether the low bits on station overlays (0x115–0x11E) select overlays by construction state; they do not match the base's manipulator kinds.
  • What each manipulator means per model (weapon mounts? engine glow? docking?).
  • The float at +0x1C (≈0.01–0.05).
  • Whether the BSP order is needed for correct transparency.

The model viewer's wireframe and face selection (see Testbed) show each polygon's index, flags, layer and UVs, which helps this research.

docs.title: XSPT sprites
docs.text:
Ten animated sprites in xobjects2.dll: blam, blamo_, boom, flak, kaplo_, laser, pop, pow, puff, wip — explosions, flak bursts, hit flashes.

Offset Type Field Confidence 0x00 char[12] name verified 0x0C char[4] tag SPT\0 verified 0x20 u32, u32 frame width, height derived 0x28 u32, u32 centre (hot spot) x, y derived 0x30 f32 frame duration or scale (0.1, 0.15) unknown 0x34 u32 frame count derived 0x38 u32 1 unknown 0x3C u32[] per-frame data offsets derived … per frame: a small header (size, origin), then 16-bit RGB555 pixel runs unknown

The pixel encoding is a run-length scheme still to be decoded (Stage 2). Until then the engine draws procedural explosions.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here

docs.title: XTXR textures
docs.text:
Palettised textures with 16 shade tables and mipmaps. verified for every size present.

Offset Type Field Confidence 0x00 char[12] name verified 0x0C char[4] tag TXR\0 verified 0x20 u16, u16 width, height (powers of two, 16–256) verified 0x24 u16 0xCDCD — 0x26 u16 0 — 0x28 u16[16][256] 16 palettes of 256 RGB555 colours verified 0x2028 16 bytes unknown unknown 0x2038 u8[] 4 mip levels of 8-bit indices: w×h, w/2×h/2, w/4×h/4, w/8×h/8 verified

Total size = 8,248 + w·h·85/64 bytes.

  • Palette 0 is full brightness; palettes 1–15 are progressively darker (shade tables for the 1998 software renderer). The engine uses palette 0 and lights with the GPU.
  • Rows are stored bottom-up (text on textures reads correctly only after flipping V).
  • Whether an index is transparent (e.g. index 0 or black) is still unknown; no transparent surfaces have been confirmed on hulls.
  • A few 32×32 textures are 15,416 bytes rather than 9,608: 7 KiB more than expected, perhaps animation frames. unknown

docs.title: R-CPN-001 One campaign at a time
docs.text:
Exactly one campaign MUST be active, chosen by --campaign, settings.yaml game.campaign or the launcher; the active set MUST be the campaign, its parent chain, the addons targeting it and their dependencies.

Rationale: A campaign is the unit a modder ships.

  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::pack::the_active_set_follows_the_chosen_campaign; app::launcher::menu_lists_viewer_and_scenarios_and_wraps; MT-2-12
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Packs, Packs, VFS and rules

docs.title: R-CPN-002 Difficulty levels
docs.text:
A campaign MUST define its difficulty levels; the player MUST choose one in the launcher, with --difficulty or in settings.yaml, remembered per campaign; definitions MUST vary by level through variants and {per_level: …} values.

Rationale: Five levels in interceptor, four in default.

docs.text:
The default campaign MUST load, validate and play with no original data present.

Rationale: Modding first: the engine stands alone.

  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: check::the_default_campaign_passes; content::loads_original_free_packs_rules_scenarios_and_models; MT-1-19, MT-2-13
  • Reverse-engineered: yes

docs.title: R-CPN-004 Default campaign content
docs.text:
Perils of the Void MUST provide its fixed six-system map, its craft, stations and weapons, the 11 generated mission types (2 on surfaces), the 12-chapter arc, the Dominion as rival and the logistics of R-STR-012 – R-STR-027.

Rationale: The worked example for modders.

  • Implements: F-CPN-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (in progress: rules, scenarios, 4 missions).
  • See: The default campaign

docs.title: R-CPN-005 Interceptor campaign content
docs.text:
The interceptor campaign MUST express every system of the original from the player's data: the 27 mission types, the simulator types and the final mission's two parts, the 71 research topics, the 68 modules, the Doomsday arc and the alien strategist; values that the original keeps in code MUST be recorded as derived.

Rationale: Compatibility; the primary test case.

  • Implements: F-CPN-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (in progress: 5 of 27 mission types, DEV-041).
  • See: The Interceptor campaign mod, Coverage matrix

docs.title: R-CPN-006 Interceptor Remastered
docs.text:
interceptor-remastered MUST declare parent: interceptor and supply ×4 textures, ×2 images and an enhanced X-1A Lightning II mesh patch, all generated by recipes from the player's data.

Rationale: Proof that a mod extends a campaign.

  • Implements: F-CPN-005, F-MOD-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Interceptor Remastered

docs.title: R-CPN-007 Events and arcs
docs.text:
Events MUST have conditions, chances per check, actions, choices, offers and cooldowns; arcs MUST order steps whose state conditions can read.

Rationale: Story.

  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.

docs.title: R-CPN-008 Rival plans and strategist
docs.text:
A rival MUST pursue plans (stages, budgets, shipments by convoy, visibility, completion, warnings) and be run by a strategist with budgets, aggression, expansion, offence and defence priorities.

Rationale: An opponent with intent.

  • Implements: F-CPN-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-CPN-009 Dynamic relations
docs.text:
Factions MUST have relations governed by relation rules, drift and stances, with effects in battle and on the strategy layer, and events on stance changes.

Rationale: A living setting.

  • Implements: F-CPN-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-CPN-010 Victory, defeat and endings
docs.text:
A campaign MUST define victory and defeat and its endings, including partial victories.

Rationale: A beginning, middle and end.

docs.text:
Screens MUST be laid out in design spaces with skins (nine-slice panels, buttons, fonts, custom panels bound to queries); menus MUST cover options, difficulty, load/save, credits, endings and campaign and mod selection.

The engine MUST play the original's Smacker cut-scenes and talking heads and image-sequence video for mods, and interactive music with states, segments, switches and stingers.

docs.title: R-HUD-004 Anchored 3D-cockpit instruments
docs.text:
Instruments of a 3D cockpit MUST be drawn in perspective at anchors on the dashboard surface, so they stay in their bezels at any window shape.

Rationale: User feedback (plan item 2.21).

  • Implements: F-HUD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::layout::corners_lie_on_the_surface_with_world_up, rays_pick_the_nearest_surface; MT-2-15
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpits (HD and 3D)

docs.title: R-HUD-005 Radar and shield rings
docs.text:
Radars MUST place contacts by angle on front and rear scopes in faction colours; the front scope MUST ring the fore shield and the rear scope the aft shield, green, amber, red, blinking when down.

Rationale: Situational awareness; shield state at a glance (DEV-037).

  • Implements: F-HUD-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::radar_places_contacts_by_angle, hud::draw::shield_rings_go_green_amber_red_then_blink; MT-1-35, MT-2-28, MT-2-30
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

docs.title: R-HUD-006 Gauges, readouts and messages
docs.text:
The HUD MUST show speed, energy, shield and hull gauges, the power settings and system lamps, MFD pages (including Systems) that cycle, and a message line that expires and keeps the newest. Text MUST be fitted to its instrument. Cockpits that do not place the power or systems instruments MUST get fallback panels.

Rationale: The pilot must always know the craft's state.

  • Implements: F-HUD-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::gauges_sweep_and_read_the_ship, power_and_system_readouts, mfd_pages_cycle_and_describe, messages_expire_and_keep_the_newest; hud::draw::lamp_grids_follow_the_panel_shape; hud::glyphs::sizes_snap_down_onto_the_ladder; MT-2-21, MT-2-29
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

docs.title: R-HUD-007 Targeting display
docs.text:
The HUD MUST bracket the target, show a lead marker where shots will meet it, show lock progress and lock, point to an off-screen target, and mark the selected nav point.

Rationale: Gunnery and navigation.

  • Implements: F-HUD-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::ai::lead_point_anticipates_motion; MT-1-10, MT-1-12, MT-1-17
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD, Deviations (DEV-002)

docs.title: R-HUD-008 Cockpit layout editor
docs.text:
F12 in the cockpit view MUST open an editor that drags and resizes 2D instruments, places instruments on a 3D cockpit by ray-picking, and saves the layout as a valid addon.

Rationale: User feedback (plan item 2.22).

  • Implements: F-HUD-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::layout::dragging_and_scaling, saved_layouts_are_valid_rules; MT-2-16, MT-2-17
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpits (HD and 3D)

docs.title: R-HUD-009 Drift display
docs.text:
The speed indicator MUST show forward speed and the sideways (X) and vertical (Y) components of the velocity in the craft's frame; the HUD SHOULD show a flight-path marker where the velocity vector points.

Rationale: User request (F-HUD-006): newtonian flight allows drift the pilot cannot otherwise see.

  • Implements: F-HUD-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item F.1).
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

Open

How the original cockpits' speed gauge shows three values, and the marker's look, are not designed.

docs.title: R-HUD-010 Brightness setting
docs.text:
The player MUST be able to set the picture's brightness in the settings, where 1 means as authored.

Rationale: User request (F-HUD-007).

  • Implements: F-HUD-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item F.3).
  • See: Settings and data discovery

Open

Range and where it is set in game (settings file only, or an options screen).

docs.title: R-HUD-011 Other craft visible at combat ranges
docs.text:
Other craft MUST be visible to the player at combat ranges in every cockpit and view.

Rationale: User request (F-HUD-007): "it is difficult to see other fighters".

  • Implements: F-HUD-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item F.3; a manual test).
  • See: Rendering

Open

The means (lighting, minimum on-screen size, contact markers or outlines) and a measurable criterion are not decided.

docs.title: R-HUD-012 Atmosphere instruments
docs.text:
In an atmosphere the HUD MUST show altitude, vertical speed and a horizon.

Rationale: Flight over terrain.

  • Implements: F-HUD-008
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Stage 3

docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Bootstrap: R-HUD-001 – R-HUD-012 (12 requirements; 8 reverse-engineered from the code)

docs.title: Combat requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for weapons, damage, systems and power, special equipment, targeting, AI pilots, stations and the look of damage.

Features: Combat. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-CMB-001 Beam fire and energy Implemented R-CMB-002 Bolt travel Implemented R-CMB-003 Missile lock Implemented R-CMB-004 Missile guidance and damage modes Implemented R-CMB-005 Mines Implemented R-CMB-006 Layered damage Implemented R-CMB-007 Ship systems and repair Implemented R-CMB-008 Power settings Implemented R-CMB-009 Tractor and capture Implemented R-CMB-010 Cloak Implemented R-CMB-011 ECM Implemented R-CMB-012 Point defence Implemented R-CMB-013 Probes Implemented R-CMB-014 Targeting Implemented R-CMB-015 Wingman orders Implemented R-CMB-016 Behaviours as data Implemented R-CMB-017 AI missile discipline Implemented R-CMB-018 Station modules Implemented R-CMB-019 Model sets and damage looks Implemented R-CMB-020 Debris and explosions Implemented R-CMB-021 Shot physics Planned

docs.title: R-CMB-001 Beam fire and energy
docs.text:
Each beam mount MUST have a cooldown of 1 / rate_of_fire; a group MUST fire only if there is energy for the whole group, otherwise report NoEnergy and hold for 0.5 s; link modes Linked (pairs), Full (all) and Unlinked (one at a time) MUST cycle.

Rationale: The original's gunnery model.

  • Implements: F-CMB-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::beams_fire_cost_energy_respect_cooldown_and_hit, beams_need_energy, link_modes_cycle_and_change_how_many_fire; MT-1-11
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-002 Bolt travel
docs.text:
A bolt MUST live for range / speed, start at its muzzle with its streak never reaching behind the muzzle, and inherit the firing ship's velocity.

Rationale: Shots must look as if they leave the gun.

  • Implements: F-CMB-001, F-CMB-011
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::a_new_bolt_streak_never_reaches_behind_the_muzzle; MT-1-34
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-003 Missile lock
docs.text:
A lock MUST build while the target stays inside flight.lock_angle (10° by default, DEV-013) and within the missile's reach for the missile's lock_time, at a speed scaled by the sensors' efficiency and halved while the target's ECM is on; leaving the cone MUST reset it.

Rationale: The original's missile model.

  • Implements: F-CMB-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::lock_builds_in_the_cone_and_missile_homes_in, lock_is_lost_outside_the_cone_and_dumbfire_works; MT-1-12
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-004 Missile guidance and damage modes
docs.text:
Missiles MUST support the guidance kinds homing, dumbfire, sidestep, parallax decoys, cloaked wait, cluster and doppelganger, and the damage modes normal, bypass shields and enveloping. The proximity fuse MUST fire on a near miss (inside proximity_radius and moving away); a hit inside the target's shape MUST deal impact damage; empty racks MUST be reported and skipped.

Rationale: Every missile of both campaigns.

  • Implements: F-CMB-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::guidance::homing_hits_and_dumbfire_misses_an_offset_target, sidestep_still_arrives, parallax_decoys_lure_enemy_missiles, cloaked_wait_sleeps_until_prey_comes_near, cluster_splits_into_submunitions, doppelganger_launches_a_decoy_ship_that_expires, damage_modes; sim::combat::proximity_fuse_fires_on_a_near_miss, empty_racks_report_and_cycle; MT-2-24
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missiles and mines, Deviations (DEV-010, DEV-036)

docs.title: R-CMB-005 Mines
docs.text:
A mine MUST stay in place and detonate with an area blast when an enemy comes within its trigger range.

Rationale: Original and default-campaign weapons.

  • Implements: F-CMB-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::ai::mines_go_off_when_an_enemy_comes_near; MT-2-24
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missiles and mines

docs.title: R-CMB-006 Layered damage
docs.text:
Damage MUST strike the fore or aft shield (by the side hit), then armour, then hull; hull at zero MUST destroy the ship and make every ship targeting or towing it let go; a shield facing reaching zero MUST say "FORE/AFT SHIELD DOWN".

Rationale: The original's damage model.

  • Implements: F-CMB-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::damage_layers_and_aft_shield; MT-1-13
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-007 Ship systems and repair
docs.text:
Each system MUST have hit points and a condition: full effect above half, half effect at or below half, stopped at zero until repaired back to 25 %, destroyed for the battle below −destroy_below × hit_points. Damage past the armour MUST strike a random system; repair MUST take the worst system first. A ship whose engines and manoeuvring are out MUST drift disabled.

Rationale: The original's system damage; thresholds are engine values (DEV-029).

  • Implements: F-CMB-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::damage_knocks_systems_out_and_repairs_bring_them_back, systems_can_be_destroyed_beyond_repair, disabled_when_engines_and_manoeuvring_are_out; sim::ai::disabled_ships_drift; MT-2-03
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Rulesets

docs.title: R-CMB-008 Power settings
docs.text:
Beam and shield charge settings A–E and switched-on equipment MUST share power.budget steps; raising one setting MUST take from the other when the budget is full; cycling MUST wrap to A; the pilot MUST be able to transfer energy and move shield points fore and aft within caps; recharge MUST follow the settings.

Rationale: The original's power management, as charge settings (DEV-024).

  • Implements: F-CMB-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::raising_takes_power_from_the_other_setting, cycling_wraps_to_a, balance_caps_and_message, shield_balance_moves_points_forward_and_recharge_follows_power, requests_change_power_and_balance; sim::flight::energy_and_shields_recharge_up_to_capacity; MT-2-01, MT-2-02
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-009 Tractor and capture
docs.text:
The tractor MUST need power, a fitting and a disabled target in range; while it is on, beams MUST be off-line; a ship holding a disabled target when it jumps MUST capture it.

Rationale: Original capture of disabled craft.

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::tractor_needs_power_a_fitting_and_a_target_in_range, tractor_holds_a_disabled_target_and_captures_it_on_jump; sim::ai::tugs_tow_disabled_enemies_away; MT-2-04
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-010 Cloak
docs.text:
A cloaked ship MUST vanish from enemy sensors beyond detection range; firing beams or a missile MUST drop the cloak with "CLOAK DROPPED".

Rationale: Original equipment; no invisible attacks (DEV-025).

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::cloaked_ships_vanish_from_enemy_sensors_beyond_range; MT-2-05
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-011 ECM
docs.text:
While ECM is on, incoming missiles MUST lose their target and enemy lock MUST build at half speed.

Rationale: Original equipment.

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::ecm_makes_incoming_missiles_lose_their_target; MT-2-06
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-012 Point defence
docs.text:
A ship with point defence MUST fire at the nearest hostile missile (decoys included) within range when cooled down and with energy, roll chance on the world's seeded generator, and spend energy per shot.

Rationale: Capital ships and stations defend against missiles (values derived, DEV-038).

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::point_defence_shoots_down_hostile_missiles; MT-2-31
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Stations, modules and probes

docs.title: R-CMB-013 Probes
docs.text:
A sensor probe MUST extend its side's radar to 8 km around it; a jamming probe MUST halve hostile radar range and missile-lock speed within 2.5 km; the radar MUST hide cloaked ships.

Rationale: Original probes given battle effects (derived, DEV-039).

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::probes_extend_radar_and_jam_their_enemies; MT-2-32
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Stations, modules and probes

docs.title: R-CMB-014 Targeting
docs.text:
The pilot MUST be able to cycle targets forwards and backwards with wrap-around, select the nearest hostile (ignoring friends and protected objectives) and select the most central ship in the sights.

Rationale: Original targeting keys.

  • Implements: F-CMB-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::targeting::cycles_forwards_and_backwards_with_wraparound, nearest_hostile_ignores_friends, in_sights_picks_the_most_central, nothing_to_target; sim::protected_objectives_are_not_picked_as_the_nearest_enemy; MT-1-10
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-015 Wingman orders
docs.text:
Wingmen MUST hold formation slots and obey: formation (ignore my target), attack my target, fire at will, evasive (10 s), retreat (flee and jump out) and status report, given from a comms menu.

Rationale: Original wingman commands.

  • Implements: F-CMB-007
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::ai::wingman_closes_on_its_slot, orders_switch_wingmen_to_attack, evasive_ends_and_retreat_jumps_out; app::flight::commands_target_and_order_wingmen; MT-1-14, MT-2-08
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-016 Behaviours as data
docs.text:
AI pilots MUST be driven by behaviour definitions: states using the built-in manoeuvres (idle, circle, patrol, attack, evade, retreat, turret, tow, mine), transitions on conditions, skill (aim, reaction), fire discipline, turret arcs, target preferences (prefer) and systems use (cloak, ECM, power). Any definition MUST accept difficulty variants and {per_level: …} values.

Rationale: Modding first; the original's AI is code, so its behaviours are derived (DEV-031, DEV-032).

  • Implements: F-CMB-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::behaviour::parses_states_transitions_and_skill, reports_mistakes, the_builtin_attack_is_valid, target_preferences_parse_and_reject_unknown_selectors; sim::ai::transitions_switch_states_on_conditions, aim_skill_decides_accuracy, turrets_fire_off_the_nose; sim::preferences_pull_the_ai_past_a_nearer_target, sim::ai_pilots_switch_cloak_ecm_and_power_by_condition; MT-2-20, MT-2-27, MT-2-33
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Format: behaviours and scripting, Behaviours and conditions

docs.title: R-CMB-017 AI missile discipline
docs.text:
AI pilots SHOULD launch missiles only when closing on their target, staggered between pilots, each pilot drawing from its own random sequence.

Rationale: Missiles from every enemy at once overwhelmed the player.

  • Implements: F-CMB-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: None recorded.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (architecture)

Open

No unit test names this behaviour; one should be added.

docs.title: R-CMB-018 Station modules
docs.text:
Modules MUST mount at a hub's attachment points (OBJ slot_<name> groups, original manipulators by index), follow the hub, provide turrets and shield generators, and fall with the hub, leaving wrecks in their destroyed look.

Rationale: Base assaults and defences.

  • Implements: F-CMB-009
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::station_modules_mount_follow_and_fall_with_their_hub, formats::obj::slot_groups_become_attachment_points; MT-2-22, MT-2-23
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Stations, modules and probes, Deviations (DEV-035)

Open

Damage zones on hubs are not built (Stage 2 deferred list).

docs.title: R-CMB-019 Model sets and damage looks
docs.text:
A model set MUST define the intact model, texture swaps that accumulate with damage levels (by hull fraction), and named states that may swap the texture, the mesh and the debris set; the viewer MUST show every look.

Rationale: Visible damage; construction stages.

  • Implements: F-CMB-010, F-STR-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::looks::swaps_accumulate_with_damage_and_state, texture_keys_ignore_folders_case_and_extensions; app::viewer::looks_cover_damage_states_and_debris; MT-2-25
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Format: objects and models, Looks

Open

Slot size classes, overlay groups and lod<n>_* files are not built (Stage 2 deferred list).

docs.title: R-CMB-020 Debris and explosions
docs.text:
Destruction MUST spawn the object's debris set (pieces with offsets, speed and spin ranges, random picks, lifetimes, seeded) and its effect (fireball size, duration, colour, optional shock wave, sound).

Rationale: Feedback on kills; engine fireballs stand in for sprites (DEV-034).

  • Implements: F-CMB-010
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::looks::debris_and_effects_parse_with_defaults; render::effects::events_create_effects_that_expire, explosion_curve_grows_and_fades; MT-1-13, MT-2-25
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Looks

Open

XSPT sprite explosions, shield flashes, lights and debris collisions are deferred.

docs.title: R-CMB-021 Shot physics
docs.text:
A ruleset option MUST choose how shots move, and the default MUST be physics: a shot MUST leave the muzzle with the craft's velocity plus the craft's turn velocity at the muzzle (angular velocity × muzzle offset) plus its own muzzle speed, and once fired MUST move independently of the craft's orientation.

Rationale: User request (F-CMB-011); decision D1.

  • Implements: F-CMB-011
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item F.2).
  • See: Simulation

Open

The option's key name and what its non-default value does are not yet specified.

docs.title: Compatibility (original data) requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for discovering and reading the player's original data. The normative format descriptions are the Original data formats pages.

Features: Compatibility (original data). How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-CMP-001 Finding the player's data Implemented R-CMP-002 Original data by name in any layout Implemented R-CMP-003 PE resources Implemented R-CMP-004 XMSH meshes Implemented R-CMP-005 XTXR textures Implemented R-CMP-006 TGA images and colour key Implemented R-CMP-007 Audio Implemented R-CMP-008 INI rules and language files Implemented R-CMP-009 XSPT sprites Planned R-CMP-010 Smacker video Planned R-CMP-011 Bad data never panics Implemented R-CMP-012 No original content Implemented R-CMP-013 Facts and deviations marked Implemented

docs.title: R-CMP-001 Finding the player's data
docs.text:
The original data MUST be found in this order: command line, environment, settings, the user data folder, the development tree; explicit and existing locations MUST win.

Rationale: Works without --data (plan item 1.14).

  • Implements: F-CMP-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: settings::resolution_order_prefers_explicit_and_existing; cli::environment_supplies_data_and_flags_override_it
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Settings and data discovery

docs.title: R-CMP-002 Original data by name in any layout
docs.text:
Original resources MUST be found by name whatever the layout of the player's copy.

Rationale: CD copies differ.

  • Implements: F-CMP-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::vfs::original_data_is_found_by_name_in_any_layout
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: CD layout

docs.title: R-CMP-003 PE resources
docs.text:
Resources MUST be read from the original DLLs by type and name, as data; non-PE and truncated files MUST be errors.

Rationale: Original meshes and textures live in DLL resources.

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::pe::finds_resources_by_type_and_name, name_ids_are_normalised, rejects_non_pe_data, truncated_files_are_errors, missing_file_is_an_error
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: PE resource container

docs.title: R-CMP-004 XMSH meshes
docs.text:
XMSH meshes MUST be read with their LODs, signed edge loops, untextured polygons and polygon flags, mirrored into engine handedness with outward winding, triangulated and grouped; overlapping overlay faces MUST be layered by depth bias.

Rationale: All 297 meshes (verified, Stage 0); DEV-023.

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::xmsh::parses_a_hand_built_mesh, polygon_flags_are_read, signed_edges_give_the_vertex_loop, rejects_bad_signature_and_bad_references; model::xmsh_is_triangulated_grouped_and_mirrored, mirrored_triangles_keep_outward_winding, later_overlapping_face_is_layered_on_top, overlay_flag_beats_file_order; MT-1-31
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: XMSH meshes

docs.title: R-CMP-005 XTXR textures
docs.text:
XTXR textures MUST be decoded through palette 0 with RGB555 expanded to full range.

Rationale: Original textures (DEV-005).

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::xtxr::decodes_pixels_through_palette_zero, expands_rgb555_to_full_range, rejects_bad_data
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: XTXR textures

docs.title: R-CMP-006 TGA images and colour key
docs.text:
TGA images (16, 24 and 32 bit, RLE, colour-mapped) MUST decode; the cockpit colour key MUST become transparent black.

Rationale: Cockpit art (DEV-017).

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::tga::decodes_16_bit_with_colour_key_and_flips_rows, decodes_24_and_32_bit_bgr, decodes_rle, decodes_colour_mapped_images, rejects_unsupported_and_truncated
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: TGA images and cockpits

docs.title: R-CMP-007 Audio
docs.text:
WAV in PCM 8/16, MS ADPCM and IMA ADPCM MUST decode.

Rationale: Original sound effects and music.

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::wav::pcm16_round_trips_through_to_wav_bytes, pcm8_is_recentred, ms_adpcm_block_decodes, ima_adpcm_block_decodes, adpcm_step_clamps_and_keeps_delta_minimum, rejects_bad_files
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Audio

docs.title: R-CMP-008 INI rules and language files
docs.text:
Original INI files MUST be read (Latin-1, comments, duplicates, warnings for ignored lines) and original language files MUST be read with their ~ line breaks.

Rationale: Balance data and text are plain files.

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::ini::parses_sections_keys_and_comments, reports_lines_it_ignores, latin1_bytes_are_accepted, merge_overrides_keys_and_adds_sections, bad_numbers_and_bools_are_none; formats::langfile::keys_text_and_line_breaks
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: INI rule files

docs.title: R-CMP-009 XSPT sprites
docs.text:
XSPT sprite animations SHOULD be decoded and used for the original explosions.

Rationale: Faithful explosions (DEV-034 until then).

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: XSPT sprites

Open

The RLE pixel runs are not decoded (unknown).

docs.title: R-CMP-010 Smacker video
docs.text:
Smacker video MUST be decoded in-crate for the original cut-scenes and MFD talking heads.

Rationale: Faithful presentation.

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Smacker video

docs.title: R-CMP-011 Bad data never panics
docs.text:
Every reader MUST return an error with a readable message on bad, truncated or out-of-bounds data, never panic.

Rationale: Modded and damaged data must not crash the game.

  • Implements: F-CMP-002, F-MOD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::out_of_bounds_is_an_error_not_a_panic, errors_have_readable_messages, formats::xmsh::truncated_mesh_is_an_error, mesh_without_lods_is_invalid
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Error handling

docs.title: R-CMP-012 No original content
docs.text:
No original asset may enter the repository or a published build in any form; tests MUST use synthetic data built in the test; original binaries MUST be read as data only and never executed.

Rationale: The player supplies the data (project rule).

  • Implements: F-CMP-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: Review against the project rules; the .gitignore safety net.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Testing policy

docs.title: R-CMP-013 Facts and deviations marked
docs.text:
Facts derived from the original data MUST be marked verified, derived or unknown, and every knowing difference from the original MUST be recorded as a deviation.

Rationale: An undocumented deviation looks like a bug.

  • Implements: F-CMP-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: Review.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Deviations

docs.title: Controls & control console requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for bindings, the controls menu, the action catalogue and overlay, and the tablet control console. The console's wire format is on Console protocol.

Features: Controls & control console. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-CON-001 One action table Implemented R-CON-002 Original default layout Implemented R-CON-003 Bindings file Implemented R-CON-004 Controls menu Implemented R-CON-005 Gamepad Implemented R-CON-006 Mouse flight and chords Implemented R-CON-007 Action catalogue Planned R-CON-008 Controls overlay Planned R-CON-009 Console server Planned R-CON-010 Console protocol Planned R-CON-011 Console actions are game actions Planned R-CON-012 Console page from web components Planned R-CON-013 Console layout Planned R-CON-014 Console telemetry Planned R-CON-015 Target viewport Planned R-CON-016 3D map view Planned R-CON-017 Serial transport Planned R-CON-018 Function-group tiles Planned R-CON-019 Features the craft lacks are disabled, not hidden Planned R-CON-020 Console theme from the active pack Planned R-CON-021 Console theme assets are original-free Planned

docs.title: R-CON-001 One action table
docs.text:
Every bindable action MUST be defined once, in one table that drives parsing of the bindings file, the defaults, the controls menu and the documentation; every action MUST be reachable from the keyboard and every flight action from the gamepad.

Rationale: One source of truth for controls.

  • Implements: F-CON-001, F-CON-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::every_action_is_reachable_from_keyboard_and_flight_actions_from_the_pad, input::editor::rows_are_grouped_and_headers_are_skipped
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-CON-002 Original default layout
docs.text:
Default keys MUST follow the original's layout, including power and equipment keys; actions the original left undocumented get the defaults recorded as deviations.

Rationale: Compatibility (DEV-001, DEV-027).

  • Implements: F-CON-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::default_keys_follow_the_original_layout, power_and_equipment_keys_follow_the_original, chase_camera_keys, view_names_parse; MT-1-04, MT-1-05
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Controls (original game)

docs.title: R-CON-003 Bindings file
docs.text:
Bindings MUST be saved in bindings.yaml with two key and two gamepad slots per action, MUST round-trip, and an old bindings.ini MUST be migrated once.

Rationale: Players keep their layout.

  • Implements: F-CON-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::bindings_file_overrides_and_round_trips; MT-2-09
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-CON-004 Controls menu
docs.text:
A controls menu, reachable from the launcher and the pause menu (K), MUST capture keys and gamepad presses and chords, take a captured binding from any other action, clear and reset bindings, and edit device settings (dead zone, invert pitch, stick layout, mouse range and invert).

Rationale: Rebinding without editing files.

  • Implements: F-CON-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::editor::capturing_a_key_rebinds_and_steals_it_from_others, capturing_pad_plain_presses_and_chords, clear_reset_and_settings, pretty_names; app::devices::key_names_match_the_bindings_vocabulary; MT-2-09, MT-2-10, MT-2-11
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-CON-005 Gamepad
docs.text:
Gamepads MUST work with sticks, buttons, a dead zone and a modifier layer (holding the left shoulder reaches a second layer that covers every power control); a button used as a modifier MUST do nothing on its own.

Rationale: Fewer buttons than keys (DEV-028).

  • Implements: F-CON-001, F-PLT-001, F-PLT-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::gamepad_sticks_buttons_and_presses, chord_parsing_and_dead_zone, pad_modifier_layer_reaches_every_power_control, stick_layouts_and_mouse_inversion; input::gamepad::axes_are_normalised, buttons_round_trip_names_and_bits; MT-1-07, MT-2-10
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-CON-006 Mouse flight and chords
docs.text:
Mouse flight MUST be a toggle; a Shift chord MUST NOT also trigger the plain key; one-shot presses MUST be carried to the next simulation tick when a frame runs none.

Rationale: Menus usable; no lost presses on high-refresh displays (DEV-004, DEV-015).

  • Implements: F-CON-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::mouse_flight_only_when_enabled, a_shift_chord_does_not_also_trigger_the_plain_held_key, one_shot_commands_and_shift_chords; sim::unconsumed_presses_carry_over_held_inputs_do_not; MT-1-06
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-CON-007 Action catalogue
docs.text:
Each action MUST have, in the one action table (R-CON-001), an id, a display name, a group and a short description, so that the bindings, the controls overlay and the console's catalogue message are generated from it.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-003): one catalogue drives keys, the overlay and the console.

  • Implements: F-CON-003, F-CON-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item F.5).
  • See: Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-CON-008 Controls overlay
docs.text:
A key MUST toggle an in-flight overlay listing the actions by group with their current bindings, without leaving the battle.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-003).

  • Implements: F-CON-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item F.5; a manual test).
  • See: Input and gamepads

Open

The request names F1, which today selects cockpit view 1 (views F1–F8, an original key). Which key opens the overlay, and whether view 1 moves (a deviation), is to be decided.

docs.title: R-CON-009 Console server
docs.text:
The game MUST be able to serve the console page and a WebSocket endpoint. The console MUST be off by default, MUST accept connections from the local network only, MUST require a pairing code, and MUST listen on port 8765 by default, with the port changeable in the settings if it conflicts.

Rationale: Decision D2: safe by default.

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C1).
  • See: Console protocol

Open

The settings keys, how "local network only" is enforced, and how the pairing code is shown to the player.

docs.title: R-CON-010 Console protocol
docs.text:
Game and console MUST exchange the JSON messages of the console protocol; the protocol MUST NOT depend on the transport.

Rationale: A later USB serial transport reuses it.

  • Implements: F-CON-004, F-CON-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C1).
  • See: Console protocol

docs.title: R-CON-011 Console actions are game actions
docs.text:
An action from the console MUST have the same effect as the bound input for that action from the catalogue; the console MUST NOT offer actions outside the catalogue.

Rationale: One set of actions, however they are triggered.

  • Implements: F-CON-003, F-CON-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C1).
  • See: Console protocol

docs.title: R-CON-012 Console page from web components
docs.text:
The console page MUST be built from custom web components and CSS, with no framework, and served by the game itself.

Rationale: Lightweight, dependency-free web UI (project dependency policy).

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C2).
  • See: Dependency policy

docs.title: R-CON-013 Console layout
docs.text:
The console MUST show the exterior-view HUD in its top row, a widened display console in the centre, shield rings and shield controls on the left, power sliders on the right, and the other functions grouped logically below. It SHOULD fit an iPad in landscape.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-004).

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C2; a manual test).

Open

The grouping of the remaining functions.

docs.title: R-CON-014 Console telemetry
docs.text:
While paired, the game MUST send craft telemetry at 20 Hz and radar contacts at 5 Hz, and events as they happen.

Rationale: Real-time knowledge of the craft's condition.

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C1).
  • See: Console protocol

docs.title: R-CON-015 Target viewport
docs.text:
The console's centre display MUST show the current target's model at its true orientation relative to the player's craft. The game MUST send each target class's mesh once, decimated.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-005).

  • Implements: F-CON-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C3).
  • See: Console protocol

Open

The decimation budget, and whether textures are sent. Original meshes sent to a device on the player's own network stay on the player's equipment (no redistribution).

docs.title: R-CON-016 3D map view
docs.text:
The centre display MUST toggle between the target viewport and a 3D map view of the battle modelled on TIE Fighter's map.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-006).

  • Implements: F-CON-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C4).

Open

What the map shows (contacts, nav points, ranges, orders) and how it is navigated.

docs.title: R-CON-017 Serial transport
docs.text:
The console protocol SHOULD be carried over a USB serial link so a physical panel (Arduino) with lights and buttons can act as a console.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-007), longer term.

  • Implements: F-CON-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C5, later).
  • See: Console protocol

Open

Framing, the message subset a microcontroller handles, and pairing over serial.

docs.title: R-CON-018 Function-group tiles
docs.text:
The console MUST present one tile per function group, each a status card for its system group. Tapping a tile MUST collapse the other tiles to their headers and open a full-width control strip for that group; tapping the open group's title MUST collapse the strip so all status cards show; tapping another group's title MUST switch the strip to that group.

Rationale: Many options per function group stay manageable on a tablet (F-CON-008).

  • Implements: F-CON-008
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C2; a manual test).
  • See: Console protocol

Open

The set of function groups and which status each card shows (the user's mockup is the reference; it is not on this site).

docs.title: R-CON-019 Features the craft lacks are disabled, not hidden
docs.text:
Every function group MUST be shown for every craft. A control for a feature the current craft lacks (for example cloak or ECM not fitted, or no missiles) MUST appear disabled: greyed, not tappable and labelled as not fitted; the group's status card MUST show that feature as not fitted. Availability MUST be sent per action in the catalogue message and resent when the craft changes.

Rationale: All function groups are common to every craft by design; only individual features differ (user correction, F-CON-008).

  • Implements: F-CON-008
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C2).
  • See: Console protocol

Open

Whether a fitted but destroyed system is shown as not fitted or as damaged (read here: damaged, from telemetry).

docs.title: R-CON-020 Console theme from the active pack
docs.text:
The console's visual style MUST come from the active campaign or mod, delivered as a console theme in the theme message; a pack without a console theme MUST get a plain, clearly labelled default.

Rationale: Immersion matching the campaign (F-CON-009).

  • Implements: F-CON-009, F-MOD-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C2).
  • See: Console protocol

Open

The theme's file format and keys in the pack (to be documented on the Modding pages when added).

docs.title: R-CON-021 Console theme assets are original-free
docs.text:
Console theme assets MUST be new art made for this project and kept in the pack's own files; the interceptor console theme MUST be styled after the current craft's cockpit overlay (palette and framing cues read at run time, or new art made in the same spirit) without reproducing any original art; every control MUST be clearly labelled. The default campaign's theme MUST follow its retro (art-deco) style.

Rationale: Never reproduce original content (project rule); legibility on a tablet.

  • Implements: F-CON-009, F-CMP-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C2).
  • See: The default campaign

docs.title: Flight requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for the flight model, speed management, collisions, the arena edge, hyperspace and atmospheric flight.

Features: Flight. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-FLT-001 Newtonian flight model Implemented R-FLT-002 Assisted flight model option Implemented R-FLT-003 Turn rates fall with speed Implemented R-FLT-004 Speed hold Implemented R-FLT-005 Afterburner Implemented R-FLT-006 Vectored thrust (VCT) Implemented R-FLT-007 Arena edge Implemented R-FLT-008 Hyperspace out Implemented R-FLT-009 Collisions Implemented R-FLT-010 Fixed, deterministic tick Implemented R-FLT-011 Atmospheric flight Planned R-FLT-012 Terrain Planned

docs.title: R-FLT-001 Newtonian flight model
docs.text:
Under the newtonian model (the default) the simulation MUST treat throttle as thrust, let a ship coast at zero throttle, decelerate it with reverse thrust or a held brake, cap forward speed at the hull's max_speed, and MUST NOT steer the velocity when the ship turns.

Rationale: Space flight with momentum, as the owner asked after the first playtest.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::newtonian_accelerates_to_the_cap_and_coasts, half_throttle_is_half_the_acceleration, reverse_thrust_slows_and_then_backs_up, brake_stops_against_the_direction_of_travel, turning_does_not_steer_the_velocity; MT-1-22
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-019)

docs.title: R-FLT-002 Assisted flight model option
docs.text:
A ruleset MUST be able to select flight: {model: assisted}, in which throttle sets a target forward speed, the ship accelerates towards it and sideways drift is damped.

Rationale: Mods that want arcade handling keep it.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::assisted_model_holds_throttle_speed_and_damps_drift
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Rulesets

docs.title: R-FLT-003 Turn rates fall with speed
docs.text:
Pitch and yaw rates MUST scale with clamp(1 − |speed| / lock_speed, 0, 1); roll MUST NOT be reduced; angular velocity MUST approach the commanded value with the hull's damping.

Rationale: The original's handling: fast ships turn wide.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::pitching_up_raises_the_nose_and_rates_fall_with_speed, yaw_right_and_roll_right_turn_the_expected_way, helpers; MT-1-04
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-004 Speed hold
docs.text:
Match speed MUST set a held forward speed equal to the target's; while held, the ship MUST thrust and brake within its own acceleration towards nose × hold, cancelling drift. Any manual throttle, reverse or brake input MUST clear the hold. AI pilots MUST manage speed through the same hold.

Rationale: Speed management under newtonian flight, with the same limits for AI and player.

  • Implements: F-FLT-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::speed_hold_matches_speed_and_cancels_drift, sim::match_speed_copies_the_targets_speed; MT-1-23
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-020)

docs.title: R-FLT-005 Afterburner
docs.text:
The afterburner MUST raise the speed cap and drain energy while lit; speed above the normal cap MUST bleed off at the hull's acceleration once it stops. Thrust and the afterburner MUST scale with the engines' efficiency (no afterburner at zero).

Rationale: Original piloting function; damage matters.

  • Implements: F-FLT-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::afterburner_raises_the_cap_drains_energy_and_excess_bleeds_off; MT-1-05
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-006 Vectored thrust (VCT)
docs.text:
A hull with VCT MUST be able to thrust sideways and vertically at 0.5 × acceleration under the newtonian model (25 % of max_speed as a slide under the assisted model), scaled by the VCT system's efficiency.

Rationale: Original equipment.

  • Implements: F-FLT-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::vct_thrusts_sideways
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-007 Arena edge
docs.text:
A ship beyond flight.arena_radius (default 60 km; 0 = no limit) MUST be placed back on the boundary with its outward velocity removed and its tangential velocity kept, and the pilot MUST be told "ARENA BOUNDARY" on first arrival.

Rationale: Coasting ships would otherwise leave for ever.

  • Implements: F-FLT-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::the_arena_edge_halts_outward_motion; MT-1-24
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-021)

docs.title: R-FLT-008 Hyperspace out
docs.text:
Hyperspace MUST count down flight.hyperspace_time seconds (doubled while the hyperdrive is damaged); pressing the key again MUST abort; on departure the ship MUST leave the battle with any ship it tows as a captured prize. The player jumping out of a mission MUST end it as retreat.

Rationale: Original retreat and capture.

  • Implements: F-FLT-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::hyperspace_counts_down_aborts_and_departs, tractor_holds_a_disabled_target_and_captures_it_on_jump; MT-2-07
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-026)

docs.title: R-FLT-009 Collisions
docs.text:
Fighters touching (spheres at 60 % of radius) MUST be pushed apart and exchange half their velocities; a fighter sweeping into a station mesh MUST be backed out and bounced; collision damage MUST be relative speed × 0.1. Bolts and missiles MUST test the segment travelled each tick so they cannot pass through a target.

Rationale: Solid stations and hits that count.

  • Implements: F-FLT-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::fighters_bounce_off_each_other_and_stations, sim::collision::segment_sphere_hits_misses_and_inside, segment_triangle_hits_inside_only, shapes_use_mesh_in_model_space; MT-1-15
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-010 Fixed, deterministic tick
docs.text:
The simulation MUST advance at a fixed 60 Hz tick, use seeded random sequences, and have no rendering or input dependency, so the same inputs give the same battle.

Rationale: Testable simulation and repeatable soak runs.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001, F-TST-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::step_advances_time_and_clears_edge_controls, sim::random_is_deterministic_and_in_range, sim::generational_handles_detect_reuse
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Architectural design

docs.title: R-FLT-011 Atmospheric flight
docs.text:
A ship in an atmosphere MUST feel drag, gravity and lift, MAY hover, MUST collide with the ground and be able to land, and MUST be able to escape through the ceiling. Per-ship values DragArea, Lift, Hover, AtmosphereMaxSpeed and Atmospheric MUST be data.

Rationale: Surface missions.

  • Implements: F-FLT-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (Stage 3 exit: "atmospheric flight feels distinct from space", manual test).
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events, Stage 3

Open

The flight model's equations and the key spellings in mod format 2 are not designed yet.

docs.title: R-FLT-012 Terrain
docs.text:
A surface environment MUST provide a heightfield from an image or a generator (craters, hills), textured with detail maps, with scattered objects, a sky gradient and fog, and MUST support ground installations (kind: ground) and anti-air turrets.

Rationale: Surface missions of the default campaign.

  • Implements: F-FLT-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events
