docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Bootstrap: R-FLT-001 – R-FLT-012 (12 requirements; 10 reverse-engineered from the code)

docs.title: Missions requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for missions as data, objectives and outcomes, the debrief, chatter, environments, hazards and mission balance. The normative file format is Format: missions, environments, events.

Features: Missions. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-MSN-001 Mission roles Implemented R-MSN-002 Arrivals and waves Implemented R-MSN-003 Objectives, timer and outcomes Implemented R-MSN-004 Mission mistakes found on load Implemented R-MSN-005 Debrief Implemented R-MSN-006 Radio chatter Implemented R-MSN-007 Voices Planned R-MSN-008 Battle environments Planned R-MSN-009 Hazards Planned R-MSN-010 Simulator missions Planned R-MSN-011 Base defence balance Planned R-MSN-012 Logistics missions Implemented

docs.title: R-MSN-001 Mission roles
docs.text:
A mission MUST declare roles with class lists, counts per difficulty level, faction, AI, behaviour, protect, state, hull, systems and speed; at start roles MUST be placed, counted and faced at the player.

Rationale: Missions as data.

  • Implements: F-MSN-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::mission::a_full_mission_parses, mission::roles_are_placed_counted_and_faced_at_the_player; MT-3-01 – MT-3-09
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events, Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-002 Arrivals and waves
docs.text:
A role MUST be able to arrive at a position relative to another (at: {distance, bearing, from, spread}) and when a condition holds (arrive:); a role without arrive: MUST enter at the start; waves MUST repeat a role's arrival.

Rationale: One place per group (DEV-040).

  • Implements: F-MSN-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: mission::arrivals_waves_chatter_and_a_win
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-003 Objectives, timer and outcomes
docs.text:
A mission MUST evaluate win, draw and lose conditions and optional objectives in the battle context; lose MUST beat win in the same tick; a timer MUST end the mission with its stated result; outcomes MUST be lists of checked actions with battle or campaign scope.

Rationale: Clear, testable results.

  • Implements: F-MSN-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: mission::lose_beats_win_and_the_timer_ends_it; script::action::actions_parse_and_check; script::battle::ids_match_and_roles_are_checked_names
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (architecture), Conditions (script)

docs.title: R-MSN-004 Mission mistakes found on load
docs.text:
Mistakes in a mission file (unknown role, bad timer result, unknown action) MUST be reported on load with where they are.

Rationale: Modders find errors before flying.

  • Implements: F-MSN-001, F-MOD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::mission::mistakes_are_reported_with_where
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-005 Debrief
docs.text:
At the end of a mission the debrief MUST show the result, its text, kills, losses, time, optional objectives and the campaign actions, and MUST offer a retry. The player jumping out MUST count as retreat.

Rationale: Closure and feedback.

  • Implements: F-MSN-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: MT-3-01 – MT-3-11 (the debrief in every mission case)
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (architecture)

Open

Salvage and score are applied by the strategy layer (Stage 4).

docs.title: R-MSN-006 Radio chatter
docs.text:
A mission MUST be able to play chatter lines when their conditions become true.

Rationale: Atmosphere and information.

  • Implements: F-MSN-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: mission::arrivals_waves_chatter_and_a_win
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-007 Voices
docs.text:
Chatter and the computer voice SHOULD play recorded or original voice samples.

Rationale: Atmosphere.

  • Implements: F-MSN-003, F-CPN-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Stage 6

docs.title: R-MSN-008 Battle environments
docs.text:
A battle MUST take place in one of the environments space, orbit, pocket or a surface, with a backdrop chosen from its map location.

Rationale: Variety; surface missions.

  • Implements: F-MSN-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events

docs.title: R-MSN-009 Hazards
docs.text:
A mission MUST be able to declare hazards: asteroids, black-hole pull, minefields and ion storms.

Rationale: Variety.

  • Implements: F-MSN-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events

docs.title: R-MSN-010 Simulator missions
docs.text:
The player MUST be able to set up a simulator mission on a setup screen and fly it.

Rationale: Original simulator.

  • Implements: F-MSN-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Stage 3

docs.title: R-MSN-011 Base defence balance
docs.text:
In every base-defence mission, at every difficulty including the lowest, the base MUST survive long enough for the player to engage more than one attacker.

Rationale: User request (F-MSN-006).

  • Implements: F-MSN-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item F.4; soak runs and a manual test).
  • See: Missions (modding), Manual tests (MT-3-01, MT-3-05)

Open

A measurable threshold (for example a minimum time to destroy the base at the lowest level, measured with --soak), and which values change (base shields and hull, attacker counts and arrivals, point defence). The changes are pack data.

docs.title: R-MSN-012 Logistics missions
docs.text:
The convoy_ambush and construction_defence missions MUST be playable: protect the convoy against attackers; defend a facility shown in its construction-stage state.

Rationale: Logistics in battle.

  • Implements: F-MSN-007
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: MT-3-02, MT-3-03
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Logistics

Open

Generation from the strategy layer is R-STR-019.

docs.title: Modding toolkit requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for packs, rule files, schemas, overrides, extraction, text, the condition language, validation and recipes. The normative structure is Mod structure; every key is in the Mod file reference.

Features: Modding toolkit. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-MOD-001 Pack manifests Implemented R-MOD-002 Load order Implemented R-MOD-003 Rules layering Implemented R-MOD-004 Gameplay values are data Implemented R-MOD-005 YAML subset Implemented R-MOD-006 Schemas and messages Implemented R-MOD-007 Settings and bindings migration Implemented R-MOD-008 Per-asset overrides Implemented R-MOD-009 Extraction Implemented R-MOD-010 Open model and image formats Implemented R-MOD-011 Paths stay inside the pack Implemented R-MOD-012 Text keys Implemented R-MOD-013 Condition language Implemented R-MOD-014 Campaign context Planned R-MOD-015 Tier 2 scripting decision Planned R-MOD-016 Headless validation Implemented R-MOD-017 Full validator Planned R-MOD-018 Recipes Planned R-MOD-019 Sound cue table Implemented R-MOD-020 Every key documented Implemented

docs.title: R-MOD-001 Pack manifests
docs.text:
A pack manifest MUST declare its kind (campaign, addon, library), and MAY declare parent, targets, format and dependencies; bad manifests MUST be rejected with a message.

Rationale: Mod structure.

  • Implements: F-MOD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::pack::parses_a_manifest, manifests_declare_kind_parent_targets_and_format, rejects_bad_manifests, discovers_pack_folders
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Mod structure, Packs

docs.title: R-MOD-002 Load order
docs.text:
Packs MUST load dependencies first and otherwise keep their order; missing, duplicate and cyclic dependencies MUST be reported.

Rationale: Predictable layering.

  • Implements: F-MOD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::pack::orders_dependencies_first_and_keeps_order_otherwise, detects_missing_duplicate_and_cyclic_dependencies
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Packs

docs.title: R-MOD-003 Rules layering
docs.text:
Definitions MUST be able to inherit original INI sections (inherit: original:…); later packs MUST merge into, delete and edit (key+, key-) earlier definitions.

Rationale: Addons change campaigns without copying them.

  • Implements: F-MOD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::rules::builds_typed_definitions_with_inheritance, later_packs_merge_delete_and_edit_lists, spelling_of_original_keys
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Rulesets and layering

docs.title: R-MOD-004 Gameplay values are data
docs.text:
Gameplay values, ship, weapon and object definitions, factions, scenarios and missions MUST live in pack data, not in engine code.

Rationale: Modding first (project rule).

  • Implements: F-MOD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: Code review against the project rules.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Architectural design

docs.title: R-MOD-005 YAML subset
docs.text:
Mod files MUST be a strict YAML subset; tabs, anchors, aliases, tags, multiple documents, complex keys and multi-line plain scalars MUST be rejected with their line number.

Rationale: One unambiguous reading, read in-crate (DEV-030).

  • Implements: F-MOD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::yaml::mappings_sequences_and_scalars, block_scalars_and_wrapped_flows, unsupported_and_broken_input_is_an_error_with_a_line, keys_with_colons_and_urls_stay_whole, writing_round_trips, empty_and_scalar_documents
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Mod file reference

docs.title: R-MOD-006 Schemas and messages
docs.text:
Every mod file type MUST be described by a schema; mistakes MUST be reported with file, line and key path, unknown keys with a did-you-mean suggestion; quantities MUST accept units (2.4km, 1.5s, 12deg, 40%); --write-schemas MUST export JSON Schemas; loading MUST report every error and keep going.

Rationale: A modder never has to guess (plan item 2.19).

  • Implements: F-MOD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::schema::good_files_pass, mistakes_are_reported_with_line_and_path, quantities_and_suggestions, json_schema_is_wellformed_enough; content::files::every_schema_builds_and_exports; content::rules::reports_every_error_and_keeps_going; content::scenario::errors_name_the_line_and_path; MT-2-18
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Mod file reference

docs.title: R-MOD-007 Settings and bindings migration
docs.text:
settings.ini and bindings.ini MUST be migrated once to settings.yaml and bindings.yaml.

Rationale: No lost settings across format changes.

  • Implements: F-MOD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: settings::parses_and_round_trips; input::bindings_file_overrides_and_round_trips
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Settings and data discovery

docs.title: R-MOD-008 Per-asset overrides
docs.text:
Any original model, texture, image or sound MUST be replaceable by a pack file at its override path; disabling the pack MUST restore the original.

Rationale: HD and 3D replacements (DEV-022).

  • Implements: F-MOD-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::pack_files_override_original_assets, content::vfs::override_paths_follow_the_convention; MT-1-25, MT-1-28, MT-1-29
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Overrides and extraction

docs.title: R-MOD-009 Extraction
docs.text:
--extract MUST write every original asset as OBJ, PNG or WAV at its override path, with keyed cockpit pixels as alpha, and OBJ exports MUST load back through the mod loader.

Rationale: Editable starting points.

  • Implements: F-MOD-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: extract::extraction_writes_override_paths, obj_export_round_trips_through_the_mod_loader, png_encoding_decodes_back; MT-1-27
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Extractor

docs.title: R-MOD-010 Open model and image formats
docs.text:
Mods MUST be able to supply Wavefront OBJ models with MTL materials (slot_* groups as attachment points) and PNG or TGA textures.

Rationale: Universal export targets.

  • Implements: F-MOD-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: formats::obj::parses_positions_uvs_normals_and_faces, parses_materials, rejects_bad_indices_and_short_faces; model::obj_models_use_materials_scale_and_flip_v; content::png_and_tga_pack_images_decode
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Models and textures

docs.title: R-MOD-011 Paths stay inside the pack
docs.text:
Asset references MUST be normalised and MUST NOT escape their pack.

Rationale: A mod cannot read arbitrary files.

  • Implements: F-MOD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::vfs::parses_asset_references, refuses_paths_that_escape_the_pack
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Packs, VFS and rules

docs.title: R-MOD-012 Text keys
docs.text:
Text MUST be referable by @key from text/<language>/ files; original language files MUST be importable by reference; the language MUST be chosen by --language or game.language.

Rationale: Translation by addon.

  • Implements: F-MOD-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::text::keys_resolve_plain_values_pass_through_and_imports_are_listed; formats::langfile::keys_text_and_line_breaks; MT-2-34
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Text and translation

docs.title: R-MOD-013 Condition language
docs.text:
Conditions MUST be parsed and type-checked at load (unknown names, argument counts and types reported) and evaluated with precedence and short-circuit, with units, in the object and battle contexts.

Rationale: Data that depends on the situation.

  • Implements: F-MOD-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: script::units_and_tokens, evaluates_with_precedence_and_short_circuits, errors_are_found_when_loading; script::object::ids_match_the_table_and_system_names_match_the_kinds; script::battle::ids_match_and_roles_are_checked_names
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Format: behaviours and scripting, Conditions (script)

docs.title: R-MOD-014 Campaign context
docs.text:
Conditions MUST gain a campaign context with system and facility queries (deposit, feature, research_site, survey_known, owned, lane_distance, facility_progress, construction_attacks).

Rationale: Strategy-layer rules and logistics.

  • Implements: F-MOD-005, F-STR-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-MOD-015 Tier 2 scripting decision
docs.text:
Before a second-tier script language is added, its dependency evaluation MUST be recorded on the dependency page; hooks and a sandboxed API follow.

Rationale: Dependency policy.

  • Implements: F-MOD-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Scripting (design)

docs.title: R-MOD-016 Headless validation
docs.text:
--check MUST validate the active campaign headlessly and report every error; the default campaign MUST pass with no errors and the full reference CD with no errors.

Rationale: Mistakes found before playing.

  • Implements: F-MOD-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: check::the_default_campaign_passes, broken_definitions_are_errors
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Validating a mod

docs.title: R-MOD-017 Full validator
docs.text:
The validator MUST check every definition, reference, condition and text key, per addon, and write a JSON report; it MUST catch every seeded error in a test mod.

Rationale: Stage 7 exit.

  • Implements: F-MOD-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Stage 7

docs.title: R-MOD-018 Recipes
docs.text:
Generated assets MUST be built by recipes (upscale, mesh-patch, recolour, composite) into a cache keyed by recipe, version and input hash, with outputs bit-identical across runs and machines.

Rationale: Remastered content without redistributing originals.

  • Implements: F-MOD-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Mod structure

docs.title: R-MOD-019 Sound cue table
docs.text:
Sounds MUST be referable by name and through the original cue table (audio.cue_table, cue:<Name>).

Rationale: Original sounds by their cue names.

  • Implements: F-MOD-001, F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::rules::sound_cues_resolve_through_the_original_table; audio::events_choose_sounds_and_volumes; MT-1-18, MT-2-26
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Rulesets and layering

docs.title: R-MOD-020 Every key documented
docs.text:
Every new rule key, scenario key or pack feature MUST be documented on the Modding pages in the same change.

Rationale: Modding first (project rule).

  • Implements: F-MOD-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: Review against the project rules.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Mod file reference

docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Bootstrap: R-MOD-001 – R-MOD-020 (20 requirements; 16 reverse-engineered from the code)

docs.title: Platforms requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for the macOS, Linux and Windows builds, packaging and dependencies.

Features: Platforms. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-PLT-001 macOS app Implemented R-PLT-002 Linux Implemented R-PLT-003 Windows Planned R-PLT-004 Release packages Planned R-PLT-005 One dependency Implemented R-PLT-006 Unsafe only at boundaries Implemented

docs.title: R-PLT-001 macOS app
docs.text:
A macOS .app bundle with the stage build number MUST open from Finder and contain only the engine and original-free packs.

Rationale: First platform.

  • Implements: F-PLT-001, F-PLT-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: MT-1-30
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Packaging

docs.title: R-PLT-002 Linux
docs.text:
The engine MUST build and run on Linux, with gamepads through the Linux joystick API.

Rationale: First-class platform.

  • Implements: F-PLT-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: platform::linux test (Linux only); MT-1-21 (not yet run)
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Platform layer

Open

Built and type-checked only; not yet run on Linux.

docs.title: R-PLT-003 Windows
docs.text:
The engine MUST stay buildable on Windows and SHOULD support XInput gamepads.

Rationale: Reach.

  • Implements: F-PLT-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Stage 8

docs.title: R-PLT-004 Release packages
docs.text:
Releases MUST provide a macOS app, a Linux tarball with a .desktop file and a Windows build, versioned, with no player data in any published build.

Rationale: Distribution.

  • Implements: F-PLT-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Stage 8

docs.title: R-PLT-005 One dependency
docs.text:
The engine MUST depend only on macroquad (pinned); any other dependency MUST be evaluated on the dependency page before it is added.

Rationale: Every dependency is a liability (project rule).

  • Implements: F-PLT-001, F-PLT-002, F-PLT-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: Review of Cargo.toml.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Dependency policy

docs.title: R-PLT-006 Unsafe only at boundaries
docs.text:
unsafe MUST appear only at FFI boundaries (platform shims) and the one documented access to macroquad's GL state, each with a // SAFETY: note.

Rationale: Teaching example and safety (project rule).

  • Implements: F-PLT-001, F-PLT-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: Review.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: FFI, repr(C) and unsafe

docs.title: Strategy & logistics requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for the strategy layer and logistics. The normative designs are Format: strategy layer and Logistics.

Features: Strategy & logistics. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-STR-001 Campaign clock Planned R-STR-002 Star map and travel Planned R-STR-003 Contacts and mission generation Planned R-STR-004 Economy Planned R-STR-005 Research Planned R-STR-006 Bases Planned R-STR-007 Ships and equipment Planned R-STR-008 Pilots Planned R-STR-009 Funding, score and reports Planned R-STR-010 Strategy screens Planned R-STR-011 Saves Planned R-STR-012 Logistics is optional data Planned R-STR-013 Demand-driven orders Planned R-STR-014 Extraction and recipes Planned R-STR-015 Government supply ships Planned R-STR-016 Supply convoys Planned R-STR-017 Supply vessel model Planned R-STR-018 Supply convoy attack position Planned R-STR-019 Logistics mission generation Planned R-STR-020 Cargo losses and depots Planned R-STR-021 Survey ships Planned R-STR-022 Construction stages Planned R-STR-023 Construction attacks Planned R-STR-024 Research stations and sites Planned R-STR-025 Facility fighter pools Planned R-STR-026 Supply cargo capacity Planned R-STR-027 Third-party convoys Planned

docs.title: R-STR-001 Campaign clock
docs.text:
The strategy layer MUST run on a campaign clock with dates, time speeds and auto-pause, start from the campaign's starts definition, and start a new game with a chosen campaign and difficulty.

Rationale: Real-time strategy.

  • Implements: F-STR-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-002 Star map and travel
docs.text:
The star map MUST be generated (classes, bodies, names, hidden black holes; seeded) or fixed, with free or lane travel, endurance and stranding.

Rationale: Both campaigns' maps.

  • Implements: F-STR-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-003 Contacts and mission generation
docs.text:
Squadrons, convoys and probes MUST move on flight plans; sensor coverage MUST decide detection; a mission MUST be generated when hostile forces meet.

Rationale: Battles with a cause.

  • Implements: F-STR-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-004 Economy
docs.text:
The economy MUST model resources, income and expense expressions, markets, factories with prioritised queues, deliveries and losses, and storage.

Rationale: The original's economy, as data.

  • Implements: F-STR-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-005 Research
docs.text:
Research MUST support the download and labs models, discovery by prerequisites, salvage and capture, and unlocks.

Rationale: Tech tree.

  • Implements: F-STR-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-006 Bases
docs.text:
Bases MUST have types, placement rules, templates, module construction with build times and construction states, limits, effects, destruction consequences and dismantling.

Rationale: The original's bases.

  • Implements: F-STR-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-007 Ships and equipment
docs.text:
Hulls, items, slots and fitting rules, power draw and stock designs MUST be data; craft MUST be bought or manufactured.

Rationale: Hangar.

  • Implements: F-STR-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-008 Pilots
docs.text:
Pilots MUST be generated with ranks, experience, training, injury and healing, bravery, recruiting, salaries and voices.

Rationale: Roster.

  • Implements: F-STR-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-009 Funding, score and reports
docs.text:
Patron funding and evaluations, score and ratings and periodic reports MUST be campaign data.

Rationale: The original's funding model.

  • Implements: F-STR-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: strategy layer

docs.title: R-STR-010 Strategy screens
docs.text:
Functional screens MUST cover the star map, bases (with the 3D base view), research, hangar, market, pilots, reports, messages and briefing/debriefing, with hand-off to battle and return.

Rationale: Playable strategy layer before skins (Stage 6).

  • Implements: F-STR-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format: interface, text and media

docs.title: R-STR-011 Saves
docs.text:
A save MUST hold the full campaign state plus the mod list and versions; loading MUST refuse a save whose mods are missing. Logistics state (stores, orders, build progress, ships in flight with their attack rolls, survey results) MUST be saved.

Rationale: Long campaigns; changing mods.

  • Implements: F-STR-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (round-trip unit tests on synthetic campaigns).
  • See: Stage 4

docs.title: R-STR-012 Logistics is optional data
docs.text:
Logistics MUST be entirely campaign data; a campaign without facility_types, recipes and logistics sections MUST behave as without logistics. The interceptor campaign MUST NOT use logistics.

Rationale: Modding first; interceptor stays faithful to the original.

  • Implements: F-STR-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-013 Demand-driven orders
docs.text:
A main base's build queue MUST create orders for components to manufacturing centers; a manufacturing center's recipes MUST create orders for materials to mining facilities; a research station's start cost MUST create a one-off order. Each order MUST be filled by the nearest suitable facility by lane. Nothing MUST be shipped speculatively.

Rationale: A basic supply-and-demand simulation.

  • Implements: F-STR-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-014 Extraction and recipes
docs.text:
Mining facilities MUST extract from deposits at their rate until reserves run out; a recipe MUST start only when its inputs are in that center's store, take its time, and leave its output in the store; storage limits MUST stop production when full.

Rationale: Production follows supply.

  • Implements: F-STR-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-015 Government supply ships
docs.text:
When an order's cargo is ready, supply ships MUST be dispatched automatically along the fixed lanes; they are provided by the government and the player MUST NOT buy or manage them.

Rationale: Logistics decision (2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-016 Supply convoys
docs.text:
A shipment MUST travel as a convoy of several supply vessels, each carrying an even share of the cargo; a convoy that is partly destroyed MUST deliver the surviving vessels' share.

Rationale: Escort missions stay interesting and playable; single ships would be destroyed quickly (decision 2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

Open

The number of vessels per convoy.

docs.title: R-STR-017 Supply vessel model
docs.text:
The default campaign MUST provide a supply vessel model that is reasonably large: a core vessel with several attached cargo containers.

Rationale: A convoy worth escorting (decision 2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-007, F-CPN-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (generated by tools/default_assets/).
  • See: The default campaign

Open

Whether the existing cargo clipper and cargo pod become the core vessel and containers, or a new model replaces them.

docs.title: R-STR-018 Supply convoy attack position
docs.text:
A supply convoy's attack position along its route MUST be chosen at random when it launches.

Rationale: Logistics decision (2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

Open

Whether every supply convoy is attacked or only some, and at what chance: the user's answer gives the 25 % roll for survey ships only (R-STR-021).

docs.title: R-STR-019 Logistics mission generation
docs.text:
A convoy_ambush mission MUST be generated when an attacked convoy reaches its attack position, and a construction_defence mission when a strike on a facility under construction is due; when the player does not fly, the mission MUST be auto-resolved.

Rationale: Logistics in battle.

  • Implements: F-STR-005, F-MSN-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-020 Cargo losses and depots
docs.text:
A destroyed vessel's cargo MUST be lost; a captured vessel's cargo MUST go to the captor and be stored at a supply depot; destroying an enemy supply depot MUST let the player seize its stock.

Rationale: Logistics decision (2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-005
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (depots in Stage 5).
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-021 Survey ships
docs.text:
Surveys MUST be flown by survey ships, a mission profile and craft distinct from supply ships, launched from a base to a system within the base's current radar range. A survey MUST reveal the system's deposits and reserves, features, the research sites it qualifies for and its suitability for each facility type. When a survey ship launches, a 25 % roll MUST decide whether it will be attacked.

Rationale: Logistics decisions (2026-11-11, revised): survey and supply are different.

  • Implements: F-STR-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

Open

What the survey-ship craft is (the design has used the Sky-Eye probe object), where and when an attacked survey ship meets its attackers, and which mission is generated.

docs.title: R-STR-022 Construction stages
docs.text:
A facility under construction MUST be shown in its build_25 state from 0 %, build_60 from 60 % and build_90 from 90 %, and intact on completion, on the strategy map and in battle.

Rationale: Thresholds confirmed (2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-008
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (the stage looks themselves are R-CMB-019, implemented).
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-023 Construction attacks
docs.text:
The enemy MAY strike a facility under construction from 50 % progress, at most three times per location; both numbers MUST be campaign data.

Rationale: Logistics decision (2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-008
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-024 Research stations and sites
docs.text:
A research topic or branch MAY be restricted to a facility type (lab:) and to systems meeting a research site's criteria (site:); its start_cost MUST be delivered once to begin the project, after which research MUST run without further supply.

Rationale: Logistics decision (2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-009
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-025 Facility fighter pools
docs.text:
Fighters MUST be built at main bases and MAY be transferred to a facility's pool, separate from base hangars; pool fighters MUST defend the facility's system and escort its convoys, and MAY be moved between facilities.

Rationale: Logistics decision (2026-11-11).

  • Implements: F-STR-009
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.title: R-STR-026 Supply cargo capacity
docs.text:
A supply vessel's cargo capacity MUST be campaign data.

Rationale: Balance belongs to the campaign.

  • Implements: F-STR-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

Open

The value is TBD, set by tech-tree balance.

docs.title: R-STR-027 Third-party convoys
docs.text:
Prospector convoys MUST fly expeditions (base → system under investigation → pause → base); Cartel convoys MUST fly to random destinations, including empty or uncharted stars; escorting or attacking them MUST change relations.

Rationale: A living map (default campaign, Stage 5).

  • Implements: F-STR-005, F-CPN-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Logistics

docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Bootstrap: R-STR-001 – R-STR-027 (27 requirements; 0 reverse-engineered from the code)

docs.title: Testbed & tools requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for the testbed launcher, viewers, headless runs, debugging tools and generators.

Features: Testbed & tools. How to read a requirement: Specification.

docs.title: R-TST-001 Launcher
docs.text:
The launcher MUST list the viewer, the asset browser, the controls menu, scenarios and missions with scrolling; MUST offer a ship choice only for scenarios that ask for one; and MUST switch campaign and difficulty.

Rationale: Playtest one component at a time.

  • Implements: F-TST-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: app::launcher::menu_lists_viewer_and_scenarios_and_wraps, scenarios_start_with_the_chosen_ship_only_when_choosing, wrapping_text; content::scenario::choose_means_the_launcher_picks; MT-1-01, MT-1-02, MT-3-10
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Testbed

docs.title: R-TST-002 Command line
docs.text:
The command line MUST accept the documented options (including --scenario, --ship, --view, --mission, --campaign, --difficulty, --language, --model, --extract, --screenshot, --frames, --soak, --check), with environment fallbacks, and reject unknown or incomplete options.

Rationale: Scripted runs and quick starts.

docs.title: R-TST-003 Pause menu

docs.title: User guide
docs.text:
How to install, run and play OpenInterceptor.

Page Contents Getting started Building, finding the player's data, the command line

Pages to come:

  • Controls: every action, its default keys and gamepad buttons, and how to rebind them.
  • Settings: settings.yaml, difficulty, language, graphics and audio options.
  • The testbed: the scenario launcher, arenas, missions and the viewers.
  • The tablet control console: using a tablet on the local network as a second control surface.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Rust 1.86 or newer (rustup, stable). The project is checked with 1.99.
  • macOS 11+ (Apple silicon) with the Xcode command line tools, or Linux with X11 (Wayland through XWayland) and OpenGL 3. On Debian/Ubuntu install libasound2-dev libx11-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev first.
  • For original content: your own X-COM: Interceptor CD, copied to a folder. For modding with only original-free packs, nothing else is needed.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
git clone <repo> OpenInterceptor
cd OpenInterceptor
cargo build --release

docs.title: Put the game data in place
docs.text:
Copy the CD contents (the folder with Resources/, ProgramFiles/ and Animations/) to OpenInterceptor/game/Game/ in a development checkout. If your copy has the CD audio tracks extracted, put them in game/CD Audio/. The game/ folder is git-ignored.

You rarely need --data: the engine looks, in order, at --data, the OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA variable, settings.yaml paths: {original: …} in the user data folder, <user data folder>/original, and finally game/ in the development checkout (Settings and data discovery). An installed copy keeps the CD (or a copy of it), settings.yaml, bindings.yaml and mods/ in the user data folder (a settings.ini or bindings.ini from an earlier build is read once and replaced by the YAML file).

docs.title: Build the macOS app
docs.text:
python3 tools/build_bundle.py            # dist/OpenInterceptor-0.3.0.app

The app contains the engine and the built-in packs, never game data. The script points settings.yaml at game/ (or --data PATH); --install-data clones the CD into the user data folder instead, as a real install would. Open the app from Finder. See Packaging.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
# The testbed launcher (the original data is found automatically):
target/release/openinterceptor

# Only original-free packs (the default campaign, your own mods):
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original

# Choose the campaign (default: the last one chosen in the launcher, else interceptor
# when the CD is found, else default):
target/release/openinterceptor --campaign default

# ... at a chosen difficulty level:
target/release/openinterceptor --campaign default --difficulty space_ace

# Go straight to one mission (or scenario) with one ship:
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --mission defend_station --ship comet

# Play a mission headless with the AI pilot and print the result:
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --soak defend_station --soak-pilot ai --seconds 400

# Go straight to one scenario with one ship:
target/release/openinterceptor --data game --scenario flight-test --ship lightning

# ... and start in the chase view:
target/release/openinterceptor --data game --scenario flight-test --ship firestar --view chase

# Headless validation of every campaign, pack, model and texture; list what loaded:
target/release/openinterceptor --check
target/release/openinterceptor --list

# Render a scenario's starting screen to a PNG and exit:
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --scenario rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --screenshot shot.png

# Open the model viewer on one model (ship id or original mesh name):
target/release/openinterceptor --model XBASE7

# Convert the original data to OBJ/PNG/WAV for modding (personal use only):
target/release/openinterceptor --extract ~/interceptor-extracted

# The quality gate (tests, build, checks):
scripts/check.sh

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text:
Option Meaning --data <PATH> The Interceptor CD or install folder. Without it: OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA, then settings.yaml, then <user data>/original, then game/ in a checkout. --mods <DIR> Folder of user mods (default: settings.yaml paths: {mods: …}, else mods/ in the user data folder). --packs <DIR> Folder of built-in packs (default: packs/ next to the program, or the source tree). --no-original Ignore the original data even if available. --campaign <ID> Load this campaign (default: the last one chosen in the launcher, else interceptor when the data is available, else default). --difficulty <ID> Play at this difficulty level, a level id of the campaign (default: the last one chosen, else the campaign's default_difficulty). --scenario <ID> Start this scenario, skipping the launcher. --mission <ID> Start this mission, skipping the launcher (Missions). --ship <ID> Player ship for --scenario when the scenario lets you choose. --view <VIEW> Start view: cockpit, forward, left, right, rear-left, rear-right, chase, chase-manual. --model <NAME> Open the model viewer on this model: a ship class id (comet) or an original mesh name (XBASE7). --screenshot <PNG> With --scenario or --model: render the starting screen for --frames frames, save it as a PNG and exit. --frames <N> Frames to run before --screenshot (default 120). --check Validate all content without a window, then exit (status 1 on errors). Every campaign is checked separately, with its own addons; --campaign checks one. --soak <SCENARIO or MISSION> Play a scenario — or a mission, which then prints its result (soak mission <id> (<level>, <pilot>): <result> after <n> s; <k> kills) — without a window for --seconds (default 60) and report what happened to the player's ship (balance testing); the player is --soak-pilot passive (default: flies at the nearest enemy and never shoots) or ai (its class's behaviour). Use with --ship, --campaign, --difficulty. --language <CODE> Text language: the packs' text/<CODE>/ folders (default en, or settings.yaml game.language). --write-schemas <DIR> Write the JSON Schema files of the mod file types (pack.schema.json, rules.schema.json, scenario.schema.json) for editor completion and checking, then exit. --extract <DIR> Convert the original data to OBJ/PNG/WAV at the paths where mod files override it (Overrides and extraction), then exit. --list List campaigns (* = loaded), packs, playable ships and scenarios, then exit. --windowed / --fullscreen Window mode (windowed is the default). --help Usage.

Environment: OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA (default for --data), OI_DEBUG_KEYS=1 (print key names as you press them).

The user data folder (settings.yaml, bindings.yaml, original/, mods/) is ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/ on macOS and $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/ (default ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/) on Linux.

The launcher lists the model viewer, the asset browser and the test scenarios from every loaded pack: Up/Down to choose, Left/Right to pick a ship, Enter to start, Esc to quit. In flight, Esc opens the menu (R restart, L back to the launcher). Default controls follow the original game; see Controls. Flight is newtonian by default: throttle is thrust and the ship coasts; Z reverses thrust, hold B to brake, M holds the target's speed.
